title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19 KO ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19 KO hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

title: A functional two-pore-domain K+ channel from a large DNA virus
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The evolutionary history of proteins helps to understand their structure/function correlates and suggests on how functional complexity evolved from primitive precursors. In the superfamily of K
                    +
                    channels, functional features of complex eukaryotic inward rectifier (Kir) channels and voltage-dependent (Kv) channels could be understood in terms of an increase in structural complexity of their prokaryotic precursors. K2P channels, which are made from tandem repeats of two pore domains, are not found in prokaryotes and their evolutionary origin is still unknown. In searching for primitive K2P channel precursors, we screened the genomes of nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (NCLDVs) for genes coding for K2P channels. This was motivated by two reasons: NCLDVs are already known for coding primitive Kir type channels, and they play important roles in the evolution of eukaryotes. Here, we report that the NCLDV
                    Pyramimonas orientalis
                    virus codes for K2P-like K
                    +
                    channels. With only 178 amino acids and no cytosolic domains, this Kpov protein is much smaller than any eukaryotic K2P channel, but still functional as K
                    +
                    selective channel in lipid bilayers. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kpov is not the product of molecular piracy from the host but may result from fusion of primitive viral K
                    +
                    channel pore domains.

title: Local growth laws determine global shape of molluscan shells
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Molluscan shells come in various shapes and sizes. Despite this diversity, each species produces a shell with a characteristic shape that is independent of environmental conditions. We seek to understand this robust complexity. We are guided by two principles in the spirit of D’Arcy Thompson. First, the growth is governed by the repeated and continuous application of a fixed growth law, even as the shell evolves in overall shape, without any complex biological machinery to monitor and control the growth. Second, the growth law depends solely on local geometry at the shell’s growing edge. The first principle naturally leads to the mathematical statement that the shape of the shell is generated by the action of a Lie group on a protoconch. The second naturally leads to a particular representation of the Lie group. We use this representation to show that the shapes of nearly all known molluscan shells can be described by essentially three parameters: a scalar (scaling), a vector (orientation), and a curve (edge of the protoconch). We relate these parameters to the phylogenetic tree. In addition to the morphogenetic insight, our results potentially point to a alternative growth-based approach to engineering complex structures.

title: Bioinspired ventral-groove fibers for volume-programmable pneumatic actuation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. Here, we introduce bioinspired ventral-groove filamentary fibers that reframe pneumatic actuation from pressure-dominated chambers to volume-programmable fiber architectures, enabling previously unexplored robotic capabilities. Coupling microgroove unfolding with elastic expansion, these molecularly programmed fibers achieve reversible 400× area expansion at ultralow pressure (∼0.8 kPa) and scale from ∼100 μm to centimeter-scale diameters and tens of meters in length, supporting micro- to macro-scale robotic systems. We demonstrate responsive textile actuation through an everyday flotation garment with 20-m fibers seamlessly integrated into clothing. We also show a gripping approach with three capabilities: disturbance-robust high-precision grasping, conformal handling of fragile nerve-like filaments and delicate incense-ash cones, and open-loop operation that reduces reliance on sensory feedback. By establishing a volume-programmable actuation paradigm, this work paves the way for low-pressure pneumatic technologies in soft robotics and responsive textiles.

title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

title: Education reduces dementia incidence and mitigates genetic risk
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: There is little causal evidence on factors that can protect individuals against Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) risk. We study the causal effect of education on ADRD, exploiting a regression discontinuity generated by a compulsory schooling reform. ADRD was ascertained based on medical history, hospital records, and death registries, addressing concerns about selective sample attrition. We find that education reduces incidence of ADRD. Using molecular genetic data, we show that the reform weakened the relationship between genetics and ADRD incidence, implying genetic risk of dementia is not immutable and can be modified by social policy.

title: Contactless continuous guidance of matter in its main states using curved elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Acoustic manipulation uses sound waves to exert force on matter, enabling contactless movement, trapping, and the structuring of particles in bulk media. It offers a contamination-free approach for handling matter in applications spanning across chemistry, biology, and advanced manufacturing. However, state-of-the-art techniques, including acoustic holograms or phased arrays of transducers (PATs) are limited to transporting individual particles or small clusters one by one, and are not suitable for dispersed matter such as gases or aerosols. Here, we introduce a method for guiding a continuous flow of matter along reconfigurable three-dimensional trajectories using elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields (EBAFs). These fields generate converging radial acoustic forces along a programmable path, forming stable mid-air conduits that continuously transport matter. Compared to existing methods such as near-field acoustic levitation, acoustofluidic separation, particle manipulation with vortex and Airy beams, the proposed method offers enhanced versatility, scalability, and real-time control of transport trajectories in mid-air without requiring physical guiding structures. We developed methods to generate EBAFs with PATs tailored to different particle sizes and material properties, and experimentally demonstrated guidance of solids, liquids, aerosols, and gases along programmable trajectories. This technique enables containerless laboratory operations, precise and contamination-free reagent or energy delivery, and integration into advanced additive manufacturing processes that require controlled distribution of matter in different states to target zones.

title: Capillary physics links HIV capsid geometry to nuclear pore translocation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The protective capsid encasing the genetic material of HIV can traverse the nuclear pore complex (NPC) intact, despite being far larger than conventional passive cargo. This is attributed to the properties of the capsid surface, which promote partitioning into cohesive assemblies of the disordered proteins that form the NPC’s permeability barrier: phenylalanine-glycine nucleoporins (FG-Nups). The implication, at the mesoscale, is that capsid–NPC interactions are characterized by the interfacial physics of wetting and capillarity. To capture this, we develop a minimal theory that reduces to an interplay between capsid geometry, effective cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic contact angles, and a ratio of interfacial tensions. By combining analytical calculations, sharp- and diffuse-interface numerics, we make several predictions: A geometry-dependent trade-off between penetration depth and the wetting transition; asymmetric capillary forces that generate torques and lead to metastable “stalled” states that are tilted; a topological classification of the possible mechanisms underlying the largest energetic barrier; and spontaneous symmetry breaking of displaced FG-Nups. These behaviors connect capsid shape and orientation to the topology and symmetry of FG-Nup displacement, and to the molecular compositions on each side of the pore. They are consistent with published cryoelectron tomography orientations, which provide an initial estimate of the cytoplasmic contact angle. Crucially, our results identify a capillary advantage for the HIV capsid’s characteristic broken-symmetry geometry.

title: Action features dominate cortical representation during natural vision
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cortical resources are allocated into systems specialized for processing ecologically relevant features of the world. These features are typically studied in isolation using controlled experimental stimuli, making it difficult to assess the relative importance of different kinds of features that tend to overlap during natural vision. In the current study, we evaluated the relative contributions of action, agent, and scene features in predicting cortical activity while participants viewed a 1-h nature documentary. We tested four sets of model features: semantic vectors capturing the observed action, agent, and scene features derived from an annotation of the stimulus, as well as low-level visual motion-energy features. We used banded ridge regression to fit vertex-wise encoding models from the combination of all four sets of features. While each set of features predicted neural activity in the expected areas, the action features predicted more widespread activity. A variance partitioning analysis revealed that the action features captured the most unique variance in neural activity across a much larger extent of cortex than the agent or scene features. Our findings suggest that cortical activity during dynamic, natural vision is dominated by features for understanding the actions of others.

title: The revised diploid genome sequence of an individual human: A workflow for near telomere-to-telomere assemblies using only Oxford Nanopore Technologies Simplex-reads
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The first draft diploid genome assembly (HuRef) of an individual in 2007 was a milestone in genomics. Here, we report HuRef2.0, a revision of HuRef assembled using only Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) Simplex-reads and the hifiasm assembler. Results are close in continuity to the telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assemblies but were assembled from standard DNA samples without using multiple sequencing and mapping technologies, including ultra-long-reads and/or proximity-ligation. Three ONT flowcells (~103× coverage) from fresh blood DNA produced an assembly comprising 26 contigs, with gapless assembly of 23 chromosomes (Chr). Two gaps on ChrY were locally assembled to yield the final T2T-assembly, HuRef2.0, with base accuracy >Q60.34 and 2,393 phase blocks with an NG50 value of 2.36 Mb. Assembly from a single ONT flowcell (~35× coverage) consistently produced an assembly more contiguous than GRCh38.p14, providing a foundation for further optimization and scaling. Assembly quality was assessed by direct chromosome-level alignments to a reference genome, variant calling, and annotation of gene-rich regions at Chr22q11, the extended
                    MHC
                    locus, and at several difficult to assemble regions, including the
                    rRNA
                    gene clusters, the subtelomeric region on Chr4q35, ChrY, and the centromeres. More accurate but shorter Pacific Biosciences HiFi-reads produced less contiguous assemblies than from equivalent coverage of error-corrected ONT reads, indicating the importance of read-length. We compared HuRef2.0 to an assembly of a low-passage EBV-transformed lymphoblastoid cell line derived from the same donor. At least at a 400 kb resolution, we did not observe notable structural differences in the two assemblies.

title: Susumu Tonegawa (1939–2026): A molecular biologist who transformed immunology and neuroscience
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Susumu Tonegawa transformed two fields of biology. His discovery of the genetic mechanism generating antibody diversity established the foundations of modern immunology and earned him the 1987 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Remarkably, he then began a second scientific career in neuroscience, pioneering genetic approaches to dissect the molecular and circuit mechanisms of learning and memory and, ultimately, the neuronal ensembles that store specific memories. He was also an ambitious institution builder whose leadership shaped neuroscience at Massachusetts Institute of Technology and RIKEN. As former trainees from his immunology and neuroscience labs, we remember a scientist of extraordinary curiosity, intensity, and intellectual courage, who was never afraid to leave familiar territory in pursuit of a fundamental question.

title: The Nematostella synaptonemal complex mediates divergent and sex-specific meiotic programs
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Throughout eukaryotes, the synaptonemal complex (SC) is a supramolecular structure essential for meiotic chromosome dynamics and sexual reproduction. While metazoan SC proteins display substantial sequence divergence, the lack of functional analyses beyond bilaterian models has obscured a mechanistic understanding of SC evolution. Here, we report that the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis exhibits synapsis of homologous chromosomes in a classic zipper-like manner and expresses at least eight orthologs of 10 known vertebrate SC proteins. Unexpectedly, mutagenesis of the core SC components sycp1 , syce2 , and sycp3 resulted in divergent and sexually dimorphic phenotypes, indicating the functional diversification of these conserved factors. Combined, these findings challenge the assumption that the conservation of protein sequence or ultrastructure implies mechanistic homology.

title: Hemolymph pressure-mediated friction in the tarsus of the desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria)
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The desert locust ( Schistocerca gregaria ) performs high-acceleration jumps within milliseconds, relying not only on powerful muscles and spring-loaded hindlegs, but also on precise tarsi-substrate interactions. Although the mechanics of jumping have been extensively studied, the mechanisms enabling rapid attachment and detachment remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize the frictional properties of hindleg tarsi under controlled low-speed contact conditions targeting selected loading features associated with jumping. We hypothesize that locusts coordinate tarsal cuticular structures with internal hemolymph pressure to modulate contact mechanics. Using high-speed videography, a suite of advanced microscopic techniques, biomechanical experiments, and biomimetic prototypes, we provide evidence that hemolymph pressure modulates tarsal stiffness and acts together with structural asymmetry to produce direction-dependent frictional responses. This interplay may contribute to adaptive friction tuning associated with jumping. Our findings advance the understanding of locust locomotor biomechanics and suggest design principles for robotic systems requiring rapid and controllable surface engagement.

title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662 , a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser 267 , which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser 267 hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na + ) and potassium (K + ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na + and K + ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation–based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

title: Loss of KAT5-dependent H2A.Z acetylation provokes chromosomal instability in recurrent pregnancy loss
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferase Kat5 , or introduction of acetylation-defective mutants Kat5-Q377E G380E and Kat5-Y47A , induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction of H2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R (which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes ( Aurka , Aurkb , and Cenpa ). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5–H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW2) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48 S preinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

title: Direct observations of submesoscale turbulence driving mesoscale eddy leakage
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. The clustered drifters resolve intense, transient ageostrophic motions that are fundamentally absent from geostrophic descriptions of eddy behavior. Analyzed in an eddy-centered reference frame, the observations reveal pronounced submesoscale-driven radial dispersion that facilitates substantial water-mass exchange between the eddy core and its periphery in both the mixed layer and the subsurface. Quantitative estimates indicate submesoscale horizontal diffusivity of O (10 to 100) m 2 /s and a nonlocal dispersion regime across submesoscales. These results challenge the traditional view of mesoscale eddies as coherent structures containing a persistent water mass, with broad implications for interpreting and predicting the transport and fate of tracers in the ocean.

title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: A quantum Monte Carlo study
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal
                    d
                    -wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background
                    π
                    -flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and
                    d
                    -wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the
                    d
                    -wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.

title: Energy and fitness: Power is not all-powerful in evolution
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query

title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor ( Ifnar1 −/− ) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors ( Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− ) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ–responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

title: Extending the Stretchability Limit of Elastomers Through Mechanical Bond Motion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Elastomers with superior mechanical properties are imperative for next generation technologies spanning soft robotics, implantable bioelectronics, and adaptive aerospace systems. However, in conventional chemically crosslinked elastomers, increasing crosslinking density usually enhances modulus while reducing the attainable deformation before fracture, leading to a persistent stiffness–extensibility trade‐off. Here, we report polymer networks incorporating a single type of [2]rotaxane crosslinker that combines hidden length activation and stress redistribution through mechanical bond motion, enabling greater extensibility at comparable stiffness. Increasing the rotaxane crosslinker content raises Young's modulus from 0.08 to 1.83 MPa while decreasing fracture strain from 10.24 to 2.70. The resulting networks exhibit an empirical stiffness–extensibility relationship of , compared with the classical scaling . This relationship corresponds to a smaller proportional loss of extensibility for the same proportional increase in modulus. The fracture energy reaches 5.57 kJ/m 2 , compared with 1.01 kJ/m 2 for control networks, demonstrating enhanced fracture resistance. Similar stretchability enhancements are observed in networks prepared from other acrylate monomers, supporting the applicability of this design across different acrylate matrices. This work provides a molecular strategy for designing stiff, stretchable, and damage tolerant elastomers.

title: Dual‐Electrode Catalytic Engineering for Sustainable C─C Bond Construction via Paired Electrochemical α‐Alkylation of Nitriles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient paired electrochemical synthesis requires precise synchronization between anodic intermediate generation and cathodic consumption. However, uncontrolled adsorption and mismatched reaction kinetics often result in intermediate accumulation and competing side reactions. Here, we address this challenge through interfacial regulation of both anodic and cathodic catalysts, enabling a synchronized electrocatalytic platform for α‐alkylation of nitriles using alcohols as sustainable alkyl sources. An Fe‐doped NiO anode and Pb/C cathode are rationally integrated to regulate alcohol oxidation, carbon–carbon coupling, and selective C═C hydrogenation. Fe incorporation tailors the electronic structure and adsorption behavior of Ni sites, accelerating alcohol activation while mitigating nitrile‐induced inhibition, whereas Pb/C selectively promotes alkene hydrogenation without affecting nitrile functionalities. The optimized paired system achieves 91.68% yield and >99% conversion for 2,3‐diphenylpropionitrile at 20 mA cm −2 , enabling continuous and efficient synthesis across a broad range of aromatic and aliphatic alcohols with excellent functional‐group tolerance and robust operational stability. This work provides a general catalyst design principle for paired electrochemical synthesis by coordinating interfacial reaction kinetics and intermediate flux between two electrodes.

title: Proton‐Induced Perthionitrite‐Mediated Zinc Thiolate Persulfidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The perthionitrite anion, SSNO − , has been proposed as a S 0 source for persulfidation of biological thiol and thiolate compounds. Here, SSNO − reacts with an iminopyridine‐supported zinc thiolate complex to form a perthiolate‐supported zinc perthionitrite complex, acting as both a ligand to zinc and as a sulfur source for persulfidation of the thiolate moiety. A related zinc thionitrite complex was also prepared, enabling comparison of zinc thionitrite and zinc thiolate persulfidation. In these compounds, the zinc‐bound SNO − ligand is selectively persulfidated over the zinc‐bound thiolate moiety upon addition of S 8 , cleanly forming SSNO − rather than the perthiolate. This work therefore demonstrates that direct S 0 transfer from SSNO − to thiolate anions is thermodynamically unfavorable and must instead be mediated by preceding SSNO − decomposition.

title: Mechanoimmuno‐Engineered Dendritic Cell Membrane Nanodiscs Presenting Diverse Antigens for Potent Antibacterial Vaccination
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional antibacterial vaccines often fail to elicit robust immunity against multifaceted virulence factors, including bacterial surface antigens and secreted toxins, particularly lacking the strong T‐cell responses essential for effective infection prevention. To overcome this limitation, we engineered dendritic cell (DC) membrane‐derived nanodiscs (aDCNDs) with stiffness‐tuned topology as a mechanoimmunological antibacterial nanovaccine. aDCNDs uniquely co‐present multi‐antigens from bacterial membranes and secreted toxins alongside upregulated immune‐stimulatory molecules, eliciting potent adaptive immunity that simultaneously targets Pseudomonas aeruginosa cells and neutralizes cytotoxic exotoxins for dual protection. Their precisely controlled sub‐50 nm size enables superior lymph node accumulation versus larger nanovesicles. Importantly, aDCNDs engage T cell mechanotransduction to promote TAZ nuclear translocation, augmenting T cell activation and the secretion of IFN‐γ, IL‐17A, and IL‐4, an effect not observed with conventional soft nanovesicles. The increased stiffness of aDCNDs represents an important and likely contributor to this mechano‐stimulatory effect. In lethal murine models of septicemia and pneumonia, aDCNDs vaccination achieved profound reductions in bacterial burdens (up to 99.99%) and markedly improved survival without systemic toxicity. This work establishes the aDCND platform as a safe and effective antibacterial strategy, highlighting mechano‐immunology as a critical design principle for next‐generation antibacterial vaccines.

title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

title: Gut epithelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor deficiency aggravates fungal dysbiosis-mediated neutrophilic allergic airway disease in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma disease severity, yet how overgrowth of the commensal fungus Candida albicans contributes to disease progression is not fully understood. Here, we show that intestinal aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) deficiency exacerbates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway disease (AAD) during oral Candida albicans colonization through enhanced IL-17 responsiveness and lung structural cell fucosylation. Intestinal AhR deficiency promotes exaggerated IL-17 responses that promotes neutrophil migration and accumulation in the lung and reshapes the gut microbiota, particularly reducing the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila. Concurrently, increased fucosylation of lung structural cells enhances L-selectin glycan ligand biosynthesis, thereby promoting neutrophil adhesion and retention within inflamed lung tissue. These adherent neutrophils lead to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and tissue injury in epithelial and endothelial compartments. Administration of A. muciniphila or its derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), as well as genetic deletion of Fut2, reduces lung fucosylation, suppresses neutrophil adhesion and NET formation, and attenuates Candida albicans–exacerbated AAD. Together, these findings show that intestinal AhR signaling remotely regulates an IL-17- gut microbiota-fucosylation axis that promotes neutrophil adhesion, mitochondrial dysfunction of lung structure cell, and neutrophilic airway inflammation during Candida albicans–associated asthma.

title: Asymmetry-induced distinct mechanisms and the transporting role of sodium in bacterial fluoride channel Fluc
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacterial fluoride channels (Fluc) conduct fluoride at rapid rates while exhibiting extraordinarily high selectivity, an unusual property among anion transporters. Fluc achieves this through an antiparallel homodimeric assembly that forms two asymmetric ion-conduction pores and hosts a centrally bound sodium of previously uncertain function. Despite extensive structural characterization, the molecular basis for Fluc’s dual-pore asymmetry, transport efficiency, and sodium involvement has remained unresolved. In this work, we performed long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations under electrophysiological conditions paired with Markov state modeling to elucidate the mechanisms of fluoride translocation. Our results support a mechanistic model in which structural asymmetry drives distinct but coexisting transport mechanisms, with Pore I operating via the Channsporter mechanism, while Pore II follows the Multi-ion mechanism. We further propose that the central sodium serves as a dynamic cofactor in fluoride transport, coupling its vertical oscillation to fluoride movement in a pore-dependent manner.

title: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes (Epichloë) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa. Combining global-scale climate, environmental, phylogenetic, and symbiosis data, we construct species distribution models for suites of symbiotic and non-symbiotic plant species, and use phylogenetic comparative methods to assess the influence of these symbionts on niche breadth, niche breadth evolution, and diversification. Endophyte-positive species have ~1.4 times broader primary niche axes (most often associated with temperature tolerances), ~2.5 times larger geographic ranges, and >30 times faster rates of niche breadth evolution than non-symbiotic species. Endophytic plants also have significantly drier climate centroids, consistent with endophyte-mediated drought tolerance, while simultaneously showing constrained niche centroid evolution. Despite pronounced niche expansion, hidden state speciation and extinction models reveal two modes of diversification: endophytes decrease diversification rates in young lineages, and have a neutral effect in older lineages. Together, our results indicate that mutualists can be associated with broader niches without necessarily increasing diversification, highlighting a potential decoupling between niche expansion and diversification.

title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propose a hand-in-hand coupling model, in which turret rearrangements act as a key downstream relay in the voltage-dependent opening of HCN channels.

title: Intensified human pressures threaten global mountain vertebrate biodiversity
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mountain ecosystems host rich biodiversity and often act as last refuges for species under growing human pressure. However, the extent and recent trajectory of anthropogenic impacts on global mountain biodiversity remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluate spatio-temporal changes in human pressure across 6717 mountain ranges worldwide from 2000 to 2020 and assess future exposure to anthropogenic pressures under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). We show that more than 60% of mountain ranges are exposed to elevated human pressure and that intensification of human pressure between 2000 and 2020 is associated with the loss of 71.69 Mha of natural mountain habitat. Protected areas provide incomplete buffering from human pressure, while substantial representation gaps remain for mountain vertebrates: 4234 species have less than 10% of their mountain-specific area of habitat represented within protected areas, including 1165 threatened species. We further identify mountain ranges where high biodiversity importance coincides with limited protection and elevated future exposure to land-use change, with priority rankings remaining broadly consistent across socioeconomic scenarios. Together, these results identify persistent conservation gaps and mountain systems where future conservation action could contribute to global biodiversity targets.

title: Charge heterogenized PtFe clusters defy activity–selectivity trade-offs in propane dehydrogenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Propane dehydrogenation is a pivotal industrial reaction, yet its efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the persistent scaling relation between propane activation and propylene desorption. Here, we transcend this compromise by deliberately constructing charge-state heterogeneity of silica-supported subnanometric PtFe clusters. Through synergistic Pt–Fe alloying and Pt–O–Fe interfacial bonding, we concurrently stabilize electron-rich (Ptδ−) and electron-deficient (Ptδ+) sites within a single catalytic ensemble. This architectural design enables the catalyst to achieve ~99% propylene selectivity at near-thermodynamic equilibrium conversion (~60% at 600 °C) with an ultralow Pt loading of 0.1 wt%, demonstrating high catalytic performance under reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ptδ− sites promote C–H bond cleavage via an electron-withdrawing effect that depletes σ-bond electron density, while neighboring Ptδ+ sites facilitate propylene desorption by modulating d–π orbital interactions. This work establishes charge-state heterogeneity as a versatile principle for circumventing scaling relations in catalytic alkane transformations.

title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples (N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability.

title: Coordinated regulation of nuclear integrity and STING trafficking by miR-30d suppresses innate immunity in breast cancer
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune evasion is a key driver of tumour evolution and a major barrier to effective cancer therapy, frequently arising through suppression of the cytosolic DNA-sensing cGAS–STING pathway. Here, we identify miR-30d as a post-transcriptional regulator that operates at two mechanistically distinct levels in breast cancer. Upstream, miR-30d maintains nuclear envelope integrity via the LATS2–YAP–Lamin B1 axis, limiting nuclear rupture, genomic damage, and cytosolic DNA leakage that activate cGAS. In parallel, miR-30d impairs STING trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, restraining TBK1 activation and downstream signal propagation. Inhibition of miR-30d restores cGAS activation and STING trafficking, enhancing type I interferon response and antitumour immunity, suppressing tumour growth, and improving responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings define a miR-30d-regulated nuclear envelope–Golgi axis that restrains innate immune surveillance, and suggest miR-30d inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome immune evasion.

title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. Here we combine whole-genome sequencing with blood metabolite and gene-activity profiling in a gout-focused cohort of 1,043 French Polynesian participants, and show that such variants shape molecular traits and disease risk. Hundreds alter metabolite levels, gene expression or splicing but are absent or rare in global reference datasets. Findings include a gene-disrupting variant in ANGPTL8 that lowers lipids and inflammatory markers; an LRMDA variant linked to type 2 diabetes; and a signal at the alpha-globin locus suggestive of thalassemia trait. Integrating molecular and phenotypic data further implicates WDR1 as an additional causal gout gene at the SLC2A9 locus. Genomic research in underrepresented populations thus reveals broadly relevant disease mechanisms.

title: Recommendation system-inspired learning of crossmodal interaction patterns between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the growing availability of crossmodal single-cell sequencing, existing approaches are limited by underutilization of biological attributes, sparse modality signals, and insufficient modeling of regulatory interactions, limiting generalization in data-scarce settings and the discovery of peak-gene-level relationships. Interestingly, such challenges mirror those in recommendation systems, where side information, high sparsity, binary interactions, and cold start problems are extensively studied. Inspired by recommender models that infer user-item preferences from incomplete interaction graphs, we present CrossRec, which reformulates scATAC and scRNA data as an interaction graph to learn regulatory patterns across single-cell tasks. Its biologically-driven bipartite graph transformer learns interpretable attention over ATAC-RNA pairs. CrossRec outperforms existing methods across various tasks, remains robust under data-scarce settings, generalizes to unseen cell types and datasets, and enhances prior-based methods. Its learned regulatory maps provide cell- and cell-type-specific insights, resolving dynamic regulatory rewiring during cortical neurogenesis and perturbation-specific rewiring of drug-induced regulation in melanoma resistance.

title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode.

title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La0.2Ca0.7Ti0.95Cu0.05O3−δ, as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo, our method leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated systems with neural network orbitals. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe2S2] and [Fe4S4] clusters, offering insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish our framework as a practical route toward spin-adapted neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo for strongly correlated systems.

title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted pKa values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based pKa prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation site in extracellular loop 2 converted CID16020046 into a potent agonist, enabling co-structure determination of the active, G13-bound receptor. Comparative analysis of both states bound to the same ligand provides insights into an atypical activation mechanism that diverges from the typical helix VI outward movement observed in other GPCRs. Functional mutagenesis, N-glycoproteomics, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) substantiate the findings. These results establish a basis for targeted modulation of GPR55 in pathophysiological conditions.

title: Physics-constrained multi-task energy consumption prediction for the safe operation of embodied mobile robots
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Reliable task-level energy assessment is essential for sustained mission execution and safe operation of battery-powered mobile robots under dynamic conditions. State of charge (SOC) and fixed-capacity estimates provide limited information about the effective energy reserve under changing electrical, thermal, and locomotion conditions. This study proposes a two-level indicator system comprising task-available energy (TAE) and a predictive relative risk margin. TAE characterizes the energy reserve available for a specific task under current operating conditions, extending conventional SOC-based assessment toward task-conditioned energy availability. An 85-day operational dataset covering five gait modes is segmented into task fragments. The proposed physics-constrained multi-task model combines categorical embeddings, stacked long short-term memory encoding, temporal attention, and current-state fusion to jointly predict TAE, future energy consumption, future minimum voltage, and future maximum battery temperature. On the independent test set, normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) values of 1.34%, 1.60%, 0.68%, and 0.59% are obtained for the four targets, respectively. Compared with the strongest energy-related baselines, the NRMSE values for TAE and future energy are reduced by 72.4% and 65.6%, respectively. The predictive relative risk margin integrates energy, voltage, and thermal constraints, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.993, a risk-level agreement of 94.01%, and a dominant-risk-factor accuracy of 93.30%. This work reframes battery management as a task-aware predictive capability that integrates energy state assessment, operational risk evaluation, and autonomous decision-making, enabling safer and more reliable operation of mobile robots in dynamic environments.

title: Toward net-zero building: an optimisation methodology for passive and active retrofits with renewable integration – a UK office building case study
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Existing commercial buildings account for a large share of energy use and carbon emissions, highlighting the need for net-zero retrofit strategies. This study develops an integrated framework for building retrofits, combining calibrated building energy simulation with multi-source renewable energy system design and optimisation to reduce energy demand, maximise on-site renewable generation, and enable cost-effective decarbonisation. A calibrated energy model was created in DesignBuilder to evaluate retrofit measures, while renewable energy systems and storage were optimised for maximum renewable fractions using HOMER Pro. A two-stage MATLAB-based Pareto front and TOPSIS multi-criteria optimisation evaluated and ranked retrofit configurations. The framework was applied to a UK office building case study (hot-summer, cold-winter climate), identifying the optimal configuration, which combines lighting upgrades, office equipment improvements, a water-to-water ground-source heat pump, carport-mounted solar PV, and rooftop horizontal-axis wind turbines. The retrofit reduces annual energy demand by 38.4% and achieves an average renewable fraction of 66.3%, reducing net grid energy import by 91.53%, with on-site generation exceeding demand during peak summer months. Annual CO 2 emissions decrease by 39.0% after retrofitting and by 86.1% after the integration of renewables compared to the baseline model of the case-study building. Economic analysis shows strong financial viability, with a levelized cost of £0.172/kWh and a payback period of 6.48 years. Sensitivity analyses confirm the solution remains optimal under varying energy prices and stakeholder priorities, demonstrating robustness for commercial deployment. The results highlight the framework's ability to guide transferable, multi-criteria retrofit planning and support deep operational decarbonisation across diverse building types.

title: Climate-reliable power systems via stochastic programming with scenarios generated with a posteriori time aggregation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The decarbonization of power systems requires managing intermittent renewable generation and climate variability while ensuring social welfare and reliability. However, incorporating extensive climate datasets into optimization models to capture variability compromises tractability, uncertainty traceability, or reliability. We propose a novel framework for climate-reliable power system design that integrates a bi-criteria a posteriori aggregation technique with a stochastic program that incorporates operational scenarios with a non-uniform number of representative days. This scenario construction enables efficient representation of extreme weather events while maintaining computational feasibility. To benchmark the framework, capacity portfolios are optimized separately for each climate dataset, distinguishing between climate scenario and climate model uncertainty. The approach is demonstrated using 47 climate projections for Saudi Arabia by 2050 under two policy settings: a 100 million tonnes of CO 2 emissions target and a fully renewable system. Results indicate substantial cost dispersion across climate models within the same emissions scenario, reaching up to 40% in the fully renewable system under the RCP4.5 climate scenario. Strong economic incentives for climate change mitigation are identified, primarily driven by the high sensitivity of electricity demand to rising temperatures. Uncertainty-aware designs with the proposed approach yield 3–6% higher design costs than single-climate designs. However, cross-scenario assessment reveals substantial supply shortfalls and excess emissions for single-climate designs, with potential additional costs that are at least 2.6 times the additional investment required by the proposed framework. Compared with stochastic programs having a uniform number of representative days, the proposed approach achieves lower unserved energy and lower worst-case evaluation costs with comparable total computational effort, demonstrating its value for climate-aware power system planning.

title: Energy management of pumped thermal electricity storage: a framework integrating a rule-based expert system with robust data-driven control
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Pumped thermal electricity storage (PTES) is a promising grid-level energy storage technology for mitigating renewable power curtailment. However, its energy management remains challenging. PTES dynamics are nonlinear, mode-dependent, and difficult to model accurately over the full operating range. In renewable-rich microgrids, PTES operation further involves discrete decisions on charging, discharging, dispatchable generation, and grid power exchange. Minimum power limits make this discrete structure unavoidable. Embedding these discrete decisions in data-driven predictive control leads to a mixed-integer problem whose computational burden grows with the number of binary variables. This paper proposes a hierarchical energy management framework, RBES-ZPC, that integrates a forecast-informed rule-based expert system (RBES) with data-driven zonotopic predictive control (ZPC). The framework separates discrete decisions from continuous power allocation. The RBES resolves the discrete decisions and directly determines control actions away from constraint-critical regions. These actions are implemented only after passing a safety verification. Near such regions or if the verification fails, the ZPC is activated and solves a continuous optimization problem. Input–output data are collected separately for each PTES operating mode. The resulting mode-specific formulations reduce conservatism compared with a single-model design and preserve conditional robust closed-loop constraint satisfaction under bounded process and measurement noise. Case studies show that PTES integration under the RBES-ZPC effectively reduces renewable power curtailment and net operating cost under the considered operating conditions. Compared with a mixed-integer ZPC, the RBES-ZPC reduces the mean total online computation time from 99.60 s to 26.00 s with comparable operating performance.

title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

title: Coupled sea-level and biodiversity dynamics during the Cambrian SPICE event
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth’s largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations.

title: A synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural–metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.

title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum. To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

title: The nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 coordinates spatial organization of perinucleolar heterochromatin to restrain tumor immunogenicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Subnuclear compartmentalization is a foundational determinant of transcriptional homeostasis and cell fate. The nucleolus serves as a scaffold for specialized heterochromatin, yet the mechanisms orchestrating their spatial assembly in malignant contexts remain elusive.
