title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

title: A multi-functionally integrated modular catalyst for efficient chemoselective hydrogenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible groups remains challenging due to the intrinsic activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here we report a multi-functional Pt-based catalyst, modularly integrating molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport and surface reaction like a nanofactory. Structurally, ~3 nm Pt nanoparticles supported on sodium titanate are encapsulated by oxygen vacancies-enriched TiOx overlayers that only permit hydrogen to adsorb on Pt particles for dissociation while preventing substrate contact. The generated active hydrogen species subsequently migrate to the catalyst surface and hydrogenate nitro groups adsorbed on surface Lewis basic oxygen vacancies, enabling an efficient condensation pathway while avoiding the use of corrosive and environmentally unfriendly alkaline solvents. The spatially decoupled yet functionally synergistic catalytic design achieves 90% 3-vinylaniline yield from 3-nitrostyrene under mild conditions with an unprecedented turnover frequency of 83,200 h−1, exceeding all previously reported metal catalysts, and exhibits broad generality toward diverse substituted nitroarenes. Collectively, these findings provide a powerful catalyst design strategy for steering complex reaction networks via spatially modular catalysis.

title: Superior energy-storage performance in BaTiO3-based MLCCs via high-entropy driven multiscale optimization
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors are essential components in modern electronic devices. However, achieving superior performance under high-temperature and high-electric-field remains a huge challenge due to the increased leakage current and limited breakdown strength. Herein, a high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy is proposed for lead-free multilayer ceramic capacitors. This approach integrates multiple elements into both A- and B-sites at the atomic scale, engineers polymorphic domain coexistence at the phase scale, and introduces a uniform SiO2 coating layer on grain surfaces to form a core–shell structure while refining grain size at the grain scale. Furthermore, a SiO2 barrier layer is constructed between the electrodes and ceramics at the device scale. Remarkably, high-entropy BaTiO3-based Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve an ultra-high energy density of 19.8 J·cm−3 and a high efficiency of 89.3% at 1421 kV·cm−1, along with an outstanding high-temperature energy storage performance. The high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy offers a universal approach to enhancing the overall energy storage performance of advanced dielectric capacitors.

title: From microstructure to function: spatial visualization of magnetic permeability
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the physics of high-frequency magnetic response is essential for advancing electromagnetic materials. Here, a general strategy is presented for visualizing magnetic permeability as a spatially distributed, frequency-dependent field, instead of a uniform bulk parameter. Our framework reveals that high-frequency magnetic loss arises from coherent spin-wave propagation and interference, leading to spatially selective energy absorption and localized regions of negative imaginary permeability. Tailoring geometric connectivity to suppress spin-wave propagation enables the selective enhancement of localized resonances. Such resonance enables deterministic control over high-frequency response through structural design. The principle is further examined in nanoscale iron spheres. Their surface morphology plays a decisive role in reorganizing the internal resonance domains. This structural reconfiguration, in turn, reshapes the broadband magnetic permeability spectra. To navigate the high-dimensional space of surface defect configurations, machine learning models are integrated with micromagnetic simulations, allowing rapid prediction of magnetic performance across microwave bands. Computational modeling provides an ideal platform to complement experimental exploration. The physic-data framework reveals geometry-to-spectra design rules, validated on iron nanoparticles. This framework uniquely bridges the microscopic spin dynamics with electromagnetic response, enabling tunable high-frequency materials for communication and sensing.

title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Noninvasive multitarget delivery of size-diverse therapeutics, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), to peri-infarct zones is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneous infarct topographies. Here, we developed a hologram-assisted multitarget BBB opening (HaMBO) platform combining low-cost 3D-printed holograms with a single-element ultrasound transducer. Spatially tailored acoustic fields enabled localized BBB opening along infarct borders. In male mice with transient focal cerebral ischemia, a single two-minute HaMBO treatment safely enhanced the peri-infarct delivery of EVs and MSCs, reduced brain atrophy by ~56%, increased angiogenesis by ~2-fold and neural progenitor proliferation by ~4-fold, and improved long-term behavioral recovery. Spatial transcriptomic analysis associated HaMBO-assisted EV therapy with reduced macrophage infiltration and enhanced pro-angiogenic and neurogenic signaling. Human skull-based simulations further demonstrated HaMBO’s clinical adaptability across diverse stroke scenarios. Thus, HaMBO provides a safe, low-cost, and customizable platform for noninvasive multitarget delivery in ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders.

title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-Q resonances based on bound states in the continuum provide a central route of enhancing light-matter interactions. Here, we present a dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding. By selectively preserving or reducing the O- and S-group symmetries of super lattice, guided modes below light cone can be converted into guided resonances or bound states in the continuum with controlled degeneracy lifting, Q-factor scaling, eigenfield profiles, and mode splitting. Besides, applying rectangular lattice provides an alternative way of tuning the Q-factors and mode splitting. Finally, we experimentally demonstrate such two types of high-Q resonances in the tetramer metasurfaces. Measurement results show that the mode splitting can be tuned from 0 nm to 70 nm while the Q-factors are modulated from 300 to 20,000 by varying the asymmetry parameters. This work establishes a symmetry-addressed route for programmable multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces.

title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor’s spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4’s groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

title: Arabian hydroclimate and hominin population dynamics over the last 500,000 years
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the discovery of a rich Palaeolithic archaeological record in Arabia over the last decade, the environmental context of hominin occupations and dispersals remains poorly understood owing to the paucity of Pleistocene palaeoenvironmental records. Here we show a multi-proxy, high-resolution dust record from the western equatorial Indian Ocean spanning the last 500,000 years, which enables evaluation of the influence of orbital-scale hydrological variations on hominin populations in Arabia. The dust evidence reinforces the view that hominin presence in Arabia was driven by enhanced monsoon precipitation during so-called Green Arabia periods. These results, coupled with hunter-gatherer demographic data, point to marked hominin population expansions during prolonged wetter periods. Hominin occupation, however, was not linked exclusively to traditional humid periods. Brief phases of high-intensity rainfall within some glacial periods, manifested by transient high dust contents associated with enhanced terrestrial moisture availability and increased supply of wind-erodible particles, also favoured hominin expansions.

title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance.

title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning.

title: Making 1000 Wh/kg LiNiO2 Cathode Nearly Strain-Free by Complex-Concentrated Doping
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.

title: rGO-MXene 2D Interfacial Engineering for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this work, we report an innovative interface engineering strategy combining bidirectional chemical anchoring and electronic bridging via a 2D reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and MXene conductive network. This hierarchical 2D structure suppresses the aggregation and stacking of single-layer MXene nanosheets while mutually compensating for individual charge transport limitations. Specifically, the abundant functional groups passivate interfacial defects (Pb2+ and I–) and bond with the PCBM layer via coordination, hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. This synergistic architecture lowers the electron energy offset. Consequently, PSCs incorporating the rGO-MXene interlayer achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.96% (certified 25.05%) and retain 96.43% of initial efficiency after 1000 h in ambient air. Furthermore, 10 × 10 cm2 large-area PSM yields a high PCE of 20.25%, maintaining 96.05% of initial efficiency under maximum power point tracking for 963 h.

title: Alicyclic Lewis Bases Enable 100 °C-Processed α-FAPbI3 Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Formamidinium lead iodide (α-FAPbI3) perovskite, despite its ideal bandgap, requires high-temperature (≥150 °C) annealing for the δ-to-α phase transformation, hindering its application in low-temperature processed inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), particularly on flexible substrates. Herein, we demonstrate that the alicyclic Lewis base caprolactam (CPL) effectively drives the complete δ-to-α phase transformation of FAPbI3 at a reduced temperature of 100 °C. Experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that CPL lowers the phase transition energy barrier and retards crystallization kinetics via strong Pb2+ coordination and controlled desorption. This strategy yields highly crystalline, fully phase-converted α-FAPbI3 films with improved morphology, reduced defect densities, and enhanced optoelectronic properties. Consequently, CPL-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.64% with good operational stability. The low-temperature processability also enables high-performance flexible PSCs with a PCE of 23.73%. This work presents an additive engineering approach for realizing efficient and stable α-FAPbI3 PSCs through low-temperature manufacturing.

title: Bridging Spectroscopy and Reactivity: Identifying the True Reactive CO Species in Electrocatalytic CO Oxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In situ electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy has revolutionized our understanding of electrocatalysis. However, establishing a rigorous correlation between spectroscopic signatures and reaction kinetics is still very challenging because high-coverage surface species may dominate the signal, whereas the truly reactive participants may be short-lived or spectroscopically silent. To disentangle spectators from true reaction participants, we developed a high-sensitivity spectroelectrochemical platform that integrates the rotating disk electrode with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (RDE-SERS). This approach enables the simultaneous acquisition of reaction kinetics and interfacial molecular information under well-defined mass transport conditions. Using this versatile approach, we investigated the benchmark carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) on the Pt surface, which enabled decoupling between the spectroscopically observable species and the catalytically active species. Despite persistent and intense Raman signatures of adsorbed CO (COad) in the diffusion-limited region, COad predominantly acts as a spectator that blocks surface sites without effectively participating in the reaction, as confirmed by the isotope substitution experiments. Conversely, the oxidation current is sustained by the continuous flux of solution-phase CO (COsol), which is identified as the kinetically relevant reactant. These findings offer a new perspective on the roles of adsorbed species versus solution-phase species during dynamic electrochemical reactions. Collectively, the RDE-SERS methodology is established as a reliable strategy for identifying true reaction pathways, bridging molecular-level spectroscopic identification with macroscopic reactivity in complex electrocatalytic systems.

title: Dual Functions of Halogen-Bonding Molecules for Stabilizing Ultra-wide Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) metal halide perovskite solar cells are essential for multi-junction solar cells with higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) potentials. In this work, we report the dual functions of 5-iodoisophthalic acid (I-BDC) to suppress phase segregation and uncoordinated Pb2+ related defects to enhance UWBG perovskite cell performance and stability. An I-BDC incorporated 1.95 eV perovskite film exhibited stable photoluminescence after 120 min of illumination. The best I-BDC cell achieved a certified reverse scan PCE of 16.5%, the highest for 1.95 eV perovskite cells to date. These UWBG perovskite solar cells are the most stable reported to date, with one encapsulated device retaining 90% of its initial PCE after 500 h of maximum power point tracking at ∼40 °C and another retaining 95% of its initial PCE after 206 thermal cycles (–40 ↔ 85 °C), passing the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61215 testing protocols at the cell level.

title: Trash to Treasure: PFAS‐Functionalized MOFs for Boosted Piezocatalytic H 2 Production
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) hold broad prospects in piezocatalysis because of their high surface area, porosity, and tunable structures, yet pristine MOFs frequently suffer from poor piezocatalytic response. Herein, this study pioneers a novel strategy using pollutant perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) as a functional additive to post‐synthetically modify MOF‐808(Hf), fabricating MOF‐808(Hf)‐F for piezocatalytic hydrogen production. PFHxA modification remarkably enhances the polarity of MOF‐808(Hf) (dipole moment from 8.90 to 12.58 D) and piezoelectricity (d 33 from 63.70 to 234.30 pm V −1 ), boosting electron‐hole separation verified by electrochemical and in situ photoluminescence characterizations. Consequently, MOF‐808(Hf)‐F achieves an excellent piezocatalytic H 2 evolution rate of 2811.4 µmol g −1 h −1 , 10.5‐fold higher than the pristine counterpart and superior to that of numerous reported MOF‐based piezocatalysts. In addition, MOF‐808(Hf) achieves a PFHxA removal efficiency of approximately 40.1% from water. This work realizes simultaneous per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal and efficient energy production, with excellent universality for Hf‐based MOFs with unsaturated metal sites.

title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next‐generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass‐derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α‐helical protein (α‐HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α ‐helical structure of α‐HP in the α‐HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N‐ and O‐containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium‐sulfur batteries employing the α‐HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long‐term cycling stability. The α‐HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g −1 and retains 487.9 mAh g −1 after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium‐sulfur battery applications.

title: 16.52% Efficiency All‐Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells via Al‐Doped ZnO/SnO 2 Electron Transport Bilayer for Improved Interfacial Energy‐Level Alignment
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial energy‐level misalignment in all‐inorganic perovskite solar cells generally causes inefficient charge extraction. Here, we propose an Al‐doped ZnO (AZO)/SnO 2 electron transport bilayer to improve energy‐level alignment in CsPbI 2 Br‐based PSCs. By this approach, we achieved a champion efficiency of 16.52%, which is the highest reported value for all‐inorganic CsPbI 2 Br PSCs without doping or passivation of the perovskite, along with a high V OC of 1.33 V. AZO‐based devices substantially outperform ZnO‐based controls, delivering a PCE of 16.52% versus 15.21%, with suppressed dark current, reduced trap density, lower non‐radiative recombination, and smaller hysteresis. The AZO device retains 80% of its initial efficiency after 662 h of continuous illumination, compared with only 312 h for the ZnO counterpart. Al 3+ substitution for Zn 2+ elevates the ZnO conduction band minimum, establishing a favorable cascade alignment among SnO 2 /AZO/perovskite that lowers the electron extraction barrier and blocks hole backflow. Al doping also suppresses oxygen vacancies, reducing interfacial trap‐state density and enhancing perovskite crystallinity. Efficient charge extraction further suppresses Ag electrode degradation and corrosion, contributing to long‐term stability. This work establishes a rational interfacial engineering approach using an AZO/SnO 2 bilayer for efficient and stable all‐inorganic perovskite solar cells.

title: Anti‐Poisoning Tin Single‐Atom Unlocks High‐Activity Ruthenium Catalysts for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) is constrained by the lack of efficient electrocatalysts for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), primarily due tothe sluggishVolmer step and inefficient intermediate desorption. While Ru‐based catalysts exhibit promising *H binding energy, their practical performance is compromised by poor water dissociation kinetics and susceptibility to active‐site blockage by adsorbed species. Herein, we report a Sn‐doped RuO 2 @Ru catalyst supported on carbon black, wherein atomically dispersed Sn modulates the electronic structure of RuO 2 via Sn─O bonds, simultaneously facilitating water dissociation, optimizing *H adsorption, and preventing *OH poisoning. The catalyst achieves exceptional performance with an overpotential of 9 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , positioning it among the most active HER catalysts reported to date. When integrated into a full AEMWE, it operates at 1.85 V and 1000 mA cm −2 with stability exceeding 300 h. Mechanistic studies suggest that Sn doping fine‐tunes the *OH and *H binding energies, addressing the kinetic imbalance inherent in conventional Ru catalysts. This work highlights the effectiveness of atomic‐level electronic engineering via an anti‐poisoning strategy for designing efficient, stable alkaline HER electrocatalysts toward industrial hydrogen production.

title: Engineering Thermoelectric‐Electrocatalytic Coupling in RuO 2 /PrCoO 3 Heterointerface for Efficient Oxygen Evolution
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is pivotal for diverse electrochemical energy conversion systems; however, it has so far been plagued by sluggish kinetics and excessive energy consumption. In this study, we proposed an innovative thermoelectric‐electrocatalytic coupling strategy to enhance OER efficiency by constructing an Ohmic heterointerface through uniform integration of RuO 2 with thermoelectric oxide (PrCoO 3 ). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the thermoelectric potential generated by PrCoO 3 selectively activates the intrinsically inert (101) facet of RuO 2 by lowering *OOH formation barrier, thereby substantially boosting the overall OER performance. Consequently, the RuO 2 /PrCoO 3 heterointerface delivered exceptional OER performance under a mild temperature gradient (Δ T ) of 175°C, achieving dramatic reduction in overpotential at 10 mA cm −2 from 300 mV (Δ T = 0°C) to 178 mV, 4 300% increase in current density, and negligible potential loss over 1,000 h. When the catalyst was assembled into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the cell driven by spontaneous heating reached a low voltage of 2.18 V at a current density of 2.0 A cm −2 , with stable operation for 600 h. These insights into harnessing thermal gradient via integrated electrocatalytic system are crucial for the recovery of industrial waste heat and its conversion into high‐value chemicals.

title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm −1 )
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries (ASSBs) offer a promising route to surpass the energy‐density limits of conventional lithium‐ion technology. However, their commercialization is hindered by interfacial instability, chemo‐mechanical degradation, and the limited ionic conductivity of current solid electrolytes, driving the search for new fast‐ion conductors, particularly among lithium oxyhalides. Here, we report a new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 , synthesized via a simple low‐temperature route. The material crystallizes in a triclinic structure composed of isolated [Ta 2 OCl 10 ] 2− dimers and exhibits a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 0.002 mS.cm − 1 . Ball milling dramatically enhances Li + transport, increasing the conductivity by a factor of 5000 to 11 mS.cm −1 while reducing the activation energy from 0.46 to 0.27 eV. Combined structural, spectroscopic, and computational analyses reveal that this enhancement originates from the formation of a highly disordered, liquid‐like Li + sublattice. Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 further demonstrates a stability window of 1.89–3.70 V vs. Li x In and enables ASSBs with low polarization and excellent capacity retention (700 cycles at 1C with decay less than 20%). These results establish Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 as a promising superionic conductor and highlight the Li–M–O–Cl family as a fertile design space for next‐generation solid electrolytes.

title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

title: Lewis‐Basic Metal Sulfide Electrode Interfaces Unlock High Power Density Alkaline All‐Iron Redox Flow Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkaline all‐iron redox flow batteries (AIRFBs) are promising for safe, low‐cost grid‐scale energy storage using Earth‐abundant elements. However, insufficient energy efficiency and power density limit practical deployment, while the interfacial kinetic origin of these losses remains unclear. Here, we identify sluggish outer‐sphere electron‐transfer kinetics of Fe‐chelate anolytes as a key kinetic bottleneck governing polarization in alkaline AIRFBs and further link this bottleneck to limited outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)‐region accessibility and weak interfacial electronic coupling. To overcome this limitation, we develop Lewis‐basic sulfide interfaces that regulate the local Fe‐chelate/electrode environment. These regulated interfaces convert inefficient diffusion encounters into productive sulfide‐assisted outer‐sphere electron‐transfer events, thereby accelerating anolyte redox kinetics and suppressing polarization. An alkaline AIRFB assembled with a Ni 3 S 4 ‐modified electrode delivers an energy efficiency of 80.65% at 200 mA cm −2 and a peak power density of 501.2 mW cm −2 , compared with 65.69% and 185.5 mW cm −2 for the pristine cell. The Ni 3 S 4 ‐based cell further maintains an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, an average energy efficiency of 77.8%, and stable operation over 3000 cycles at 200 mA cm −2 . This work reveals an interfacial kinetic bottleneck in alkaline AIRFBs and establishes Lewis‐basic interface engineering as a strategy for high‐power and low‐cost long‐duration energy storage.

title: Stabilizing Ru Sites via Lattice Oxygen Locking of Nb‐Ru/RuO 2 to Break the Activity–Stability Trade‐Off for Acidic Oxygen Evolution
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly active and stable Ru‐based catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to accelerate the industrialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). However, Ru‐based catalysts inevitably follow the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) during the actual reaction, which in turn triggers severe Ru dissolution. While shifting the reaction pathway to the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) improves stability, it often compromises catalytic activity. Herein, we design an Nb‐doped Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure catalyst to inhibit the unstable LOM, and concurrently propose a favorable Brønsted Site‐Promoted Proton Transfer (BSPT) mechanism derived from the AEM. Specifically, the synergy between Nb doping and Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure enhances activity by improving deprotonation capability and optimizing oxygen‐intermediate adsorption, while simultaneously improving durability by stabilizing lattice oxygen and suppressing excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ru. Consequently, the Nb‐Ru/RuO 2 delivers an overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm −2 with impressive durability over 3000 h. In a working PEMWE, it exhibits remarkable durability for 3000, 1200, and 900 h at 500, 1000, and 2000 mA cm −2 . This study offers novel design principles and theoretical foundations to advance efficient, low‐cost PEMWE hydrogen production.

title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal‐Organic Network for CO 2 Conversion
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous‐phase synthesis of a woven metal‐organic superstructure assembled from Cu 2+ and 2,4,6‐trinitrobenzene‐1,3,5‐triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu 2+ yields charged one‐dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two‐dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu 2+ cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π‐conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox‐active Cu 2+ centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu‐TNPG network was evaluated for visible‐light‐driven CO 2 reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu‐TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre‐activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H 2 , highlighting its structural and functional versatility.

title: Natural Versus Artificial Photosynthesis: Pushing Beyond Nature's Limits to Deliver Low‐Cost Solar Fuels
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural photosynthesis (NP) sustains life by coordinating light harvesting, charge separation, multielectron catalysis, carbon fixation, regulation, and repair. Artificial photosynthesis instead aims to convert solar energy selectively into fuels and chemicals through designed light absorbers, interfaces, and catalytic sites. This review compares the two systems across light harvesting, charge separation and transfer, catalytic conversion, photoprotection, and system integration, emphasizing that meaningful comparisons require similar functions, comparable metrics, and clearly defined system boundaries. Field‐scale NP typically operates at sub‐percent solar‐to‐biomass efficiencies, whereas selected artificial photosynthetic devices have achieved double‐digit solar‐to‐fuel efficiencies under defined conditions. These values should not be directly ranked because the products and system functions differ. We identify the respective strengths of artificial systems in spectral, interfacial, catalytic, and product control, and of natural systems in regulation, repair, regeneration, and multiscale coordination, providing design principles for efficient, durable, and scalable solar‐to‐chemical conversion.

title: Ultrastable 4.99 V Li rich Mn-based cathodes achieved by catalytic-shielded and strain-buffered interface engineering
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxides (LROs) offer high theoretical capacity but are limited by irreversible oxygen redox, voltage fade, and structural degradation upon cycling. Herein, we develop a dual-interface engineering strategy for LRO cathodes, integrating a catalytic-shielded carbon coating and interface-confined discrete spinel domains. The carbon layer decouples electrolyte decomposition from lattice-driven catalysis, suppressing cathode-electrolyte interphase growth and oxygen release, while subsurface-confined spinel phases establish three-dimensional Li+ transport pathways and mitigate lattice strain. title: 3D Ordered Macroporous Cu‐Based Multimetallic Alloy Enables Efficient Asymmetric C–C Coupling for Selective CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The abundant Cu 0 /Cu δ+ interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C–C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuO x . The designed catalyst exhibits superior Faradic efficiency of 64.1% for electrochemical CO 2 reduction to ethylene at −1.55 V versus RHE under acidic conditions, and stability for over 60 h at 600 mA cm −2 in a flow cell. In‐situ experiments and theoretical simulations reveal that the 3DOM structure enhances the surface electric field, raises the local pH, and accelerates interfacial mass transport. The electronic structure of Cu δ+ (0δ+ sites could govern *CO adsorption and hydrogenation pathways, thereby enhancing ethylene selectivity.

title: Adaptive Supramolecular Interactions Govern Redox‐Active Molecules in Aqueous Redox Flow Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Weak noncovalent interactions critically govern molecular behavior in solution, yet how they shape redox processes in aqueous electrochemical environments remains underexplored. Here, we demonstrate control over the solubility and redox stability of aromatic redox‐active molecules in aqueous redox flow batteries (RFBs). Zwitterionic substitution of naphthalene diimide (NDI) bearing quaternary ammonium and sulfonate groups shows weak π–π cohesion through steric and electrostatic effects, rendering otherwise insoluble NDIs responsive to external anions. Hydrophobic and weakly hydrated anions such as iodide and bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide disrupt residual stacking through anion–π interactions, enabling dissolution to concentrations approaching 1.3 M. Upon electrochemical reduction, these anions dissociate, and the reduced NDI species are instead stabilized through spin pairing and cation‐mediated intermolecular interactions, which suppress irreversible aggregation, slow self‐discharge, and enable rapid redox reactions. Operando Raman spectroscopy, 1 H NMR, and EPR elucidate the redox‐state‐dependent evolution of these supramolecular assemblies. Together, these results establish zwitterionic molecular design for adaptive supramolecular redox chemistry in aqueous RFBs.

title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard‐Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion–Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard‐carbon anode design lacks a precursor‐level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed‐pore formation. Here we establish a precursor‐level cohesion‐solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene‐fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke‐like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard‐carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect‐engineered carbon galleries. The solvent‐selected AHC‐80‐1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g −1 at 0.05 A g −1 with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide‐temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at −20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10‐kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC‐80‐1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg −1 and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle‐to‐gate life‐cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC‐80‐1400 production reduces climate‐change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor‐stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.

title: Time‐Encoded Ligand Presentation via a Magnetically Actuated Hydrogel Mitigates T Cell Exhaustion
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Adoptive T cell therapy (ACT) requires ex vivo expansion of tumor‐reactive CD8 + T cells, yet prolonged antigenic stimulation frequently induces exhaustion, limiting persistence and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we present a magnetically actuated, extracellular matrix–mimetic hydrogel that enables reversible control of T cell receptor (TCR) stimulation timing. By embedding αCD3ε/αCD28‐functionalized magnetic nanoparticles within a soft hyaluronic acid matrix, external magnetic fields dynamically expose or conceal stimulatory ligands, allowing programmable alternation between activation and rest. Continuous ligand presentation sustains TCR signaling and drives inhibitory receptor expression and functional exhaustion. In contrast, alternating activation–rest cycles periodically attenuate proximal TCR signaling, reduce exhaustion‐associated marker expression, and bias differentiation toward central memory‐like states while preserving cytokine production and recall capacity. T cells expanded under intermittent stimulation exhibit enhanced antigen‐specific cytotoxicity, reduced dependence on PD‐1 blockade, and superior tumor control in vivo, together with increased CD8 + T cell abundance across analyzed tissues. These results identify temporal control of mechanochemical signaling as a materials‐encoded regulator of T cell fate and provide a non‐genetic strategy for generating functionally competent T cell products with reduced exhaustion‐associated dysfunction and improved antitumor activity.

title: Dicationic Porous Poly(Ionic Liquid)s with Hydrogen Bond Donors for Efficient Catalytic Conversion of CO2 under Mild Conditions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The formation of cyclic carbonates by coupling CO2 with epoxides offers a practical way of upgrading the surplus CO2 that has accumulated in the atmosphere, and thus helps to mitigate global warming. Because CO2 is intrinsically robust thermodynamically and sluggish kinetically, however, this transformation usually demands harsh conditions. Herein, a family of porous poly(ionic liquid)s denoted bAm-PIL-x (bAm = bis-amide) was constructed by radical copolymerization of an imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer (tVIm-IL) and a quaternary ammonium-based ionic liquid monomer (tQAm-IL) in the presence of N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide as the cross-linker. These polymers combine a moderate specific surface area, pores spanning several size regimes, and a pronounced affinity for CO2, which makes them well suited to both capturing and converting CO2. Applied to the coupling of CO2 with epoxides under solvent-free, metal-free, and cocatalyst-free conditions, bAm-PIL-2 delivered excellent performance at a mild 80 °C and 1.0 bar. The catalyst was readily regenerated and recycled, and it accepted a wide range of epoxide substrates. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations together with in situ infrared spectroscopy were used to probe how the catalyst, the epoxides, and CO2 interact, and on this basis a plausible reaction mechanism for the cycloaddition is proposed. The present findings offer meaningful guidance for designing highly efficient catalysts for CO2 conversion.

title: Programmable Engineered Living Vehicles as Autonomous Biofactories for Synergistic Osteomyelitis Management and Bone Regeneration
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional static biomaterials and synthetic nanomedicines struggle to penetrate recalcitrant biofilms and orchestrate tissue regeneration in deep‐seated infections due to limited autonomous navigation and a lack of spatiotemporal responsiveness. Here, we conceptualize and develop a programmable engineered living vehicle (ELV) that functions as an autonomous biofactory for the synergistic management of drug‐resistant osteomyelitis. Built upon a self‐propelled Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 chassis with innate ecological dominance, these living biofactories are hierarchically equipped with environmental biosensors and logic‐gated computing modules. Crucially, leveraging AlphaFold 3‐guided molecular docking, we engineered multiscale thermo‐responsive genetic logic circuits that enable precise, temperature‐dependent biomanufacturing of bacteriolytic lysostaphin (LYS) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) (≥37°C), coupled with a fail‐safe thermal self‐destruct mechanism (≥42°C). Furthermore, surface‐engineered (DSS) 6 peptides confer robust hydroxyapatite affinity, acting as a bone‐homing navigation module. In a rat osteomyelitis model induced by methicillin‐resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), intravenously deployed ELV biofactories autonomously navigate to the infected niche, actively penetrate biofilms, and outperform vancomycin in pathogen clearance. Concurrently, localized payload secretion reprograms the osteo‐immune microenvironment, significantly accelerating bone repair. This work establishes a versatile paradigm for next‐generation smart living therapeutics, bridging synthetic biology with micro‐engineering to address complex clinical challenges.

title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large‐Area Tin‐based Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin‐based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p‐type small molecule, 4,4'‐(5,6‐bis(2‐methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole‐4,7‐diyl)bis(2,5‐difluoro‐N,N‐bis(4‐methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic‐angle spinning 1 H NMR, 1 H‐ 1 H double‐quantum‐single‐quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning‐rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high‐quality Sn‐based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap‐assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG‐PEDOT:PSS‐based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1‐cm 2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04‐cm 2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N 2 atmosphere.

title: Regioisomerism‐Guided Molecular Passivation for 26.05%‐Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Defect‐mediated nonradiative recombination remains a major barrier to efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Although considerable advances have been made with molecular additives, how the spatial arrangement of functional groups affects device performance remains largely unexplored. Here, we present a regioisomerism‐guided molecular design strategy using fluorinated aniline as a well‐defined model system to incorporate into the lead iodide (PbI 2 ) precursor solution during two‐step sequential perovskite deposition. By systematically comparing ortho‐, meta‐, and para‐fluoroaniline, we demonstrate that the ortho isomer, 2‐fluoroaniline (2‐FA), affords the most effective regulation of defect states and device performance. This superiority arises from the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen bond, which redistributes the molecular electrostatic potential and confers stable bidentate coordination with the perovskite lattice. Additionally, 2‐FA facilitates high‐quality α‐FAPbI 3 films and aligns the energy level favorably with the hole transport layer, yielding a champion efficiency of 26.05% for the n‐i‐p PSCs. Moreover, the 2‐FA‐containing device exhibits superior operational stability. This regioisomerism‐guided design works universally across n‐i‐p and p‐i‐n architectures, irrespective of one‐step or two‐step fabrication. Our work establishes regioisomerism as a simple yet powerful molecular design principle for molecular engineering and provides new insight into the rational development of efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Resolving the Structural Origin of Lattice Oxygen Release across Scales in Practical Lithium‐Manganese‐Rich Electrodes
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Gas evolution from lattice oxygen release is a major obstacle to deployment of high‐energy‐density cathodes, yet its structural origin within dense electrodes remains challenging to resolve across multiple length scales. This difficulty arises because gas evolution is the collective outcome of oxygen release from numerous grains and particles, whose environments can vary across electrode, secondary‐particle, and grain scales. Here, by integrating online electrochemical mass spectrometry with synchrotron X‐ray and electron microscopy, this study resolves the spatial origin of O 2 evolution through mapping Mn reduction, a chemical fingerprint of oxygen release, across four orders of magnitude in length scale. Two lithium‐manganese‐rich layered oxide (LMR) electrodes that vary only in secondary‐particle size are employed as a model system, and their O 2 evolution differs twofold. Spatially resolving Mn oxidation state distribution reveals no detectable Mn‐reduction gradient across the electrode thickness or within particles, indicating that the difference does not originate from electrode‐ or particle‐scale heterogeneity. Instead, frontal facets (lithium‐intercalation planes) of grains exhibit deeper Mn reduction and surface reconstruction than lateral facets, consistent with favorable oxygen vacancy formation and migration. O 2 evolution matches after frontal‐facet area normalization, identifying frontal‐facet exposure as a key structural descriptor for O 2 evolution in these practical LMR electrodes.

title: Biomimetic Liquid Diodes Across Materials and Scales for Directional Liquid Transfer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The last decade has witnessed remarkable advancements in liquid diode, evolving from fundamental research to cutting-edge applications such as microfluidics, thermal management, and wearable electronics. However, how material characteristics and structural scales mediate liquid transport on liquid diodes has yet to be fully clarified to date. In this study, we develop a Crassula muscosa inspired liquid diode (CMLD) with superior material adaptability and structural scale adaptability spanning three orders of magnitude. Such a liquid diode endows a cross-material, and cross-scale unidirectional liquid transfer from microscale to macroscale. The mechanisms underlying the role of the wettability, viscosity and structure scale in regulating the liquid transfer kinetics including transfer distance, transfer velocity and liquid rectification, are clearly demonstrated. By combining experimental observation, numerical simulation, and building a theoretical retention force model, the liquid transfer and pinning mechanisms governed by asymmetric reentrant structures are systematically elucidated, which enables superior robustness for unidirectional liquid transfer of continuous flows with various flow rates. These results provide a robust framework for coupling material characteristics and structural scales to achieve controllable unidirectional liquid transfer, laying a solid foundation for the practical implementation of liquid diode-based technologies.

title: Promoting Glycine Electrosynthesis from Nitrate and Oxalic Acid over Co–Cu Dual-Site Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical coreduction of nitrate (NO3–) and oxalic acid to glycine (ENOG) provides a sustainable alternative to conventional glycine production but remains limited by sluggish reactant activation, inefficient C–N coupling, and competing reaction pathways. Herein, a dual-site metal–organic framework, CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu, is developed as an efficient and robust cathode catalyst for ENOG. Operando spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal the cooperative effect of Cu–Co dual sites in promoting OA-to-*C2H2O3 conversion, *NO3 reduction to *NH2OH, *C2H2O3-*NH2OH coupling to *C2H3NO3, and subsequent *C2H3NO3 hydrogenation for selective glycine formation. Moreover, by integrating cathodic ENOG over the CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu catalyst with an anodic glycerol oxidation over the PbO2 catalyst in a two-electrode electrolyzer, we achieve a glycine Faradaic efficiency of 78.3% and a glycine yield rate of 629.3 mmol h−1 g−1, while enabling the gram-scale production of high-purity glycine.

title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024–2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe’s annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering.

title: Regulating the Activity and Product Selectivity of Electrocatalytic Glycerol Oxidation by Changing the Au Loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) has attracted much attention recently in the production of high-value-added chemicals coupled with water electrolysis for energy-saving hydrogen production due to its mild reaction conditions, green and harmless, and lower onset potential than the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis. However, under alkaline conditions, glycerol is prone to generate low-value-added C1 products, and the selectivity for C3 products is a significant challenge. In this work, we successfully regulated the activity and product selectivity of electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation by changing the Au loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF. The results showed that the selectivity of Au/Ni2.86Te2/NF-3 for glyceric acid (GLA) was 72.41%, and its GOR performance and selectivity were superior to those of recently reported catalysts. An appropriate Au loading results in favorable changes in Au distribution and surface electronic structure, which are associated with improved GOR activity and GLA selectivity.

title: Constructing Continuous Proton Channels through One-Dimensional Confined Nanofillers for High-Performance H2/O2 Fuel Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Establishing continuous proton transport pathways alongside robust interfacial interactions remains a critical bottleneck for organic–inorganic composite proton exchange membranes (PEMs). Herein, we report a rationally designed hybrid nanofiller (SUC@PHNTs) that integrates the long-range orientational order of one-dimensional (1D) halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) with the high-density proton-hopping sites of the metal-organic framework UiO-66-(COOH)2 (UC) and zwitterionic surface grafts. Subsequently when dispersed in a sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) matrix, this 1D confined architecture bridges discrete UC domains into interconnected, continuous proton-conducting channels, effectively reducing proton transport tortuosity. Specifically, the S/SUC@PHNTs-3.0% membrane delivered 174.72 mS cm–1 (80 °C, 100% RH), corresponding to a 35.21% increase relative to pristine SPEEK. In an H2/O2 single-cell test, the membrane delivered a maximum power density of 793.29 mW cm–2, substantially exceeding that of SPEEK. Moreover, the voltage decay rate over 150 h of continuous operation was merely 0.42 mV h–1, indicative of excellent long-term operational stability. Overall, these results establish that the 1D confined nanofiller design strategy provides a promising technological pathway toward high-performance PEMs.

title: 3D Printed Sandpile-Shaped Photothermal Evaporator Based on Thiol-Ene Click Chemistry for Efficient Water Evaporation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The interface evaporation technology driven by solar energy has received widespread attention due to its advantages of being clean, pollution-free, and low in energy consumption. However, the cumbersome preparation process of existing high-efficiency evaporators hinders their large-scale promotion and application. Furthermore, we find that the inclined slope of the sandpile has the geometric condition of “forced reflection,” and the incident light can form reciprocating reflection between adjacent sandpiles, greatly improving the light capture efficiency and providing a structural basis for achieving efficient evaporation. Inspired by this, we construct a sandpile-shaped photothermal evaporator with different array densities by digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technology with thiol-ene click chemistry reactions, using pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate) (PETMP) and poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) as photothermal materials to achieve integrated molding of the evaporator. Through structural optimization, the 3 × 3 array structure exhibits the best evaporation performance, with an evaporation rate of 1.91 kg m–2 h–1 and an evaporation efficiency of 90.9% at one solar intensity. When used for photocatalytic degradation of dye wastewater, the degradation efficiency of dyes can reach 86%. In addition, using a 3 × 3 array evaporator to treat salt-containing dye wastewater can cause directional salt collection due to the temperature difference between the top and bottom. After 5 complete evaporation and collection cycles, the average salt collection capacity of the evaporator can still be maintained at 0.593 g, with a salt collection rate of 158.34 mg m–2 h–1. This biomimetic photothermal evaporator provides a solution for the recycle and high purification of salt-containing dye wastewater.

title: Robust Thermal Stability, Flame Retardancy, and Weather Resistance Cross-Linked Cellulose Aerogel toward High-Performance Passive Radiative Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The frequent occurrence of high temperatures has driven the development of green passive cooling technologies. Traditional passive radiative cooling materials have single performance, insufficient weather resistance and structural stability, and are unable to adapt to outdoor multifunctional thermal management. In this study, cellulose nanofibers were used as the substrate, and silica and methyltrimethoxysilane were incorporated to prepare a composite aerogel. Tests show that the optimal sample has excellent radiation cooling, heat insulation, flame retardancy, hydrophobicity, and sound absorption performance. With a solar reflectance of 93.5% and a mid-infrared emissivity of 94.3%, it provides a maximum outdoor temperature reduction of 15.7 °C. Its minimum thermal conductivity reaches 0.034 W m–1 K–1, offering excellent thermal insulation performance. The total heat release and the rate of heat release were significantly reduced, and flame retardancy was greatly improved. In addition, the sample exhibits a water contact angle of 137.2°, endowing it with favorable self-cleaning properties. The average sound absorption coefficient reaches 0.78 in the broadband range of 1000–6300 Hz, and the noise reduction performance is superior to that of commercial materials. This multifunctional composite aerogel overcomes the performance limitations of traditional materials and offers new insights into the development and application of outdoor integrated thermal management functional materials.

title: Activation‐Free and Strain‐Resilient Island‐Bridge Liquid Metal Inks for Machine‐Learning‐Enabled Epidermal Electromyography
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid metal particle‐based inks offer a scalable route toward stretchable electronics, yet their practical implementation is hindered by activation‐dependent conductivity and poor electrical stability under deformation. Herein, we report an intrinsically conductive and strain‐resilient liquid metal ink with a rationally engineered island‐bridge micro‐architecture, in which Cu‐decorated carbon nanotubes (CuCNTs) bridge adjacent liquid metal particles (LMPs) through initial hydrogen‐bonding/coordination‐assisted attachment to the native gallium‐oxide shell, followed by local Cu‐Ga alloying at the CuCNTs/LMPs interface. Enabled by solvent‐mediated dispersion and interfacial hybridization, the strain‐resilient composite ink supports high‐resolution (100 µm) screen printing and deformable circuit integration. The dynamically reconfigurable island‐bridge network retains a sheet resistance of 1.3 × 10 −1 Ω sq −1 at 300% strain, together with stable resistance during prolonged cyclic stretching and bending. When printed into a compact 12‐channel array on breathable fibrous substrates, the resulting electrode array exhibits low skin‐electrode impedance and superior high‐density surface electromyography (HD‐sEMG) performance compared with commercial gel electrodes. Combined with machine‐learning‐assisted analysis, the electromyography arrays enable training‐state recognition, individualized load assessment, and continuous monitoring of fatigue‐associated exercise states during dynamic exercise. This work provides a scalable strategy for intrinsically conductive liquid metal electronics and advances their application in intelligent wearable biointerfaces and soft electronic systems.

title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude – a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

title: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution.

title: Metal–Organic Framework@Polysulfone Composite Beads for Air Filtration of Postharvest Pathogenic Fungal Spores
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Phytopathogenic fungal infections pose a persistent threat to postharvest fruit quality and food security worldwide, with resistant strains increasingly limiting the efficacy of conventional fungicides. This study explored metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as an emerging class of antifungal materials and examined their potential for air-based decontamination in storage environments. Among the zinc- and copper-based frameworks tested, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 demonstrated exceptionally broad-spectrum antifungal activity, completely inhibiting mycelial growth of Penicillium expansum, Penicillium citrinum, and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, while maintaining strong inhibition of Botrytis cinerea and Mucor piriformis. To enable practical deployment, the most active MOFs were incorporated into polysulfone composite beads via phase inversion, preserving their antifungal properties while offering a processable and scalable format. In vitro assays revealed that these MOF@PSF beads substantially suppressed both mycelial growth and spore germination, with HKUST-1@PSF and ZIF-8@PSF composites reducing conidial viability to near-complete levels. Mechanistic studies revealed that HKUST-1 primarily acts through substantial copper ion release (≈19 ppm), leading to pronounced metabolic inhibition, whereas ZIF-8 operates via reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Evaluation in a dual-chamber air-filtration prototype demonstrated remarkable performance: both composites reduced airborne spore transfer by 95.2–96.7% for P. expansum and by 99.4–99.6% for B. cinerea, effectively preventing contamination of the clean chamber and protecting the stored produce. These findings establish MOF@PSF composite beads as bioactive filtration materials that combine physical spore capture with intrinsic antifungal action, offering a residue-free route to limiting fungal dissemination during postharvest storage.

title: Angular solar absorption and thermal energy storage seasonally modulate radiative cooling
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling materials (RCs) maintain low surface temperatures under sunlight and can reduce building cooling loads and urban overheating. However, RCs with static optical properties overcool in cold seasons, and adaptive RCs proposed to date rely on temperature/humidity to switch their optical/radiative properties. Further, they address either daytime or nighttime response and are subject to ageing and to false switching on mild sunlit winter days. Here, we propose a system to seasonally modulate RCs with angular solar absorption, achieved with L-shaped fins, and with thermal energy storage (TES), implemented with phase change materials (PCMs) and concrete mass. The L-shaped fins have solar-absorptive, equator-facing walls shaded by horizontal eaves, enabling high direct solar absorption only at the low solar elevations of winter, with RC film on all other surfaces. Coupled with TES, the system is an angular-dependent thermal-mass-enhanced radiative cooler (ATMRC). In field campaigns in Western Sydney, the finned RC samples reached winter daytime surface temperatures 6–9 °C above the static RC and up to 11 °C above the unfinned RC + TES, resolving the daytime overcooling that TES alone introduces. The ATMRC with the 8 °C PCM reduced winter dew and frost durations by 56% and 73%, respectively, relative to the static RC. The summer daytime penalty against the static RC was 2 °C. Ray-tracing yields seasonal absorbed fractions of 37% in winter and 21% in summer in Sydney. Effective adaptive RCs therefore require both TES against night overcooling and angular-dependent solar absorption for daytime modulation.
