title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH4-rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d-p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH4 over 1000 mA/cm2. With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH4-rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells.

title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.

title: Cephalopod-inspired embodied camouflage system for simultaneous evasion of artificial and human visual perception
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam’s potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications.

title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5σ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

title: MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS2-based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is −58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS2-based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties.

title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

title: Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Minimizing H2O2 consumption for efficient water decontamination is a crucial objective of Fenton-like reaction. However, the limited H2O2 activation and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) utilization efficiency are still two obstacles, mainly caused by high O-O bond energy barrier and short-lived free·OH generation. Here, we show an iron-based metal-organic frameworks with pyridine N secondary coordination sphere, i.e., N/MIL-53(Fe), whereas secondary coordination sphere has a strong interaction with the key *OH intermediates, thereby decreasing O-O homolytic cleavage barrier and promoting in-situ generation of long-lived adsorbed ·OH. Therefore, N/MIL-53(Fe) exhibits a H2O2 conversion efficiency up to about 90%, with adsorbed ·OH accounting for over 90% of the total. Meanwhile, N/MIL-53(Fe) achieves high activity for bisphenol A, tetracycline, phenol, p-chlorophenol and ciprofloxacin degradation (98% within 5 min) under trace H2O2 (0.5 mM), with H2O2 consumption equivalent to only 3% ~ 10% of reported Fenton-like catalyst. This study provides an efficient pathway for low-consumption water decontamination.

title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ/10 and annular features smaller than λ/60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration.

title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses.

title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis.

title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual’s distress to one’s own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer’s position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer’s spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2-expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases.

title: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with—and is in some cases surpassed by—TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists’ grading reaches quadratic Cohen’s kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology.

title: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution.

title: An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell (Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. We find that M. dawaensis has a soft, plastic-like deformation, a thick cuticle, a thin calcareous layer formed by non-interlocking shell units, and a significantly thick shell membrane. Its shell membrane is similar to that of avian eggs in structure, diameter, and arrangement of the fibers, as well as in the distinctions among outer, inner, and limiting membrane layers, but it is much thicker than that of avian eggs. In dinosaurian egg evolutionary history, M. dawaensis provides evidence of early Jurassic soft-shelled eggs, may represent the earliest stage of biomineralization, and bridges the gap between non-biomineralized membranous soft eggshells and biomineralized semi-rigid eggshells.

title: Thermo-responsive Ionizable Xanthone Bolaamphiphiles for Dynamic Self-Assembly into Nanovesicles Enabling Enhanced Intracellular Drug Release and Tumor Growth Inhibition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive supramolecular nanocarriers capable of controlled drug release have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional chemotherapy; however, the development of structurally defined small-molecule systems exhibiting thermo-responsive behavior within biologically relevant temperature ranges remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of ionizable xanthone-based bolaamphiphiles (X1–X3) engineered to undergo temperature-triggered self-assembly in aqueous media. Systematic modulation of oxyethylene-chain density revealed that X3 exhibits a sharp and reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transition within the physiological temperature window (35–40 °C), leading to the formation of stable nanovesicular assemblies. The resulting X3 nanovesicles accommodate doxorubicin (DOX) with an encapsulation efficiency of ∼25% and a drug-loading content of 11% while maintaining good colloidal stability under physiologically relevant conditions. X3-DOX nanovesicles exhibit progressive thermoresponsive drug release near physiological temperature, which is further enhanced under mild hyperthermia, together with an additional acid-responsive release behavior associated with protonation of the piperazine units (apparent pKa ≈ 4.5). Cellular studies performed in 4T1 breast cancer and A549 lung cancer cells demonstrated enhanced intracellular drug accumulation, superior cytotoxicity, and effective suppression of multicellular tumor spheroids compared with free DOX. Furthermore, the nanoformulation exhibited excellent hemocompatibility, favorable biodistribution characteristics, and efficient systemic clearance. In a 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model, X3-DOX induced remarkable tumor-growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. These findings establish thermo-responsive xanthone-based nanovesicles as a versatile supramolecular platform for controlled anticancer drug delivery and provide a molecularly defined strategy for developing stimuli-responsive nanomedicines.

title: Organic matter composition modulates its degradation under the combined effects of iron (oxyhydr)oxides and light
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. Carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-containing OM undergoes oxidation and decarboxylation, releasing carbon dioxide, whereas protein-like carboxyl–amine OM forms cross-linked products through condensation and polymerization, with only limited degradation. Iron and light promote oxidation–decarboxylation by enhancing electron transfer and visible-light absorption, while iron promotes protein unfolding and light may provide energy for polymerization. Under high-irradiance conditions equivalent to one-month cumulative daylight exposure, a conditional assessment of representative sunlight-exposed topsoil OM indicates potential carbon losses of ~8% for carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-type OM versus ~1% for carboxyl–amine-type OM. Photochemically promoted amide formation may limit OM degradation and carbon loss, informing carbon management and process-based carbon cycle models.

title: High- k Gate Dielectrics for Organic Field-Effect Transistors: Interfacial Engineering, Performance Optimization, and Scalable Flexible Electronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) are promising platforms for flexible, wearable, biointegrated, and large-area electronics owing to their mechanical compliance, solution processability, low-temperature fabrication, and molecular tunability. However, their practical application requires low-voltage operation, low power consumption, high operational stability, and scalable manufacturing, which are strongly influenced by the gate dielectric and its interface with the organic semiconductor. High-k gate dielectrics can increase gate capacitance and enhance electrostatic control, enabling low-voltage operation. However, a higher dielectric constant does not necessarily lead to better device performance, as strong polarization, surface polarity, interfacial trapping, dipolardisorder, remote phonon scattering, leakage, ion migration, and dielectric–semiconductor incompatibility can impair charge transport and device reliability. This Review presents a performance-oriented and interface-centered overview of high-k gate dielectrics for OFETs. We first classify high-k dielectric systems into inorganic oxides, molecularly engineered polymers, organic–inorganic hybrids and composites, and all-organic composite/multilayer structures, highlighting their polarization mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and structure–property relationships. We then discuss how dielectric properties and interfaces affect carrier mobility, threshold voltage, switching characteristics, charge injection, leakage current, hysteresis, and operational stability. Particular attention is given to interface engineering strategies, including surface modification, buffer layers, multilayer architectures, molecular design, composite construction, and defect/passivation control. We further discuss long-term reliability under electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses, as well as emerging dielectric systems, low-temperature and scalable fabrication, large-area uniformity, process integration, and commercialization challenges. Finally, we summarize key design considerations for balancing high capacitance, low leakage, interfacial compatibility, mechanical robustness, environmental stability, and scalable processability. By integrating dielectric design, interface engineering, device physics, reliability, and manufacturing, this Review provides guidelines for developing low-voltage, stable, and scalable OFETs for next-generation flexible electronics.

title: Harnessing Surface Wrinkling Instability for Visualizing Dynamic Chemistry in Polymer Networks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Studying dynamic chemical behaviors is fundamental to understanding and regulating the dynamic responses and functions of polymer materials. However, real-time, intuitive, and selective visualization of these molecular processes─particularly when multiple dynamic motifs coexist─remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce surface wrinkles as a visualization platform that directly translates dynamic chemical behaviors in polymers into observable macroscopic morphological changes. Using a dual-cross-linked polymer network (DCN) containing quadruple hydrogen bonds and mechanical bonds as a model system, we fabricate stable wrinkles via modulus mismatch in a bilayer architecture. In situ microscopy reveals that acid-triggered dissociation of quadruple hydrogen bonds causes rapid wrinkle erasure due to network disruption, whereas base-induced rotaxane sliding leads to gradual wrinkle erasure owing to network relaxation, reflecting their distinct dynamic mechanisms and time scales. Rheological analyses on single-cross-linked model networks corroborate these macroscopic observations at the molecular level. Moreover, by programming wrinkle patterns with “write–hide–read” functionality, we achieve macroscopic visualization and differentiation of microscopic dynamic processes. This work establishes surface wrinkling as a powerful and intuitive platform for real-time monitoring of dynamic chemistry and provides valuable insights for designing functional polymer materials with tunable macroscopic properties.

title: Aligned Self-Assembled Nanostructure by Chemical Force Trigger, Biased Migration, and Oscillatory Hydrogel Growth
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does. The trade-off between multiple microscale interactions in the chemo-material network implies molecular-biased migration resembling chemotactic-like directed motion in synthetic settings, which promotes spatial self-assembly remodelling. Consequently, regulating the reaction-diffusion chemistry, we demonstrate oscillatory hydrogel growth by encasing the c-FCRN with a physical membrane barrier. Furthermore, c-FCRN provides a rudimentary structure-building system to create various complex hydrogel structures, bypassing the 3D printing tools. Thus, the chemo-material network provides proof-of-concept for biomimetic material development by emulating biologically inspired technologies.

title: Operando X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Reveals Oxide Solid Electrolyte Stability against Electrochemically Plated Lithium
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

title: Non-equilibrium fluctuations in the corrosion process
source: Matter
abstract: Why does corrosion attack specific sites under some conditions but spread uniformly under others? Liang et al. combine real-time nanoscale imaging with atomistic simulations to show that corrosion reflects a competition between local structural heterogeneity and thermodynamic driving force. Near equilibrium, strained regions preferentially corrode and promote localized pitting; far from equilibrium, stronger driving forces overwhelm these local differences and produce rapid, uniform corrosion. The findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling localized material degradation.

title: Polymer coordination enables alloying-free synthesis of stable α-FAPbI3 thick films for real-time X-ray imaging
source: Matter
abstract: Stable α-FAPbI3 is promising for high-performance X-ray imaging but is difficult to produce without alloying. Here, polymer coordination with PVP enables stable, alloying-free α-FAPbI3 thick films by controlling crystallization and lattice strain. The resulting detectors combine high sensitivity, low-dose operation, and fast response, enabling high-resolution, real-time X-ray imaging.

abstract: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.

abstract: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances are used in data centre infrastructure manufacturing and cooling and can be contained in end-of-life waste. This Review examines the use of these chemicals across the data centre value chain and considers their management and potential for reduction.

title: Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Esters have widespread applications in nature and industry, making the strategic installation of ester bonds critical for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, polymers and other functional materials. However, achieving regioselective esterification of sterically demanding secondary alcohols in the presence of more reactive primary sites remains a formidable challenge. Here we report the engineering of aldehyde dehydrogenases into oxidative ester synthases (OxiEs) with divergent selectivities. Structure-guided protein engineering yielded two complementary catalyst classes: imidazole-dependent OxiEs1 favours primary alcohols and imidazole-independent OxiEs2 exhibits exclusive selectivity for secondary alcohols. Mechanistic studies revealed that imidazole acts as a molecular switch, allosterically tuning the active-site geometry to control regioselectivity. This system demonstrates a broad substrate scope, enabling direct, highly selective acylation of various secondary alcohols. Furthermore, we showcase its utility in controlling enantioselectivity, enabling redox-neutral synthesis and preparing valuable esters on gram-scale. This work establishes a strategy for regioselective control in esterification, transforming a classical hydride-transfer enzyme into a tunable platform for ester bond formation under mild, sustainable conditions.

title: Mechanistic Insights of Electroreductive Cobalt-Catalyzed Asymmetric Radical Addition
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric electroreduction has emerged as a compelling platform for enantioselective C–C bond formation, with notable advances in electroreductive cross-coupling. Translating this success to stereocontrolled radical additions across unsaturated bonds remains a formidable challenge, particularly for the construction of fully substituted stereogenic carbon centers. Herein, we report an electroreductive, cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric radical addition of diverse organohalides to α-imino esters. This protocol delivers enantioenriched α-quaternary amino acid derivatives in up to 95% ee, completely circumventing the need for stoichiometric metal reductants. Beyond its synthetic utility, the electrochemical platform uniquely enables the direct interrogation of the operative electron-transfer events. A comprehensive mechanistic study─encompassing cyclic voltammetry, in situ electrochemical EPR spectroscopy, DFT calculations, stoichiometric experiments, and radical-trapping experiments─elucidates a highly orchestrated catalytic manifold. Crucially, we demonstrate that the α-imino ester serves a dual role, acting as both a radical acceptor and a redox-active ligand for the chiral cobalt catalyst. Subsequent cathodic reduction of the resulting cobalt–imine complex generates a key low-valent species that engages the alkyl halide via a turnover-limiting single-electron transfer (SET) to produce the requisite alkyl radical. Overall, this work establishes a robust electrochemical framework that synergizes reaction innovation with fundamental mechanistic elucidation in asymmetric radical catalysis.

title: Decoding the risks of hydrogels for bone regeneration
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Hydrogels offer adaptable matrices for bone regeneration, yet clinical translation remains limited by application-specific failures in dynamic skeletal environments. This Review organizes these failures into mechanical, spatiotemporal and immune risks and outlines translational benchmarks and risk-controlled design principles.

title: Nested economies of scale in global city mass
source: Nature Cities
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    A long-standing puzzle in urban science is whether there is an intrinsic match between human populations and the mass of their built environments. Existing models assume proportionality: each additional resident demands the same amount of building material. Our analysis of more than 3,000 cities worldwide challenges this linear assumption. Built mass grows more slowly than population (that is, sublinear scaling), across cities (
                    β
                     = 0.90) and across neighborhoods within a city (
                    δ
                     = 0.75). This means that larger cities and denser neighborhoods achieve economies of scale with less per capita built mass. Our theoretical framework further shows that the across-city scaling pattern emerges from the uneven within-city distribution of people. These findings caution against well-meaning interventions, such as height and building-size limits, that artificially flatten cities’ natural density gradients. Effective urban policy should instead move beyond per capita linear thinking, adopting scale-adjusted metrics and managing cities as nested complex systems.

title: Urban scaling and the dynamics of individual cities
source: Nature Cities
abstract: Cities are often compared through scaling laws, usually expressed as power-law relations between population size and aggregate urban quantities related to infrastructure, socioeconomic activity, or environmental impacts. These laws are influential because their exponent is often interpreted as describing what happens when a city grows, with implications for urban theory, planning, and policy. Here, we show that this interpretation is generally misleading. An exponent measured by comparing many cities at one date does not, in general, describe the trajectory of any individual city. Instead, it reflects a statistical pattern produced by cities with different histories, constraints, institutions, and growth paths. Apparent sublinear or superlinear scaling can therefore arise even when individual cities follow simpler dynamics, as we show for the area--population relation. Cross-sectional scaling laws can reveal system-level regularities, but should not be used alone to infer growth mechanisms or guide policy for a given city.

title: In Situ Activated Bi2WO6 Nanosheets with Fast-Response and Self-Bleaching Electrochromism for Automotive Antiglare Rearview Mirrors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Trailing vehicle headlight glare critically endangers nighttime driving safety, with electrochromic devices (ECDs) being the most promising solution. Nevertheless, commercial organic electrochromic materials face high cost and irreversible degradation, whereas inorganic alternatives exhibit slow response and severe memory effect, severely restricting their application in antiglare rearview mirrors. Herein, we report the electrochromic behavior of thin bismuth tungstate (T-BWO) nanosheets synthesized via a facile hydrothermal method. A unique in situ activation process is discovered, accompanied by (19.7 ± 1.8)% leaching of surface Bi atoms and a transient dark transition state, which endows the activated T-BWO with exceptional electrochromic performance: an ultralow working voltage window of –0.6/0.3 V, ultrafast coloration/bleaching times of (0.81 ± 0.06)/(0.55 ± 0.04) s, a high coloration efficiency of (148.3 ± 7.8) cm2 C–1, and reasonably fast self-bleaching under open-circuit conditions. The assembled T-BWO-based self-bleaching ECD delivers a moderate optical modulation (ΔR) of (37.8 ± 1.7)% and excellent cycling stability (86% performance retention after 900 cycles). This work not only introduces a novel high-performance inorganic electrochromic material but also provides a new design paradigm for functional ECDs toward practical automotive antiglare applications.

title: Programmable mRNA vaccine materials for temporal control of antitumour immunity
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: mRNA cancer vaccines offer programmable control over antigen expression and immune activation, but their clinical performance may depend on when and where these signals occur. This Perspective introduces temporal immunoengineering and proposes phase-matched mRNA nanocarrier designs to coordinate immune priming and reinforcement across the perioperative window.

title: Comparing Nuclear Reaction Coordinates Driving Photoinduced Proton-Coupled Electron and Energy Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proton transfer is coupled to electron transfer or electronic excitation energy transfer in proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and proton-coupled energy transfer (PCEnT) reactions, respectively. Although photoinduced PCET and PCEnT have been studied extensively in anthracene–phenol–pyridine molecular triads, the nuclear reaction coordinates for these two pathways are still unknown. Herein, we identify the nuclear reaction coordinates for PCET and PCEnT in the triads by sampling the seam space between the relevant intersecting diabatic states. The reaction coordinate has contributions mainly from anthracene and phenol for PCET but involves the entire triad, including pyridine, for PCEnT. Both reaction coordinates involve motions related to contraction of the phenol C–O bond as well as motions within the anthracene rings that differ for PCET and PCEnT due to different charge distributions. The proton acceptor motion contributes more to the PCEnT than the PCET reaction coordinate. Both PCET and PCEnT reactions are concerted in that there is no stable intermediate, but they are both most likely asynchronous. Our analysis also suggests that PCET proceeds through a conical intersection in its minimum energy pathway, whereas PCEnT moves through an avoided crossing. The quantum mechanical treatment of the transferring proton within a vibronically nonadiabatic framework suggests that the kinetic isotope effect may be greater for PCEnT than for PCET, although more extensive calculations are required for confirmation. Understanding the fundamental similarities and differences between PCET and PCEnT mechanisms will help guide the design of proton-coupled systems that favor either charge transfer or energy transfer.

title: Cisplatin Conjugated with Vinylsulfonamide Cross-Links Pyruvate Kinase M2 to Trigger Ferroptosis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cisplatin serves as a first-line chemotherapeutic agent due to its DNA binding property. However, this intrinsic electrophilicity drives off-target interactions with proteins, which compromises anticancer efficacy, and also suggests the presence of unexplored targets. To identify platinum-binding proteins, a class of platinum(II) complexes containing a covalent vinylsulfonamide group were designed to provide stronger affinity for target engagement. By using competitive chemical proteomics technology, pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) was identified as the direct target of Pt1. The intracellular binding involved the recognition of the Cys49 pocket via cis-platinum moiety, which was strengthened by the synergistic event of platinum-centered ligand exchange and vinylsulfonamide-mediated covalent anchoring. This effective multimodal interaction disrupted PKM2 oligomerization and promoted its nuclear translocation. Subsequently, Pt1 induced ferroptosis via the PKM2-HMOX1 axis, further enhanced by mitochondrial oxidative stress. In xenograft models, Pt1 exhibited antitumor efficacy comparable to that of cisplatin, along with lower hepatotoxicity. This study presents a cisplatin conjugate that induces ferroptosis through intramolecular protein cross-linking, providing a synergistic coordination-covalent strategy for nonclassical platinum-based therapeutics.

title: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs. The quasi-solid precursor state facilitates efficient template infiltration while remaining reactive for COF crystallization, affording ordered macroporous photonic architectures within 3 min. This strategy is broadly applicable to a library of 16 COFs spanning β-ketoenamine, hydrazone, imine, and imide linkages, yielding decimeter-scale monoliths with designable structural colors across the visible spectrum. By integrating periodic macroporosity, permanent framework porosity, and photonic functionality into one material platform, the resulting IO COF PhCs enable cross-scale programmable optical encoding and visually self-reporting adsorption. The application potential of IO COF PhCs is demonstrated for biomimetic anti-counterfeiting patterns and structural-color-indicated Au capture. This work establishes a general route toward crystalline IO COF PhCs and provides a versatile platform for coupling molecular functionality with photonic regulation in advanced smart materials.

title: Modelling and Emulation of Afferent-Like Excitatory–Inhibitory Spiking Using Ovonic Threshold Devices for Neuromorphic Oscillatory Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spike-based computing has attracted increasing attention for efficient information processing, creating demand for neuromorphic hardware capable of generating and processing spikes. Ovonic threshold switching (OTS) devices are promising spiking neurons because their threshold-switching behavior and negative differential resistance enable compact spike-generation circuits, while their scalability supports dense integration. However, a circuit-level design framework linking defect dynamics with conduction behavior remains lacking. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an intensity-tuned artificial neuron based on a GeAsTe OTS device integrated with a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit. The neuron shows a non-monotonic excitatory–self-inhibitory response with applied voltage, phenomenologically analogous to excitatory–inhibitory behavior in biological neurons. The spiking frequency initially increases and then decreases beyond an inflection voltage point. This transition arises intrinsically from competition between RC charging dynamics and conductive filament retention in the OTS device, rather than from a separate inhibitory pathway. The neuron achieves a spiking frequency of up to 1.6 MHz. The behavior is supported by simulations using a dynamical model for diffusive filament-based memristors, accounting for resistance changes from filament formation and rupture. Furthermore, a physics-informed compact SPICE model combining defect-state transitions and filament evolution reproduces OTS switching and predicts neuron dynamics under varying temperatures, internal resistances, and circuit conditions. Finally, circuit simulations of a coupled OTS neuron network demonstrate vertex coloring with phase convergence within approximately 5 μs, highlighting the potential of this framework for compact, energy-efficient brain-inspired computing.

title: Improvement of Photocatalytic and Nanomechanical Properties of GaN Nanowires via Core-Shell Surface Modification
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The practical implementation of photocatalytic water splitting for sustainable hydrogen production is largely limited by the efficiency of the oxygen evolution reaction at the photoanode. Gallium nitride is a promising material for photoanode fabrication, provided that suitable nanostructuring strategies are applied to enhance its efficiency and stability. Here, we report the functionalization of gallium nitride nanowires with a 5 nm-thick titanium dioxide layer of and a 10 nm biomimetic polydopamine coating, resulting in a 1.9-fold (190%) increase in the anodic photocurrent, as demonstrated by chronoamperometry. We provide a detailed explanation of this enhancement based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and a series of optical studies. The observed decrease in photoluminescence intensity (60–90%) and shortening of carrier lifetimes from 0.17 to 0.07 ns correlate with the improved photocatalytic performance. Moreover, the 50% reduction in the band-to-band to defect emission ratio and the analysis of exciton recombination pathways show the role of defect-related and surface recombination processes in determining the photocatalytic activity of the nanowires. The enhanced photocatalytic performance is further attributed to shell deposition, which induces surface-state passivation, band realignment, and the quantum-confined Stark effect. Concurrently, changes in strain distribution are confirmed by increased heterogeneity of the GaN E2high phonon mode frequency distribution, expressed by an increase in the standard deviation from 0.09 up to 0.17 cm–1 and linewidth broadening from 3.2 up to 3.4 cm–1, as observed by Raman spectroscopy. Additionally, we show that the nanomechanical properties of the nanowires are significantly improved after shell deposition, by the elimination of pop-in events, enhanced elastic recovery, and an increase in Young’s modulus from 12 to 37 GPa. Finally, we point out opportunities for further optimization of similarly functionalized nanowire systems to achieve even higher efficiencies and support emerging applications.

title: Controlled Interfacial Electronic Coupling in Chemical Vapor Deposition-Grown WSe2 Monolayers on Au(111)
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report on the controlled growth and interface engineering of high-quality WSe2 monolayers on Au(111) using ambient-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) combined with comprehensive surface-sensitive characterization in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). The as-grown films exhibit a selenium buffer layer, which enables the formation of a weakly coupled WSe2 phase at the metal interface, as revealed by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). Annealing in UHV removes the selenium buffer layer and leads to the emergence of a pronounced moiré superstructure and a transition toward a strongly coupled WSe2 phase. Furthermore, this transformation is accompanied by pronounced modifications of the electronic structure, including phase-dependent changes in the valence band structure observed by angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES), a hybridization-induced metallization measured by scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), and a significant decrease in the work function determined by field emission resonance (FER) and ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy (UPS). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm strong WSe2–Au hybridization and the presence of the mid-gap states for the strongly coupled phase, whereas the Se8 buffer layer weakens the interaction of WSe2 with Au, so that its electronic structure is close to that for the freestanding system. Our results demonstrate that growth-induced interface chemistry provides a powerful handle to tune the electronic coupling in WSe2/Au(111), establishing a direct link between interfacial structure and electronic properties in metal–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) interfaces.

title: Surface and Electronic-Structure Regulation of NiCrPt-LDH for Ampere-Level Methanol-Assisted Hydrogen Production in Alkaline Seawater
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Substituting the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) provides an energy-saving route for alkaline seawater electrolysis, but it demands bifunctional electrodes that efficiently facilitate both anodic MOR and cathodic hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) in chloride-containing alkaline media. This work reports a surface and electronic-structure regulation strategy for a low-Pt (0.86 wt %) NiCrPt-LDH electrode constructed on nickel foam via a single-step hydrothermal route. The NiCrPt-LDH electrode integrates an open nanosheet framework, a defect-enriched metal–oxygen surface environment, and a super-hydrophilic/-aerophobic interface, which requires only 74, 146, and 228 mV to deliver 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm–2 for HER, respectively, with 1380 h of stability at 500 mA cm–2. Its Pt-mass-normalized HER activity is much higher than that of commercial Pt/C. For MOR in methanol-containing alkaline seawater, NiCrPt-LDH reaches 100 mA cm–2 under an applied potential of 1.401 V vs RHE. The NiCrPt-LDH (+) || NiCrPt-LDH (–) electrolyzer outputs 100 mA cm–2 at an operating voltage of 1.477 V, underscoring the potential of low-platinum, surface-engineered bifunctional LDH electrodes for methanol-assisted hydrogen production in alkaline seawater electrolysis.

title: High-Performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ Red Phosphor via Alloy Precursor Synthesis for Laser-Driven and Wide-Gamut Displays
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this work, the alloy-precursor solid-state synthesis strategy (AS-method) is employed to fabricate high-performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ phosphors. This approach effectively suppresses the oxidation of Eu2+ to Eu3+ compared to conventional solid-state synthesis (S-method). The resultant optimization of the local structure not only enhances the structural rigidity but also modulates the surrounding chemical pressure at different activator sites. This site-selective regulation leads to spectral narrowing and a blue shift in the emission. The optimized phosphor exhibits an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 52.38%, a value that ranks among the highest reported for the SLA-based phosphors. Furthermore, it demonstrates an ultrahigh saturation threshold of 90.69 W/mm2 under blue laser excitation, surpassing most reported red phosphors. When applied in white LEDs, it achieves 104% of the NTSC color gamut. Thus, this phosphor indicates great potential for applications in both laser-driven and high-color-gamut displays.

title: Vicinal Functional-Group Engineering in Defect-Engineered MOFs for One-Step Ethylene Purification
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of C2H6-selective adsorbents offers a promising strategy for energy-efficient C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. However, the similar physicochemical properties of C2H6 and C2H4 make it challenging to achieve preferential adsorption of C2H6. Herein, we propose a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy to construct C2H6-recognition domains, enabling efficient one-step C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. The adjacent functional groups on the modulators are introduced close to the defect sites of MOFs, constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments for C2H6 recognition. The fluorinated-defective MOF (UiO-66-(CF3)2) exhibits C2H6 preferential adsorption with an uptake of 2.2 mmol/g at 298 K and 100 kPa. Breakthrough experiments further confirm the dynamic separation performance of UiO-66-(CF3)2, achieving high-purity C2H4 (>99.99 %) with a productivity of 12.67 L/kg. Theoretical calculations further reveal that the adjacent functional groups in the ligands would induce electrostatic potential redistribution and confined pore structures, strengthening C2H6 adsorption on defective MOF over C2H4. This work establishes a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy for constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments toward C2H6 recognition in MOFs.

title: Three-Dimensional-Printed Lithium-Doped Conductive Carbon@Hydroxyapatite Scaffolds for Coordinated Neurovascular-Osseous Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The repair of critical-sized bone defects remains a formidable clinical challenge, where coordinated neurovascular reconstruction is important for effective bone regeneration. Accordingly, this study aimed to develop a three-dimensional (3D)-printed hydroxyapatite (HAp) scaffold integrating a polydopamine (PDA)-derived conductive carbon interface with Li+ release, and to evaluate its neural-, vascular-, and osteogenic-related effects in vitro and its bone-regenerative performance in vivo. A lithium-containing, hydrothermally carbonized HAp scaffold (HAp@C/Li) was fabricated through 3D printing, Li+-assisted dopamine coating, and hydrothermal carbonization. Material characterization confirmed a PDA-derived carbon coating with measurable local surface conductivity and Li+ release characterized by an early release phase followed by a gradual plateau. In vitro experimental results revealed that HAp@C/Li possessed excellent cytocompatibility. It effectively promoted neurite outgrowth of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, migration and tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), as well as osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In vivo evaluation in a rat femoral condyle defect model showed favorable bone repair, collagen deposition, vascular remodeling, and neural-associated tissue responses, with significantly higher BMD at 8 weeks, whereas BV/TV did not differ significantly from that of the HAp group. Collectively, these results indicate that the HAp@C/Li scaffold provides a promising therapeutic strategy for the clinical repair of critical-sized bone defects.

title: Dynamic Energy-Dissipating Interface Design Reconciles Thermal Performance with Interfacial Reliability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Highly filled thermal interface materials (TIMs) are essential for reliable heat dissipation in high-power electronics, yet restricted polymer chain mobility and reduced interfacial conformability make it difficult to achieve high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and crack-growth resistance simultaneously. We propose a dynamic energy-dissipating interface (DEDI) strategy that coordinates favorable interfacial affinity, stable chemical anchoring, and dynamic bulk energy dissipation to improve interfacial stability and crack resistance in highly filled TIMs. γ-Methacryloxypropyl trimethoxysilane (γ-MPS) provides stable chemical anchoring at the substrate interface, while urethane-associated polar interactions contribute to favorable interfacial affinity. Reversible disulfide and hydrogen-bond interactions within the bulk network promote deformation accommodation and mechanical energy dissipation. Surface-modified Al2O3/ZnO hybrid fillers form a multiscale network that provides efficient heat-transfer pathways. The resulting PSM-60-1.2 exhibits a thermal conductivity of 3.88 W·m−1·K−1, an adhesion strength of 4.25 MPa, and an adhesion energy of 3080.04 J·m−2. Combined experimental and finite-element analyses support coordinated interfacial stabilization, bulk energy dissipation, and enhanced thermomechanical deformation accommodation. After 100 thermal shock cycles between −40 and 150 °C, PSM-60-1.2 shows a 6.0 °C increase in maximum steady-state temperature, compared with 16.2 °C for the commercial thermally conductive adhesive, with less interfacial cracking and low-viscosity liquid infiltration. The DEDI design offers a molecular strategy for combining high thermal conductivity, high adhesion energy, and long-term thermomechanical reliability in highly filled TIMs.

title: Magnetic Fe/Cu Metal–Organic Frameworks-Derived Trilayer Cathode for Enhanced Enrofloxacin Degradation in Heterogeneous Electro-Fenton via Synergistic Radical and Nonradical Pathways
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous electro-Fenton (HEF) technology represents a promising eco-friendly strategy for wastewater remediation. However, sluggish Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling and reliance on a single hydroxyl radical (•OH) pathway limit its overall catalytic efficiency and oxidant utilization. Herein, a bifunctional trilayer cathode (Fe8Cu2@C-GF/ACF) was fabricated by integrating activated carbon fiber (ACF) with a magnetic Fe/Cu metal–organic frameworks-derived layer grown on graphite felt. This architecture spatially couples H2O2 electrogeneration with immediate activation, maximizing the effective utilization of generated oxidants. Furthermore, Cu incorporation thermodynamically accelerates Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling. The bimetallic synergy facilitates the simultaneous generation of radical (•OH) and nonradical (1O2) species. Quenching and EPR analyses confirmed these dual pathways collectively accelerate enrofloxacin (ENRO) degradation. The system achieves excellent mineralization across a broad initial pH range (3.0 to 9.0). Crucially, effective operation at neutral pH eliminates the need for chemical adjustment. Specifically, treating 100 mg L−1 ENRO at initial pH 7.0 and 18 mA cm−2 yielded a 75.6% mineralization degree. Degradation intermediates were elucidated via DFT calculations and UPLC-QqQ-MS analysis. Finally, the cathode exhibits high stability and low metal leaching. Its intrinsic magnetic recoverability prevents secondary solid waste and promotes practical material reuse for sustainable water treatment.

title: An Organic–Inorganic Hybrid Memristor with Trap-Assisted Hopping for Synaptic Plasticity and Artificial Nociceptor
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware demands artificial synaptic devices that mimic biological synapses. Achieving multifunctional emulation of synaptic plasticity and nociceptive behavior in a single, highly stable, low-power device remains a major challenge. In this report, zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONP) are synthesized via a surfactant-assisted sol–gel method. These are incorporated into an organic small-molecule matrix of 6,13-bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl)pentacene (TP) to fabricate a solution-processed organic–inorganic hybrid memristor. The as-fabricated hybrid memristor mimicked artificial synaptic behavior at a low operating voltage (<±1 V) while demonstrating high stability with retention exceeding 105 s in ambient atmosphere. The TP/ZnONP-based memristor has illustrated both short-term and long-term synaptic plasticity, facilitating the exemplification of learning and memory functions of biological synapses. The memristor has been found to exhibit pain-perception-related nociceptive behavior, including protective responses to excessive stimulation and self-recovery, closely resembling that of biological nociceptors. The device exhibits neurapraxia-like responses with a recovery time of only 40 s. The experimentally obtained synaptic characteristics are further employed in a device-aware fully connected artificial neural network, yielding a handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 97.9%. Various investigations on the dynamics of charge transport have revealed trap-assisted hopping through transient localization, which is induced by shallow and deep traps. The integration of artificial nociception and pattern recognition in a highly stable low-power synaptic device demonstrates the potential of the hybrid memristor for multifunctional neuromorphic hardware.

title: Hierarchical Functionalized Lignin Interfaces Regulate Water Transport in Low-Coating-Content Bio-Based Polyurethane-Coated Urea
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bio-based polyurethane coatings are promising for controlled-release fertilizers, but their release performance at low coating contents is often limited by rapid surface wetting and water transport through the coating membrane. Here, we constructed a hierarchical lignin-based interface on castor-oil-derived polyurethane-coated urea to regulate water–coating interactions. Lignin micro/nanospheres were sequentially functionalized with polydopamine and octadecyltrichlorosilane and introduced at the outer polyurethane interface during the final coating stage. Thermodynamic calculations and spectroscopic analyses were consistent with interfacial chemical coupling between polydopamine-associated functional groups and residual isocyanate groups in the polyurethane coating. The resulting interface increased the apparent water contact angle from 87.4° to 157.2°, weakened the calculated adsorption of water, and reduced water-vapor permeability through the coating. Under a nominal total coating-material input of approximately 3 wt %, the cumulative nitrogen release within 10 days decreased from 56% for bio-based polyurethane-coated urea (BCU) to 20% for OTS-LMNPs@PDA-modified bio-based controlled-release urea (SBCU), while the time required to reach 80% nitrogen release increased from 20 to 49 days. This enhanced release performance was associated with reduced surface wetting, lower water affinity, and slower water transport across the modified coating, which collectively delayed water penetration, urea dissolution, and subsequent nitrogen diffusion. These results demonstrate that lignin-based interfacial modification provides an effective strategy for regulating water transport and improving the controlled-release performance of low-coating-content bio-based polyurethane fertilizers.

title: Synergistic Interfacial Engineering in V2C MXene Heterostructures for Enhanced Nano-aluminum Reactivity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nano-aluminum (nano-Al) is a high-energy-density material with exceptional reactivity, making it promising for aerospace and military applications. Reducing particle size increases the active surface area and interfacial mass diffusion, but intrinsic agglomeration and dense alumina shells hinder diffusion. Conventional additives often reduce reactivity. Here, we modulate nano-Al interfacial diffusion through synergistic interactions in a V2C MXene heterostructure. The self-assembly of nano-Al on MXene suppresses agglomeration, while fluorine-containing terminations etch the alumina shells. The heterostructure also forms metal oxide contact layers that promote solid-phase thermite reactions. These effects increase the peak heat flow in air to 107.6 W g−1, 3.5 times that of pristine nano-Al. Solid-phase reactions complete energy release before Al melting, minimizing energy loss. The composite shows larger flame areas and a lower minimum ignition concentration (≥5 wt %). Adjusting the heating temperature reduces the total combustion duration by 88.9% and increases the dynamic pressure. This versatile fabrication process enables tunable performance for diverse operational environments.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Matching in Amorphous Fe2O3/Crystalline Cu2O Enables Efficient Nitrate-To-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate (NO3–) reduction to ammonia (NH3) is a promising route for simultaneous nitrate remediation and sustainable NH3 synthesis, yet remains challenged by sluggish multistep hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we report an amorphous Fe2O3/crystalline Cu2O catalyst (a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O), in which ultrasmall Cu2O nanocrystallites are uniformly dispersed in an amorphous Fe2O3 matrix. The resulting a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O interface induces strong electronic interaction and complementary catalytic functions. The pH-dependent potential analysis shows that a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O maintains a highly alkaline interfacial microenvironment, while stepwise kinetic measurements reveal favorable kinetic matching between NO3– activation and subsequent NO2– hydrogenation. In situ spectroscopic studies reveal a tandem catalytic pathway in which NO3– is first activated on c-Cu2O to form NO2–, followed by transfer to adjacent a-Fe2O3 sites for hydrogenation to NH3. Consequently, a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O achieves an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 92.4% and an NH3 yield rate of 6.25 mmol h–1 mg–1, and sustains stable operation for 100 h in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer. This work offers a viable strategy for promoting nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis through amorphous/crystalline interfacial engineering.

title: Quantum Ghost Spectroscopy Reveals Hidden Coherence in Molecular Aggregates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ultrafast spectroscopy of complex molecules has been achieved under light–matter coupling by the use of laser pulses and single photons. Yet, the excited-state dynamics essential to photochemistry is suffering from the convolution of multiple relaxation pathways and limited resolution in nonlinear signal, which still remain challenging. To address these, we develop time-resolved quantum ghost spectroscopy (tr-QGS) with entangled light, which enables a background-free detection of excited-state emission while offering precise control over temporal resolution. We apply this approach to perylene bisimide (PBI-1) trimers by combining a quantum description of light-molecule interaction with time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (TD-DMRG) simulations. This explicitly includes five vibrational modes and nonadiabatic coupling between electronic states. Our simulations reveal that tr-QGS captures electronic coherence oscillating at 0.6 eV for ∼50 fs, a signature of nonadiabatic coupling that was obscured in time-resolved measurements. Moreover, we observe a direct transfer from electronic to vibrational coherence at 200 fs, providing real-time visualization of vibronic relaxation pathways. Photon entanglement eliminates background noise and ground-state bleaching artifacts, which plague time-resolved measurements. These results establish tr-QGS as a transformative tool for interrogating nonadiabatic dynamics in molecular aggregates, light-harvesting complexes, and photocatalysts, offering a route to reveal quantum coherence effects in chemistry with unprecedented precision.

title: Synergistic Coordination Regulation and Nanofiller-Guided Ion Transport in a Polyacrylamide Gel Electrolyte for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zn Metal Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite their safety and cost advantages, aqueous zinc-ion batteries remain limited by the instability of Zn metal anodes, including nonuniform deposition, dendrite growth, and parasitic reactions. A PAM/CMC-Na/CNTs (PCC) hydrogel electrolyte is constructed by incorporating sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC-Na) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into a polyacrylamide (PAM) matrix. The –COO– and –OH groups of CMC-Na regulate the local coordination environment of Zn2+ and suppress water-related side reactions, while CNTs reinforce the gel network and improve interfacial contact. PCC exhibits an ionic conductivity of 24.16 mS cm–1 and an apparent Zn2+ transference number of 0.791. These transport characteristics, together with interfacial analyses, are consistent with more uniform Zn deposition. Zn//Zn symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2300 h at 1 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 1 mAh cm–2 and for approximately 550 h at 5 mA cm–2 with a capacity of 5 mAh cm–2. Zn//Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.94%, while Zn//MnO2 full cells retain 81.64% capacity after 700 cycles at 1 A g–1. A high-loading Zn//MnO2 pouch cell further demonstrates favorable energy-storage performance. This work presents a strategy for designing hydrogel electrolytes that integrate coordination regulation, homogenized ion transport, and mechanical robustness.

title: Amorphous Halide Cathodes Enable 75C All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Power delivery in all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) is often pursued by maximizing the bulk ionic conductivity of cathode active materials (CAMs), while grain-boundary (GB) ion-transport barriers caused by lattice mismatch remain a major kinetic bottleneck. Here, we reveal that minimizing GB transport barriers, rather than simply enhancing intrinsic conductivity, unlocks ultrafast ion-transport in halide CAMs. Amorphization converts crystalline LiVCl4 into a conformal amorphous phase that preserves short-range V–Cl coordination while minimizing long-range ion-transport tortuosity. Despite lower bulk Li+ conductivity, amorphous LiVCl4 dramatically reduces GB-associated interfacial resistance and enables a catholyte-free cathode (CAM content: 90 wt %) to deliver a capacity of 74.3 mAh g–1 at 5 mA cm–2, compared with 10.2 mAh g–1 for the crystalline counterpart. Meanwhile, the ASSLB further operates across a wide temperature range from −30 to 60 °C and achieves 84.2% capacity utilization at an ultrahigh A-LiVCl4 areal loading of 53.4 mg cm–2. Coupled with amorphous LiTaOCl4, the ASSLB achieves 102.1 mAh g–1 at 20 mA cm–2 (∼75C) and retains 82.3% capacity after 16,000 cycles. These results establish amorphization-enabled conformal interfaces as a new paradigm for ultrahigh-power ASSLBs.

title: Macrocycle Size-Controlled Dynamic and Static Chirality in Donor–Acceptor [2]Catenanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chiral [2]catenanes, a prominent class of mechanically interlocked molecules (MIMs), can exhibit either static or dynamic mechanostereochemistry. Controlling these mechanostereochemical states without altering the covalent connectivity, however, remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of chiral [2]catenanes derived from ExBox and cycloparaphenyleneperylene (CPPP), whose dynamic behavior is altered by the size of the CPPP macrocycle. We identified a sharp, size-dependent threshold: The conformational stereogenic unit of [7]CPPP is kinetically locked, whereas those of [8]CPPP and [9]CPPP are dynamic at room temperature. This conformational stereochemistry strongly biases the co-conformational stereochemistry in the catenane, effectively resulting in a single dominant diastereomer. This effective coupling of the two stereogenic units allows the conformational stereochemistry to be biased by the ion pairing of the interlocked cationic ring with a chiral anion. This research highlights the potential of mechanically interlocked architectures for controlling the dynamic mechanostereochemistry.
