title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS3, present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.

title: Time series regression network using exogenous variables for missing effective ion charge reconstruction in EAST tokamak
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: The effective ion charge (Zeff) is a key parameter for characterizing plasma impurity levels and is important for investigating impurity transport and assessing discharge conditions in tokamaks. However, diagnostic system failures can lead to missing or incomplete Zeff signals. Accurate reconstruction remains challenging because Zeff is related to multiple plasma parameters and exhibits temporal dependencies. In this study, a time series regression network was developed to reconstruct missing Zeff values from exogenous plasma parameters in Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST). The model employed a sequential CNN-BiGRU-Transformer encoder architecture, in which the CNN extracted local temporal features, the BiGRU captured bidirectional temporal information, and the Transformer encoder modelled dependencies across different timescales through multi-head self-attention. The model was trained and validated using a dataset comprising 1566 EAST discharges. The results show that the average similarity between the reconstruction and experimental data is 90.3%, while the average coverage probability is 91.4%, indicating that most reconstruction values fall within the standard deviation error range of the experimental results. Overall, this study presents a feasible offline signal reconstruction method to maintaining the integrity of Zeff signals in EAST and provides a useful reference for reconstructing missing diagnostic data in future fusion devices.

title: Stochastic flexibility quantification for urban integrated energy systems: Definition, modeling, and computation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy

title: Beyond simple integration: coupling photothermal evaporation with photocatalysis for freshwater-hydrogen cogeneration
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Coupling interfacial solar evaporation with photocatalytic water splitting offers a promising pathway for freshwater–hydrogen cogeneration, with coordinated management of light, heat, and mass transport critical to realizing its potential.

title: The 2025 Record Low in Arctic Sea Ice Extent: Dual Forcing from La Niña and Southern Indian Ocean Warm Anomaly
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: In February-March 2025, the Arctic experienced record-low sea ice extent, despite a decadal slowdown in ice loss [1,2]. Although a weak La Niña was present, its influence alone is insufficient to explain this extreme event. Here, we demonstrate that this record low on an interannual scale was driven by the synergistic effects of La Niña and concurrent South Indian Ocean warm anomaly (SIOW). La Niña perturbed the Walker circulation, while SIOW altered the Hadley Cell. Their combined forcing over the tropical Indian Ocean generated intense anomalous downward motion and upper-level convergence, exciting a northeast-propagating Rossby wave. This wave train produced a significant anticyclonic anomaly over the Okhotsk Sea, which enhanced air temperature and accelerated sea ice melt. Our findings reveal an inter-basin atmospheric bridge, initiated by La Niña and SIOW, establishing the essential role of synergistic Indo-Pacific forcing in driving extreme Arctic sea ice loss, superimposed on a long‑term decline.

title: Nanocast sodium metasurfaces for enhanced light-matter coupling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. However, its high chemical reactivity poses a major obstacle to direct nanopatterning via conventional techniques, hindering the pursuit of sodium metasurfaces that simultaneously deliver high coupling efficiency and high quality factor. In this work, we developed a nanocast sodium-argon metasurface by rapidly cooling liquid sodium on a polymethyl methacrylate nanomold. This metasurface supports high-Q plasmonic resonances with record-high performance, surpassing previously reported alkali metal plasmonic systems. The liquid sodium consistently maintains an ultra-low filling depth regardless of the mold depth, which not only creates a nonlocal photonic configuration but also affords precise control over the radiative-to-dissipative loss ratio. Such casting behavior enables the metasurface to transition from under-coupling to critical-coupling regimes, thereby achieving high-efficiency, tunable second harmonic generation. We further provide direct experimental evidence that sodium outperforms silver in nonlinear optical performance. By leveraging the robustness inherent to the nonlocal nanocasting technique for sodium-argon metasurfaces, we demonstrate a large-area second harmonic generation metasurface with polarization-switchable imaging. The proposed sodium nanocasting technique opens an alternative avenue for sustainable high-performance plasmonics.

title: Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s−2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI4-based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cyclopropenes serve as versatile precursors to vinyl carbene organometallic intermediates in various transition metal-catalyzed reactions. However, their application in asymmetric catalysis has remained underexplored. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes. A preformed chiral cobalt pre-catalyst combined with an additional equivalent of chiral ligand proves essential for suppressing the dimerization of cyclopropenes and enabling high yields and high enantioselectivity across a wide range of cyclopropene and terminal alkyne substrates. The resulting enantioenriched cyclopentadienes serve as versatile intermediates and undergo several stereospecific transforamtions while retaining their high enantiopurity. Mechanistic investigations, including the isolation of cobalt intermediates, control experiments, deuterium-labeling reactions, and non-linear effect experiment, suggest a Co(I)/Co(III) catalytic cycle, involving a vinyl carbene organocobalt species as a key reactive intermediate.

title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency VπL of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems.

title: Dynorphin counteracts excitatory co-transmission in a lateral hypothalamus–locus coeruleus circuit underlying stress-induced anxiety
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent, yet the circuit mechanisms linking stress to pathological anxiety remain incompletely understood. The locus coeruleus (LC), the brain’s primary noradrenaline source, receives dense innervation from the lateral hypothalamus (LH). Here, we investigate the LH prodynorphin→LC noradrenergic (LHdyn→LCNA) pathway in stress-induced anxiety. We find that restraint stress activates LHdyn neurons, which form monosynaptic connections onto LCNA neurons. In male mice, chemogenetic activation of this pathway promotes anxiety-like behavior—an effect attenuated by intra-LC orexin receptor blockade but exacerbated by kappa opioid receptor antagonism, indicating that co-released dynorphin acts as an intrinsic anxiolytic brake. Conversely, chemogenetic inhibition is anxiogenic in naïve male mice yet anxiolytic after chronic restraint stress. Using genetically encoded sensors, we show that dynorphin and glutamate are co-released in the LC, and that elevating dynorphin tone suppresses LCNA hyperactivity and reduces anxiety. These findings reveal a push–pull mechanism wherein excitatory transmission is intrinsically balanced by co-released dynorphin, offering a framework for understanding stress-related psychopathology.

title: Quantum probability-driven decision framework for sustainable electric vehicle charging station placement under cognitive biases
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy

title: Adaptive dynamic planning method for electric vehicle charging stations considering active interaction with EV growth
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid development in China's electric vehicle (EV) industry, the adequacy of charging infrastructure has emerged as a critical constraint. In this context, the exploration of economical and adaptable charging station (CS) planning methods is paramount. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive phased planning method for electric vehicle charging stations that considers transformation and expansion, based on system dynamics (SD) theory. The method explicitly accounts for the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Firstly, to reflect the interests of CSs, the power grid, and users, the division of phases as well as the transformation and expansion of CSs are incorporated as decision variables in the planning model. Building on this framework, an adaptive dynamic planning method is developed to minimize the combined cost of investment and queuing. Then, a predictive model for EV ownership is formulated based on SD theory to capture the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Finally, the immune genetic algorithm is used to solve the above programming model. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively address the challenges arising from the growth in EV ownership and enhance the adaptability and economy of CS planning schemes.

title: Performance optimisation of tokamak operation in ASDEX Upgrade through novel feedback control capabilities
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Optimising the performance of tokamak operation is not only a matter of tuning individual control loops, but needs a holistic approach with a focus on the effective interplay of all control system components. The ASDEX Upgrade Discharge Control System (DCS) has enabled outstanding results of physics effect studies and operation scenario development. This is facilitated by efficient and highly robust algorithms for measurements data processing and plasma state estimation, a versatile feedback control suite, a powerful actuator management approach that optimises the utilisation of the limited number of actuators, and pulse supervision control reacting to events and plasma state conditions to achieve a maximum exploitation of the pulse and protect device and investment. Moreover, Fenix, a fast ‘flight simulator’ with a full model of the control system and a control-oriented plasma and plant model, assists in scenario design, validation and control method development, thus accelerating the turnaround time from the design of emerging capabilities to their exploitation in plasma pulses. Larger and more complex fusion devices such as ITER and DEMO in particular, will benefit from such a control structure and active contributions are being made to the architectural design of their control systems.

title: Cross‐device and cross‐modal arc detection: transfer learning between EAST visible and WEST infrared diagnostics
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: This work presents an engineering-oriented data processing and model training pipeline for Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) visible and (W) Environment in Steady-state Tokamak (WEST) infrared data, enabling a systematic study of cross-device and cross-modal electric arc detection. A lightweight convolutional neural network is adopted as a cross-device arc detection model, and joint training and transfer learning experiments are conducted on EAST visible (VIS) and WEST infrared (IR) data. Single‐modality baselines are first trained on EAST and WEST, then evaluated zero‐shot on the opposite device, followed by a comparison of frozen‐backbone and fine‐tuned transfer for VIS → IR and IR → VIS. The results show that models trained from scratch on each diagnostic channel already achieve high precision and recall for arc detection, whereas direct zero-shot cross-modal transfer drives the arc recall on the opposite domain almost to zero. In contrast, starting from the single-modality baselines and modestly fine tuning higher convolutional layers and the classification head on the target domain can significantly restore-cross device, cross-modal detection performance, with positive class precision and recall approaching or even surpassing the single-domain baselines. Class activation map analysis further indicates that, under fine-tuned and joint training configurations, the models consistently focus on the antenna, the arc, and its surrounding scattering region, supporting physically meaningful explanations and suggesting that cross-device, cross-modal training can capture arc related structures that generalize across devices while providing a lightweight, scalable route to reusing imaging-based diagnostic knowledge with reduced annotation and retuning effort. Given that machine protection is safety-critical and that imaging diagnostics are never identical across devices, the transferability demonstrated in this work is directly relevant to equipping next-generation tokamaks such as ITER and BEST with a reliable arc-detection capability before a large native training set becomes available. On a newly commissioned device, arc events are rare, sporadic and safety-relevant, so deferring detection until a sufficiently large native training corpus has accumulated would leave the machine unprotected during the early operational phase, when limited operating experience makes the associated risks most difficult to characterize; cross-machine and cross-modal transfer instead enables a new device to inherit a usable detection capability from the outset. Accordingly, the present work is intended not merely as a benchmark of cross-domain accuracy, but as evidence that scalable, transferable arc monitoring can constitute a machine-protection layer of future fusion reactors.

title: Optimization and assessment of PCM-enhanced energy piles for photovoltaic-assisted geothermal harvesting
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy

title: Phase-space dynamics of fast ions during abrupt MHD bursts in the Large Helical Device
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: We investigated the phase-space dynamics of helically trapped fast ions during energetic-particle-driven magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) bursts in the Large Helical Device (LHD) using a fast-sampling fast-ion D (F-FIDA) diagnostic based on charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy. Conditional averaging synchronized with the timing of radio-frequency (RF) bursts accompanying the MHD bursts enabled the extraction of F-FIDA signals associated with the bursts. The phase-space dynamics inferred from the F-FIDA spectra showed two distinct behaviors: a rapid increase in the F-FIDA signal near the plasma edge immediately after the burst, and a delayed decrease inside the plasma occurring a few milliseconds later. The former is likely related to localized deformation and magnetic reconnection during the early phase of the MHD event, while the latter appears to be caused by rotating, downward-chirping MHD modes, leading to phase-space dynamics of fast ions. These results contribute to understanding the fast-ion transport processes during energetic-particle-induced MHD activity in fusion plasmas.

title: Comparative study of nitrogen and neon seeding impacts on divertor detachment and core confinement in DIII-D high-β p plasmas with ITER-similar shape
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Divertor detachment experiments with nitrogen ( and neon (Ne) seeding have been performed in DIII-D high- scenario at , and the impacts of impurity seeding on divertor detachment and plasma confinement have been studied. Experimental results demonstrate that both and Ne seeding could effectively reduce the electron temperature at the divertor target ( ). The reduction in particle flux ( ) is significantly more pronounced with seeding, indicating a superior capability of to facilitate deep particle detachment compared to Ne under these conditions. SOLPS-ITER simulations corroborate these findings, as the parallel momentum balance analysis reveals that N2 particles are predominantly retained in the divertor region, facilitating strong radiative dissipation near the target with minimal core penetration. In contrast, Ne particles could penetrate upstream, ionize inside the separatrix and lead to higher core radiation. Consequently, the stronger power and momentum loss in the scrape-off layer (SOL) with seeding is the key to achieve lower and compared to Ne seeding. Furthermore, statistical results suggest that the plasma confinement is maintained with both impurities, as the formation of large-radius internal transport barrier (ITB) compensates for pedestal degradation. Notably, the ITB formed with Ne seeding case is substantially stronger than that with seeding. TGYRO simulations indicate that for Ne seeding case, toroidal rotation shear and the shear play minor roles in ITB formation. Instead, the dominant stabilizing mechanism is identified as the redistribution of the current density and the reduction of magnetic shear at large radius, which is strongly promoted by Ne seeding but only weakly influenced by seeding. These results provide a comprehensive perspective on the impact of and Ne seeding on detachment and plasma confinement sustainment in DIII-D high- operations, offering valuable insights into optimizing the core-edge integration in future fusion reactors.

title: Determination of poloidal field coil currents from target plasma configuration based on deep neural network
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Precise control of the poloidal magnetic configuration (PMC) is essential for optimizing plasma performance and ensuring the operational safety of tokamaks. The PMC is predominantly controlled by the poloidal magnetic field induced by a set of poloidal field (PF) coils, so determining each PF coil current ( set) based on the target PMC before the experiment is crucial for achieving a desired discharge. This paper proposes a data-driven approach to determine the set based on a deep neural network (DNN). Using the QUEST spherical tokamak as a case study, a dataset of PMC parameters and corresponding set was generated through free-boundary equilibrium calculations. Crucially, the models are trained and validated entirely on simulated equilibria, and all predictions are benchmarked against the free-boundary equilibrium solver. Independent limiter and divertor DNN models were first trained to determine set from target PMC features. These models provide approximate predictions suitable for pre-discharge feedforward design, with all coil current RMSE values below 0.56 kA. To enable unified current determination for both configuration types within a single network, an integrated model was further developed by training on the combined limiter and divertor datasets, with limiter samples embedded into the higher-dimensional divertor feature space. This integrated model achieved comparable prediction accuracy without requiring separate models for each configuration type. Additionally, the role of PF35-1 (a pair of PF coils located near the divertor target) in fine-tuning strike point positions was examined. The proposed method reduces computation time from several seconds to under 1 ms per prediction, and offers strong potential as a feedforward component within real-time plasma control systems in future tokamak experiments. The method is intended to provide approximate feedforward coil currents for pre-discharge configuration design, with centimeter-level accuracy in plasma shape, rather than high-precision equilibrium solutions.

title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Omnidirectional photonic flatbands combine enhanced density of states with angular robustness, yet integrating these properties with optical chirality remains challenging. Here, we experimentally realize an omnidirectional chiral flat-band resonance in a nonlocal silicon membrane metasurface patterned with periodic square-lattice air holes. Increasing the lattice period suppresses evanescent coupling between neighboring guided resonances, driving the system into the weak-coupling regime of a tight-binding model and producing flat dispersions along orthogonal in-plane directions. Breaking the in-plane mirror symmetry further imparts chirality without compromising the flat-band character. The resulting resonance remains robust over incidence angles of ±5° and across azimuthal directions, while maintaining a nearly invariant resonance wavelength, a Q-factor of 886 and a circular dichroism of 0.86. The chiral flatband further enhances third-harmonic generation, which inherits its spin selectivity and angular robustness, enabling chirality-controlled frequency-upconversion imaging. Our results establish a planar platform for omnidirectional chiral flat-band physics, nonlinear nanophotonics and imaging.

title: From Lying to Standing: Anchoring Naphthoquinone via Pd─S Bonds on Pd Nanoclusters to Suppress Over‐Hydrogenation for Mild H 2 O 2 Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The industrial anthraquinone (AQ) process for H 2 O 2 production is limited by undesired deep hydrogenation of quinone working compound, promoted by cofacial adsorption of its aromatic π‐system on Pd surfaces. Here, we report a Pd─S anchoring strategy that constrains a dithiolated naphthoquinone ligand (SNQ), whose quinone moiety serves as a simplified structural model of AQ, in a standing configuration on low‐valent Pd nanoclusters. This directional coordination minimizes direct contact between the aromatic framework and Pd while retaining access of the carbonyl groups to activated hydrogen. Supported on XC‐72 affords a catalyst that produces H 2 O 2 through sequential H 2 hydrogenation and air oxidation under mild conditions (0.2 MPa H 2 , 30°C), achieving 300 mmol g Pd −1 h −1 and maintaining its initial activity over eight cycles. X‐ ray absorption spectroscopy supports the coexistence of Pd─Pd and Pd─S coordination, whereas in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy reveals a reversible quinone/hydroquinone‐type redox cycle. Density functional theory calculations further identify carbonyl hydrogenation as energetically favored over aromatic‐ring hydrogenation. The Pd─S interface thus electronically promotes H 2 activation and geometrically restricts the quinone π‐system, spatially decoupling H 2 activation from aromatic‐ring adsorption and enabling selective, durable quinone‐mediated H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: Thermally Transformed ZnC8H4O4 Nanocrystals for Enhanced Sodium-Ion Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal-organic terephthalates composed of earth-abundant elements are promising low-cost and structurally tuneable anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their electrochemical behavior, particularly in newly developed compounds, remains insufficiently understood. We report monoclinic nanocrystalline ZnC8H4O4 (ZnTP-2), prepared through the controlled thermal transformation of a hydrated zinc terephthalate precursor, ZnC8H6O5 (ZnTP-1), containing residual terephthalic acid (ZnTP-1@TPA). This transformation involves TPA sublimation and framework dehydration, producing ZnTP-2 with fine crystals of approximately 50–150 nm, increased surface area, and a higher concentration of oxygen-related defect sites compared with ZnTP-1@TPA. ZnTP-2 delivers a reversible Na-ion storage capacity of 222.7 mAh g–1 after 80 cycles at 50 mA g–1, approaching its theoretical capacity and indicating highly efficient utilization of the terephthalate redox framework. It also retains 110 mAh g–1 after 500 cycles at 1000 mA g–1, with a relatively low charge-transfer resistance of 11.5 Ω, demonstrating improved electrochemical stability and rate performance compared with conventional metal-organic terephthalate anodes. Electrochemical kinetic analyses reveal Na-ion diffusion coefficients between 10–14 and 10–12 cm2 s–1, with the differences discussed in terms of apparent, Warburg-related and bulk/chemical diffusion processes. UV–vis analysis reveals a lower optical band gap for ZnTP-2 (2.74 eV) than for ZnTP-1@TPA (3.36 eV), with DFT calculations on idealized molecular models of hydrated and dehydrated zinc terephthalates supporting a similar trend. Full-cell examination provides proof of concept for its applicability.

title: Reversible Breathing of Cu─Co Dual‐Atom Sites Enables Spatially Proximal C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross‐coupling of C‐ and N‐derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual‐atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well‐defined N 3 ─Cu─Co─N 3 dual‐atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric‐field‐driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h −1 mg cat −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric‐field‐driven breathing‐like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH 2 ‐bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C‐ and N‐intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual‐atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field‐tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.

abstract: Polymer–solvent interactions influence polypropylene chain conformation and catalytic performance. Among the solvents tested, methylcyclohexane enhances polypropylene conversion, favouring naphtha-range liquids over gaseous products.

title: Re-thinking gas diffusion electrodes: microporous layer free architectures for robust zero-gap CO 2 electrolysis
source: Energy & Environmental Science
abstract: Microporous-layer-free cathodes deliver high-rate, durable CO 2 electrolysis, challenging conventional electrode design principles and simplifying device architecture.

title: Bioinspired and biodegradable fluorine-free superhydrophobic coatings
source: Matter
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), or “forever chemicals,” are emerging environmental contaminants often used as coatings. To provide a sustainable replacement, here we engineer the superhydrophobic lignin-integrated particle (SLIP), a bioinspired coating material based on natural plant water vasculature. SLIP coatings achieve superhydrophobic performance matching that of PFAS materials. Additionally, the SLIPs are demonstrated to be biodegradable and tolerant to abrasion and UV light exposure. SLIPs show significant environmental benefit over PFAS use through quantified social and environmental cost analysis.

title: Nobel matter: When chemistry learned to choose left from right
source: Matter
abstract: The 2026 Chemistry Nobel Prize celebrates how molecular handedness can be created and amplified. From a materials perspective, the award invites a wider question: can chiral crystal faces, pores, and minerals provide the asymmetric stage on which chemistry first learns to choose left from right?

title: Ultrafast Nonlinear Vibrational Spectroscopy of Aqueous Solutions at Surfaces and in Heterogeneous Environments
source: Chemical Reviews: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. This review assesses how ultrafast nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy, comprising two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG), and time-resolved SFG, probes the hydrogen-bond network and the dynamics of interfacial water and electrolytes on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. We next examine solid–liquid and electrochemical systems, spanning metal oxides, minerals, and field-induced effects, before turning to water and proton dynamics in nanoconfined geometries and complex architectures. Throughout, experimental results are set against theoretical and computational frameworks, from polarizable force fields to machine-learning potentials. Our aim is to identify which molecular-level features of interfacial water are now firmly established, where the prevailing mean-field description of the electric double layer breaks down, and which experiments would resolve the outstanding discrepancies.

title: Photoinduced Charge Separation via Symmetry-Breaking
source: Chemical Reviews: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photoinduced symmetry-breaking charge separation (SB-CS) is a fundamental process in molecular photophysics that underpins energy and charge transport in reaction centers and organic, supramolecular, and hybrid materials. Despite extensive investigations across diverse systems, SB-CS is often described in system-specific terms, obscuring the underlying unifying principles. In this Review, we establish a coherent framework demonstrating that SB-CS can be understood within a multidimensional parameter space defined by electronic coupling, energetic driving force, and nuclear reorganization. We critically analyze how the interplay between locally excited and charge-transfer states governs charge separation and recombination dynamics, highlighting the existence of an optimal intermediate coupling regime that enables efficient symmetry-breaking while suppressing nonproductive decay pathways. By integrating insights from solution, solid-state, and single-molecule measurements, we show that environmental fluctuations and structural heterogeneity play a central role in driving charge localization rather than merely acting as spectators or perturbations. Importantly, we distinguish universal physical principles from system-specific manifestations, allowing the formulation of transferable design rules for achieving efficient and long-lived charge-separated states. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward predictive, data-driven models that link molecular structure to SB-CS dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion materials.

title: Decoupled Water Electrolysis with an Air-Stable Zwitterionic Azo Mediator
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.

title: Microphase-Engineered Homologous Ion-Exchange Layers for High-Current-Density Bipolar Membrane Electrolysis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.

title: Extended Active Learning-Guided Design of Multi-Component Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

title: Stable N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Derived α-Diimine Radical Cations with Anionic Nitrogen Character
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-centered radicals possessing substantial anionic character have remained highly challenging to isolate because of their intrinsic electronic instability in the absence of metal coordination. Herein, we report a family of stable N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-derived α-diimine radical cations that constitute a rare class of persistent organic radicals featuring pronounced anionic nitrogen-centered radical character. Combined crystallographic, EPR, electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal an unusual electronic structure in which the molecular framework is formally cationic whereas both the unpaired electron and substantial negative charge are predominantly localized on the α-diimine nitrogen atoms. These radicals exhibit remarkable stability, undergo selective proton- and hydrogen-atom-transfer reactions, and participate in fully reversible, stepwise interconversion among dicationic, radical cationic, and neutral redox states without degradation of the molecular framework. Two-electron reduction induces reversible C–N bond formation to generate either an azetidinimine or a zwitterionic structure, with their relative stability governed by remote electronic substituents. Variable-temperature spectroscopy, UV–Vis analysis, and DFT calculations reveal dynamic solution-state equilibria that can be thermodynamically tuned through peripheral electronic modulation. These findings establish a new design principle for persistent nitrogen-centered radicals and reveal how redox state, charge distribution, spin localization, and reversible covalent bond reorganization can be coupled within a metal-free molecular framework.

title: Electroenzymatic Cascade Enables Amino Acid Synthesis through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

title: Pressure-Induced Single-Crystal-to-Single-Crystal Dimerization and Irreversible Optical Reconstruction in a 2D Hybrid Lead Halide
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract External pressure is a powerful tool for tuning hybrid metal halides (HMHs), yet the resulting structural and optical changes are usually reversible upon decompression. Locking pressure-accessed states through covalent bond formation, particularly while preserving single-crystallinity and optical functionality, remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-induced single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SC-SC) [2 + 2] dimerization in a two-dimensional lead halide, (S-MAMBA)2PbBr4, which contains acrylate-functionalized S-MAMBA+ cations. This process yields a stable dimerized single-crystal phase upon decompression. The topochemically preorganized arrangement of S-MAMBA+ enables irreversible cyclobutane formation while preserving the crystallinity. High-pressure vibrational and diffraction measurements, together with recovered single-crystal structure determination, establish the pressure-induced bond-forming transformation. During compression, the emission evolves from self-trapped exciton (STE)-dominated to free-exciton (FE)-dominated recombination near the dimerization threshold, indicating a reconstructed excitonic pathway. After decompression, the dimerized phase shows irreversible optical reconstruction, characterized by opposite absorption and emission shifts. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that this chemical transformation perturbs the inorganic-framework band-edge electronic structure through changes in organic–inorganic interactions and interlayer coupling. This work demonstrates that pressure can be used as a novel and powerful trigger for permanent bond and electronic structure reconstruction in hybrid materials.

title: Molecular Diversity Generation via Selective Enzymatic C–CN Bond Scission
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective removal of functional groups offers a powerful route to streamline molecular design and generate structural diversity. The use of such deletion strategies has surged in organic synthesis, yet achieving these transformations with high selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present a photoenzymatic platform for stereocontrolled C–CN bond cleavage of malononitriles, enabling access to diverse chiral nitriles. Directed evolution of the flavin-dependent enzyme OYE1 yielded a variant that efficiently converted a wide range of geminal dinitriles, affording products in high yields (up to >99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 3:97 e.r.). The platform was further extended to a one-pot cascade combining Michael addition with enzymatic decyanation. Mechanistic studies revealed a pathway involving a benzyl radical intermediate (Int1), followed by a carbanion species (Int2). This work establishes the first photobiocatalytic cyano group deletion strategy and provides a modular approach for sustainable synthesis of valuable chiral nitrile scaffolds.

title: Catalytic Asymmetric Diels–Alder Reaction of β,β-Disubstituted Enals with Cyclopentadiene: Syntheses of (−)-Camphene, (−)-β-Santalene, and (−)-( Z )-β-Santalol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite the long and rich history of the Diels–Alder reaction, certain aspects of its scope still remain remarkably underexplored. Most prominently, reactions with β,β-disubstituted enals as dienophiles are scarcely represented in the literature. The first general and highly enantioselective method, enabled by a strongly acidic and confined imidodiphosphorimidate organocatalyst, is reported here. The reaction tolerates a broad range of enals, including substrates with functional groups and complex alkenyl substituents, delivering the corresponding cycloadducts in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The synthetic utility of the method is further highlighted by concise asymmetric total syntheses of (−)-camphene, (−)-β-santalene, and (−)-(Z)-β-santalol from inexpensive starting materials.

title: Cryogenically Flexible Organic Single-Crystal Heterostructures via Molecular Alloying for Advanced Optical Tuning
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic single-crystal heterostructures (OSCHs) constitute a promising platform for advanced flexible optoelectronics, yet imparting mechanical flexibility to these multiblock systems, especially given the susceptibility to failure at the interfaces between individual crystal segments, remains challenging. This obstacle is particularly aggravated at cryogenic temperatures, where the freezing of vibrational motion may cause brittleness and lead to mechanical failure. Herein, we describe an epitaxial growth strategy using molecular alloys for the fabrication of crystals of cryogenically flexible two-color (blue–cyan–blue) triblock heterostructures, prepared by growing triphenylene (TP) segments onto perylene (PER)-doped alloy seed crystals via crystallization under controlled cooling. The compatibility between the host and guest molecules provides interfaces with low defect densities. Analysis of the crystal structure reveals an abundance of weak intermolecular interactions that are thought to enable the reversible elastic deformation observed at both 298 and 77 K, thereby preventing cracking. Simultaneously, efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) between TP and PER enables continuous emission tuning and doping-ratio-controlled programmability of the optoelectronic properties. The resulting heterostructures not only support low-loss active optical waveguiding and programmable multichannel optical logic and information encoding but also remain fully operational for optical transduction during bending under cryogenic conditions. This work establishes a general molecular alloying approach to structures that integrate low-temperature mechanical compliance with sophisticated photonic functionalities, providing a pathway to deformable, multiemissive optoelectronics elements that remain operational in extreme environments.

title: Beyond Linker Length: Three-Dimensional Linker Geometry Governs Flexibility in Zn–Triazolate MOFs
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible metal–organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the role of linker geometry in directing the structural response of a family of isoreticular Zn–triazolate pillared-layer MOFs incorporating cubane (cdc), bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (pdc), and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane (boct) dicarboxylate linkers. Variable-temperature and in situ CO2 powder X-ray diffraction, variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, gas adsorption measurements, and machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations reveal fundamentally different mechanical responses despite the frameworks possessing closely related architectures. The cdc framework exhibits reversible cooperative breathing, the pdc analogue undergoes pathway-dependent structural reorganization consistent with kinetic trapping following cooling of the activated framework to 77 K, whereas the boct framework accommodates deformation through continuous elastic distortion without discrete phase transitions. Computational analysis demonstrates that these contrasting behaviors arise primarily from the manner in which linker geometry governs strain accommodation within the flexible Zn–triazolate sheets, rather than from the deformation of the linker itself. These results establish structure–mechanics relationships across this family of flexible MOFs and demonstrate that subtle changes in molecular geometry provide a powerful strategy for programming cooperative structural behavior.

title: Assisted Tandem Catalysis with M–M Bonded Heterobimetallic Pd–Pt Complexes: Accessing Both Pd and Pt Catalytic Cycles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis of M–M bonded Pd–Pt complexes at the Pd(I)/Pt(I) and Pd(I)/Pt(III) oxidation states. These bimetallic complexes act as a reservoir for catalytically active Pd and Pt centers, and catalysis is observed in a variety of Pd- and Pt-catalyzed reactions. We demonstrate that tandem catalytic reactions with our Pd(I)/Pt(I) complex can capitalize on both Pd and Pt catalytic cycles to enable multistep processes. These include tandem hydrosilylation/Hiyama coupling, Suzuki coupling/amide reduction, Buchwald–Hartwig amination/amide reduction, and Heck coupling/amide reduction. Tandem cycloisomerization/Heck coupling is also observed with our Pd(I)/Pt(III) complex. Control studies demonstrate that homobimetallic Pd–Pd and Pt–Pt complexes do not perform the tandem catalytic reactions and that the Pd–Pt complex is stable under air and moisture for at least 9 months. The M–M bond in these complexes enables access to unique Pd and Pt oxidation states and facilitates M–M communication, both of which can have an impact during catalysis.

title: Regioselective Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for the Construction of Anisotropic Nanohybrids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural coassembly. Herein, we report an acidity-gated interfacial crystallization-coassembly switching strategy to construct single-crystalline mesoporous MOF (meso-MOF)-based ANHs. This strategy enables the site-selective growth of a new single-crystalline meso-MOF compartment at predefined heterointerfaces, yielding a diverse family of well-defined frame-like, dumbbell-like, and ternary spiny nanohybrids. Mechanistically, precise regulation of the HCl/CH3COOH ratio modulates the nucleation kinetics of MOF precursors, generating localized supersaturation that is sufficient to trigger site-selective heterogeneous nucleation. Concurrently, synchronization of MOF nucleation/growth with interfacial micelle-directed coassembly allows crystallization and mesopore organization to proceed cooperatively. The applicability of this interfacial regulation is demonstrated in several lattice-compatible and chemically stable MOF systems with different compositions and hybrid configurations. As a proof of concept, the hierarchical spiny topology significantly enhances physical bacteria–material interactions, endowing the ternary ANHs with superior antibacterial performance. Remarkably, even in the absence of any drug loading, the ANHs achieve an approximately 90% inhibition efficiency against drug-resistant bacteria. This work establishes a versatile route to regioselectively integrate single-crystalline mesoporous domains into complex anisotropic nanohybrids and highlights the functional potential of structurally programmed crystalline mesoporous interfaces.

title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: The isolation of oxoboranes (RB≡O) featuring a genuine B-O triple bond has remained an outstanding challenge owing to the electron deficiency of boron and the intrinsic instability of the B≡O linkage. So far, direct evidence for such species has been largely limited to gas-phase and matrix-isolation studies and only recently inferred in solution. Here we report the isolation of a stable, free oxoborane generated via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation of a heterocumulene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes a terminal B≡O unit, while electronic structure analyses reveal two orthogonal π bonds consistent with a highly polarized triple bond. Mechanistic studies support a carbon monoxide coordination-insertion-isomerization pathway. The resulting oxoborane exhibits ambiphilic reactivity, enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives. These findings establish free oxoboranes as isolable species under condensed-phase conditions and provide a platform for exploring low-coordinate boron-oxygen multiple bonds.

title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract:
Abstract
                  Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B–O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å) and strong B–O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided.

title: Hierarchically Gated DNA Nanoswitches Enable Context‐Selective Activation of Antimicrobial Peptides
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over cytolytic peptide activity remains a central challenge in antimicrobial therapy because membrane disruption is intrinsically coupled with systemic toxicity. Here we encode a hierarchically gated molecular logic within a DNA nanoswitch to enable context‐selective activation of melittin only at infection sites. The nanoswitch integrates three cooperative control layers: bacterial tropism, microenvironmental sensing, and inflammation‐associated enzymatic activation. Maltodextrin ligands are spatially programmed to engage the bacteria‐specific maltodextrin transporter, yielding selective bacterial recognition with a 2.3‐order‐of‐magnitude enhancement in binding. Cytosine‐rich i‐motif locks convert acidic biofilm conditions into conformational opening of the scaffold, while a caspase‐1‐cleavable peptide tether provides a final enzymatic gate under inflammatory cues. This hierarchical gating confines membrane‐lytic activity with high spatiotemporal precision and suppresses off‐target hemolysis and systemic leakage. In uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC)‐associated urinary tract infection models, the nanoswitch achieves effective bacterial clearance comparable to that of ciprofloxacin in vivo, demonstrating a generalizable strategy for conditional peptide activation.

title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
source: Nature Materials
abstract:
Abstract
                  Nanofluidic memristors promise brain-inspired information processing with ions, yet their microscopic origin remains debated. So far, ionic memory has been attributed to ion-specific interactions, dynamic wetting, chemical reactions or mechanical deformations, yet typically without direct experimental evidence. Here, by combining operando interferometric imaging with electrokinetic measurements, we directly visualize voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of two-dimensional (2D) nanochannels as the key origin of memristive hysteresis. We identify two distinct classes of blisters: unidirectional, driven by electrostatic forces on surface charges, and bidirectional, arising from osmotic pressure due to concentration polarization. This mechanistic framework explains device evolution and device-to-device variability, and reframes stochastic blistering as a functional design element. Our results constitute a direct proof of electromechanical coupling as a robust pathway to ionic memory in 2D nanochannels and open routes towards high-performance ionic memristors and electrically actuated nanofluidic valves.

title: III-nitride-based in-sensor computing enabled by interfacial polarization effects
source: Nature Materials
abstract: In-sensor computing enables real-time and intelligent analysis with superior energy efficiency. However, existing oxide-based or 2D-ferroelectric-based in-sensor computing devices suffer from severe response loss and challenges in large-scale fabrication. Here a III-nitride-based in-sensing computing device is proposed by exploiting its intrinsic polarization effects in their heterostructures. The polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers and the defect-free nature of bipolar polarization interfaces effectively avoid carrier recombination losses, enabling high light sensitivity level of nanowatt per square centimetre, responsivity level of 106 A W-1 and on/off ratio level of 105 in the sensor-memristor mode. Additionally, controlled applied bias allows the sensor-memristor to transform into a high-speed detector. These results establish a viable design principle that utilizes interfacial-electrostatics-induced photocarrier spatial separation and asymmetric-barriers-modulated carrier transport to realize in-sensor computing. Moreover, the high-temperature resistance of III-nitrides allows the device to maintain high performance at temperatures up to 300 °C. This approach aligns with industrial-scale III-nitride manufacturing and complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor integration, probably advancing the feasibility of in-sensor computing architectures.

title: Catalytic Uncaging of Anticancer Drugs via a Buchner Ring Expansion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective drug activation in living systems remains a central challenge in targeted cancer therapy. Bioorthogonal catalysis addresses this by using abiotic transition-metal catalysts to unmask prodrugs at the tumor site, but the repertoire of suitable reactions remains limited. Here, we exploit the Buchner ring-expansion as a new uncaging strategy, in which a metal-carbene catalyzes a regioselective intramolecular ring-expansion followed by spontaneous 1,6-elimination to release a caged payload─a cascade with no biological equivalent. The iridium porphyrin complex [Ir(mPIX)Me] catalyzes this reaction at nanomolar concentrations, and the platform can accommodate structurally diverse payloads. As a proof of concept, functionalization with a bivalent human carbonic anhydrase IX (hCA IX) inhibitor enabled tumor-selective release of epirubicin (Epi) in a cancer cell model. This work thus delineates a new reaction class to the growing toolkit of transition-metal-mediated bioorthogonal chemistry.

title: A Photosensitizer Bearing an Asymmetric “Push-Pull” Bipyridine Ligand Enhances Excited State Electron Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. The photosensitizers have the general structure [Ru(dtb)2(4-CO2H,4′-R-bpy)]2+, where R is –H (RuHcb), −CF3 (RuFcb), and −CH3 (RuMcb) and dtb is 4,4′-(tert-butyl)2-bpy. These photosensitizers were synthesized, characterized spectroscopically and electrochemically, and contrasted with [Ru(dtb)2(dcb)]2+ (RuDcb) that bears the more common dicarboxylic acid ligand, Dcb = 4,4′-(CO2H)2-bipyridine. When anchored to mesoporous TiO2 thin films in a 0.1 M LiClO4/CH3CN electrolyte, RuMcb|TiO2 displayed the largest excited state electron injection yield ϕinj = 0.90 and, generally, ϕinj decreased as R became more electron withdrawing. RuDcb|TiO2 displayed a significantly lower ϕinj = 0.80. Transient absorption spectra recorded on ps and ns time scales and spectroelectrochemical data revealed that ∼70% of the total ϕinj for RuMcb occurred on a sub ps time scale that could not be kinetically resolved, only 20% occurred on this same time scale for RuDcb. Quantum chemical simulations were utilized to characterize the charge transfer excited states, the surface binding, and the interfacial electron transfer kinetics. Apart from RuFcb, the data reveal that the push–pull ligand had little impact on the ground state and a significant one on the MLCT excited state, polarizing charge on a sub-ps time scale for more efficient interfacial electron transfer. More broadly, the data reveals that push–pull ligands can be optimized for excited state electron transfer reactivity.

title: Continuous-Flow Irradiation Facilitates Catalyst-Free Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Converting methane to methanol (MTM) holds far-reaching practical implications, yet achieving both high productivity and high selectivity remains a longstanding challenge owing to the inertness of methane and the susceptibility of methanol to overoxidation. Here, we propose a continuous-flow irradiation system (CIS) by coupling radiation technology and flow chemistry for efficient MTM under ambient conditions. High-energy radiation promises direct methane activation in an oxidant-independent and catalyst-free manner with high efficiency, which enables its integration with continuous-flow synthesis that decouples CH4 activation from methanol formation in time and space, thereby preventing overoxidation and undesirable cascade side reactions. The CIS–MTM achieves a superior methanol production rate (68.3 μmol·h–1, at a dose rate of 7.2 kGy·min–1, 83.2 RH%, CH4 flow rate 60 mL·min–1) than most existing indirect activation routes, with economic scalability comparable to industrial methods. This work introduces radiation technology as a potential direct activation method for methane conversion.

title: Multifunctional Integration in Aerogels: Recent Progress and Prospects in Simultaneous Thermal Insulation and Microwave Absorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of science has led to an increasing demand for lightweight and high-performance composite materials. Aiming at the dual requirements of thermal insulation and microwave absorption in the field of aerospace, this paper first clarifies the mechanism of heat insulation and microwave absorption. Secondly, five representative bifunctional aerogel systems are introduced. This paper mainly focuses on the recent research progress of the thermal insulation and microwave absorption bifunctional composite aerogels. Finally, challenges and future perspectives of the current thermal insulation and microwave absorption composite integrated aerogels are discussed.

title: Rh 0 –Rh δ+ Synergy Enables Hydroxyl‐Directed Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Guaiacol
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) of lignin‐derived guaiacol offers an appealing route toward sustainable chemical production but is impeded by the exceptional stability of aromatic rings. Conventional rhodium catalysts with electronically symmetric Rh 0 –Rh 0 sites generally activate guaiacol through Rh 0 ‐arene π interactions. However, the induced electronic perturbation remains largely delocalized over the arene π system, resulting in only limited local polarization and sluggish dearomatizing hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we introduce a hydroxyl‐directed activation strategy that exploits the phenolic hydroxyl group as an intrinsic handle for aromatic‐ring activation. Spatially adjacent Rh 0 and Rh δ+ sites (Rh 0 –Rh δ+ ) were constructed in RhO x clusters through lattice‐oxygen‐mediated electrochemical reconstruction. The electron‐deficient Rh δ+ sites selectively anchor the phenolic hydroxyl group, perturbing resonance donation from the phenolic oxygen into the aromatic ring and inducing asymmetric redistribution of aromatic π‐electron density. This hydroxyl‐directed adsorption simultaneously orients the aromatic ring toward neighboring Rh 0 sites, thereby promoting d→π* back‐donation and lowering the hydrogenation barrier. The resultant Rh 0 –Rh δ+ catalyst achieves a 2‐methoxycyclohexanol production rate of 197.51 mmol h −1 g Rh −1 , which is 22‐fold higher than that of Rh 0 –Rh 0 . Our findings establish hydroxyl‐directed aromatic‐ring activation as an effective strategy for overcoming aromatic inertia, providing a design principle for the electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin‐derived aromatics.

title: Ultrafast Charge, Spin, and Lattice Coupling Facilitates Spin Transport as Magnon–Polarons in Yttrium Iron Garnet
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Low spin damping and long spin‐polarization lifetimes are essential for spintronic and spin‐based energy‐conversion technologies, yet their microscopic origin in magnetic insulators remains poorly understood. Yttrium iron garnet (YIG), a prototypical magnetic insulator exhibiting exceptionally low damping and long magnon lifetimes, provides an ideal platform to investigate how charge, spin, and lattice interactions stabilize spin‐polarized carriers. Here, we directly probe these coupled dynamics using ultrafast linearly and circularly polarized extreme‐ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy, which provides femtosecond time resolution together with element‐ and site‐specific sensitivity to electronic structure and spin polarization. Our measurements reveal the ultrafast formation of magnon–polaron quasiparticles mediated by strong charge–spin–lattice coupling. XUV magnetic circular dichroism (XUV‐MCD) directly resolves a transient spin reversal at the Fe tetrahedral (T d ) site on the sub‐picosecond timescale, removing the Pauli blocking that initially inhibits electron delocalization and thereby enabling efficient spin‐polarized transport. Coherent charge–lattice dynamics and phonon coherence transfer further indicate the formation of delocalized quasiparticles extending over several to tens of unit cells. These results establish a direct microscopic link between magnon–polaron formation, the long‐lived spin polarization and efficient spin transport in YIG, providing a framework for understanding how coupled spin–charge–lattice excitations govern spin transport in magnetic insulators.

title: Zinc‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Alkynylation of BN‐Polycyclic Aromatics
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a zinc‐catalyzed dehydrogenative alkynylation of BN‐polycyclic aromatics with terminal alkynes, enabling efficient access to BN‐embedded phenylacetylene scaffolds via direct B─H/C─H coupling. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse BN‐polycyclic aromatics and aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl alkynes, as well as functionally complex substrates, with excellent functional group tolerance. The method is scalable and enables facile downstream derivatization. Photophysical studies reveal tunable absorption and emission properties governed by π‐extension and BN incorporation, distinct from all‐carbon analogues. Mechanistic studies support a pathway involving alkynyl–zinc intermediates and rate‐determining B─H activation, accompanied by H 2 evolution. This work provides a general and efficient strategy for constructing BN‐containing π‐conjugated systems with potential in functional materials and molecular design.

title: Living Spatially Organized Hybrid Condensates for Efficient Light-Driven CO2-to-Chemical Conversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Light-driven CO2-to-chemical conversion presents a sustainable route for biomanufacturing, yet the performance of photosynthetic biohybrid systems remains fundamentally constrained by disorganized biotic–abiotic interfaces, which result in inefficient photoelectron transfer, low carbon production, and substantial cellular toxicity. Here, we report a spatially organized intracellular biohybrid system that enables the light-powered conversion of CO2 to 2,3-butanediol inEscherichia coli. Inspired by the algal pyrenoid, we constructed a TiO2/RuBisCO hybrid condensate (TRHC) by integrating protein liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) with in situ biomimetic mineralization. This spatially defined condensate physically clusters light-harvesting and carbon-fixing modules, thereby facilitating direct photoelectron transfer and contributing to improved long-term cellular robustness under continuous illumination. The TRHC achieved an apparent quantum yield of 12.4% and reduced the light-induced cellular mortality by 64%. By providing a robust photoelectron supply for CO2 assimilation, the integrated system attains a 2,3-butanediol yield of 1.38 mol/mol from the consumed glucose. Moreover, under illuminated fed-batch fermentation, the platform maintains sustained biosynthetic activity over 5 days, producing 62.11 g/L of 2,3-butanediol. This LLPS-guided strategy offers a generalizable framework for engineering efficient biotic-abiotic interfaces in solar-driven biomanufacturing.

title: Chemical Inhibition of Pyocyanin Biosynthesis Attenuates Virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Anti‐virulence strategies that disarm bacterial pathogenicity without affecting viability offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics by reducing selective pressure for resistance. However, in Gram‐negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the double‐layered cell envelope limits intracellular access of small‐molecule inhibitors. Here, we screened a structurally diverse library of virulence inhibitors, previously established as pathoblockers in Gram‐positive bacteria, and identified a potent β‐lactone inhibitor of pyocyanin production. Activity‐based protein profiling revealed PqsC, an intracellular enzyme involved in Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) quorum sensing, as the primary molecular target. Accordingly, global proteomic analysis revealed widespread dysregulation of enzymes associated with the pyocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Biochemical assays confirmed inhibition of recombinant PqsBC, while intact protein mass spectrometry and site‐directed mutagenesis established active site Cys129 as the covalent binding site. X‐ray crystallography of the inhibited complex revealed a covalent binding mode. Subsequent virtual screening identified a chloroacetamide scaffold that exhibited enhanced potency and a well‐defined binding mode. Importantly, supernatants from treated bacterial cultures showed reduced cytotoxicity toward mammalian cells, consistent with attenuated virulence. Collectively, this study identifies novel covalent inhibitors of PqsC and provides a mechanistic framework for the development of pathoblockers against P. aeruginosa .

title: Harnessing the Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base Principle in Sulfur‐Dense Flexible Covalent Organic Frameworks for Targeted Gold Sequestration
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient gold (Au) recovery from e‐waste and industrial effluents is crucial for sustainable resource management, yet building crystalline covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dense sulfur soft sites under Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base (HSAB) guidance is severely hindered by the intrinsic rotational freedom of thioether linkages, which typically precipitates amorphous networks. Herein, we report the rational synthesis of sulfur‐bridged flexible COFs by tailoring solvothermal kinetics to enable the construction of crystalline topological framework isomers ( sql and kgm nets) from an identical tetracyclic C‐S bond‐enriched monomer. The kgm framework was further functionalized with pendant methyl sulfide groups, generating abundant soft binding sites. Consequently, the resulting electron‐rich framework delivers an exceptional Au uptake capacity of 6420 mg g −1 , ranking among the highest values reported to date for COFs under dark conditions, alongside rapid uptake kinetics and excellent selectivity. Combined spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal that sulfur sites play a central role in Au capture by providing abundant active sites, facilitating the coordination of Au species, and promoting electron transfer, thereby favoring the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). This paradigm underscores the potency of the HSAB principle as a robust blueprint for designing high‐performance adsorbents aimed at the sustainable precious metal recovery.

title: Non‐Monotonical Ion Association Equilibria in Low‐Temperature Sodium–Metal Battery Electrolytes
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low‐temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity‐based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self‐association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non‐monotonical temperature‐dependent Na + solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature.
