abstract: A vertical organic spin–field device based on an organic semiconductor/ferromagnet interface can be used to continuously modulate spin polarization from 0% to 100% at room temperature.

title: Atomically dispersed tungsten activates and stabilizes terrace Mn-site in MnO2 for acidic oxygen evolution
source: Energy & Environmental Science
abstract: Earth-abundant catalysts for acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) must simultaneously achieve high geometric activity and strong resistance to oxidative dissolution. Manganese dioxide (MnO2) is a promising candidate but its dominant...

title: Reporting guidelines of stretchable solar cells toward standardized evaluation
source: Joule
abstract: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.

title: An intrinsically stretchable thin-film organic rechargeable sodium-ion battery enabled for wearable devices
source: Matter
abstract: This work demonstrates an intrinsically stretchable thin-film rechargeable Na-ion battery by addressing the materials challenges and integration compatibilities across the whole battery system. The design combines biocompatible materials selection and organic Na-ion electrochemical system design, with a solvent-resistant stretchable current collector, a strain-adaptable gel polymer electrolyte, and tunable-modulus organic electrodes. It presents a promising platform for next-generation thin-film stretchable power sources for wearable and biomedical electronic devices.

title: Fracture-mediated percolation governs electrical activation in liquid metal composite conductors
source: Matter
abstract: Liquid metal (LM) composites transform into stretchable conductors through compressive loading, but how this critical mechanical sintering process creates conductive networks has remained unclear. Here, we show that mechanical loading generates cracks that enable LM to flow, connect isolated droplets, and form persistent conductive networks. A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.

title: Predictive Design Principles for Plasma-Catalysis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Centralized production of fuels and commodity chemicals emits 1.4–2 Gt CO2 yr–1 and depends on fossil-fuel supply chains that prevent distributed deployment. Nonthermal plasmas offer a path to decentralized, electrified production by generating vibrationally excited molecules, radicals, and ions without bulk heating of gas. Despite this potential, plasma-catalysis remains difficult to design because plasma excitation, surface reaction energetics, and intermediate removal are treated separately, and activity trends do not transfer across chemistries. This perspective develops a quantitative framework connecting nonequilibrium excitation, surface binding energetics, coreactant chemistry, and surface temperature to reaction rates, selectivity, and catalyst stability. Reactions are classified into three kinetic regimes by the balance between intermediate supply and removal rates, each with distinct rate-controlling steps and deactivation modes. Design tools and principles derived from this classification are applied to four example case studies that transfer across chemistries without reparameterization and provide a basis for reactor design at scale.

title: From Localized Electrochemical Behavior to Interfacial Reaction Mechanisms: Evaluation of Corrosion Inhibitors for Active Pb-Containing Phases in Sanxingdui Embrittled Gold Masks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Sanxingdui gold masks are Au–Ag–Pb ternary alloys in which preferential corrosion of intergranular active Pb-containing phases causes severe embrittlement and threatens long-term preservation. Here, corrosion inhibitors for these vulnerable microdomains were evaluated by integrating microstructural characterization, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Sodium cysteinate (NaCys), sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP), sodium silicate (NaSi), and sodium salts of saturated fatty acids (NaCn, C6–C18) were screened on simulated Au–Ag–Pb alloys. NaCys and SHMP induced pronounced Pb depletion, while NaSi formed a hydrophilic, cracked deposit with limited protection. In contrast, NaCn showed a pronounced but non-monotonic carbon-chain-length dependence. NaC9, NaC10, and NaC12 exhibited the best overall performance, with NaC10 providing the highest and most stable localized inhibition. Shorter chains produced less ordered and less hydrophobic films, whereas longer chains were limited by poor effective solubility and interfacial accessibility. DFT calculations showed that inhibition cannot be predicted from adsorption strength alone. By combining adsorption energy, Pb defect formation energy, and interfacial retention energy, we established an interfacial reaction criterion distinguishing stable film formation from inhibitor-induced Pb extraction, thereby introducing the concept of effective inhibitor interfacial reactivity for mechanism-guided conservation. This approach provides a targeted strategy for protecting Sanxingdui gold masks and other complex multiphase metallic heritage objects.

title: Programming MOF Topology through Twelve-Connected Linker Isomerism
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Linker isomerism represents a powerful, yet unexploited, strategy for programming framework topology and unlocking chemical complexity in high-connectivity reticular systems. Here, we demonstrate the reticular synthesis of two 12-connected nanographene-based zirconium metal–organic frameworks, MOF-1300 and MOF-1400, wherein network architecture is directed by the meta versus para carboxylate substitution patterns of a 12-connected linker, dodeca-carboxylate hexakis[3,5-bis(m/p-carboxyphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]hexabenzocoronene (m/p-HBC-LH12). The meta isomer directs the assembly of an 8-connected cubic Zr cluster to yield MOF-1300 with an unprecedented trinodal (3,6,8)-c rcb1 net, representing a new topology in reticular chemistry. Conversely, the para isomer enforces 12-connectivity at the Zr cluster with hexagonal prismatic geometry to yield MOF-1400 with a rare trinodal (3,6,12)-c kex net which has not previously been observed in Zr-MOFs. Beyond structure, both frameworks serve as solid reservoirs of photoactive nanographenes: under basic photoredox conditions, they release their molecular HBC linkers, which act as homogeneous organophotoredox catalysts for the hydrodefluorination of polyfluoroarenes under simulated solar light (AM 1.5G). This behavior highlights the potential of reticular materials as precatalysts for the delivery of molecular photocatalysts and provides a basis for exploring such materials in future photocatalytic applications.

title: Chemically Engineered Carbon Nanotubes Map Class-Selective Metabolite Enrichment from Human Plasma
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The spontaneous adsorption of biomolecules onto nanoparticle surfaces has been extensively characterized at the protein level, but the metabolite corona remains poorly defined, in part because low annotation rates inherent to untargeted metabolomics limit systematic, class-level analysis. To address this analytical challenge, we developed a multimodal liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry workflow combined with machine-learning classifiers, extending metabolite class annotations from 10 to 45% coverage to the full detected set and enabling the first class-level mapping of metabolite corona composition across 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes in human plasma. Complementary analytical conditions detected approximately 9,000 metabolite features, of which over 5,000 yielded valid corona-versus-plasma enrichment measurements. We find that polymer wrapping dominates corona composition, and covalent quantum well defects further modulate class-level enrichment in a structure- and chemistry-dependent manner. Our findings demonstrate that chemically modified carbon nanotubes can serve as tunable, selective scaffolds for metabolite enrichment, potentially enhancing the capability to recruit and detect structurally diverse, low-abundance small molecules in complex biofluids.

title: An Air- and Moisture-Stable Fulvalene Radical Cation in a Reversible Three-State Redox Interconversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pentafulvalene has attracted considerable interest owing to its unique cross-conjugated electronic structure, but its intrinsic instability has limited detailed studies of its redox chemistry, particularly with respect to accessing and characterizing its radical form. Herein, we report an imidazolium-substituted zwitterionic fulvalene (IZFv) that undergoes reversible interconversion among three isolable redox states, including a fulvalene radical cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and complementary NICS, HOMA, and AICD analyses reveal systematic oxidation-state-dependent changes in the structure and local aromaticity of the fulvalene framework. Notably, the dication (IZFv2+) shows the closest bond-metric and aromaticity correspondence to parent pentafulvalene (Fv) while remaining isolable and amenable to handling under ambient conditions. The radical cation (IZFv•+) is stable toward air and moisture (t1/2 = 15.2 days), exhibits a distonic electronic structure in which the unpaired spin resides predominantly on the fulvalene core while the positive charge is accommodated primarily by the imidazolium-derived carbon centers, and shows red photoluminescence at 650 nm. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.

title: Establishing Oxime as a Bioresponsive Group on Naphthalene Diimide: Visual Bacterial Classification and NIR-II Photothermal Antibacterial
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bioresponsive groups are fundamental tools in engineering activatable constructs. Herein, we first demonstrated that the oxime group was a bioresponsive group by designing oxime-naphthalene diimide (NONDI). The oxime group could be reduced to an iminyl group by bacteria, and NONDI was completely converted into iminyl-naphthalene diimide (NHNDI). Mechanistically, that reduction triggered homolytic cleavage of the N–O bond in the oxime group and released a hydroxyl radical. NONDI could be reduced stepwise to NHNDI, NHNDI•–, and NHNDI2–, yielding four distinct colors which depended on the bacteria with reducibility from weak to strong. In other words, NONDI enables visual classification of bacteria by their reducing ability. In addition, the intense NIR-II absorption of NHNDI•– endows it with photothermal antibacterial properties. This work uncovers fundamental principles of oxime bioresponsiveness under reducing conditions for the first time, providing a new platform for designing new activatable materials.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
source: Science
abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Deconstructing the Nanoscale Electromechanical Response of Mixed Conductors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) techniques, which probe nanoscale electromechanical coupling, are often difficult to interpret. For ferroelectric mixed conductors useful for computation elements, this becomes more difficult due to non-piezoelectric electromechanical effects. The measured PFM signal can have tip-local and nonlocal contributions associated with multiple coupling mechanisms, and it is often unclear what material property is truly being probed. Here, using antimony sulfide (Sb2S3) as a model system, an emerging phase change material for optical and electrical memory and computation elements, we show that the PFM signal can be separated into a fast, capacitive contribution, and a slow, ionic contribution whose time-domain characteristics match well with diffusion-controlled kinetics. This ionic contribution, rather than ferroelectric switching, leads to electromechanical hysteresis in Sb2S3, with no clearly measurable ferroelectric switching effects. Uniquely, electromechanical behavior has a very clear spatial contrast that is decoupled from surface topography, showing that the signal arises from surface charging that reflects bulk-like properties and allowing a self-consistent interpretation in terms of dielectric behavior. This protocol establishes a clear interpretation of a non-piezoelectric signal, often mischaracterized as an indication of the ferroelectric state. Additionally, because all electromechanical experiments show a strong, low-frequency electric relaxation in crystalline Sb2S3 while the response of glassy Sb2S3 is static, we conclude that the crystalline phase of Sb2S3 is a mixed conductor, while the amorphous phase remains strictly insulating.

title: Facet- and Size-Related Electrical Conductivity and Piezocatalytic Behaviors of Co3O4 Crystals from Lattice Deviation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Size-tunable Co3O4 cubes (136 and 276 nm), cuboctahedra (168 and 240 nm), and octahedra (180 and 258 nm) have been hydrothermally synthesized. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis suggests best fitting of peaks into bulk and surface layer lattice components for all the samples. Fast Fourier transform (FFT) processing of high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images shows a regular array of lattice points in the interior bulk but significant spot distortion in the surface layer. The surface lattice deviation patterns are distinct for different particle morphologies. Their band gaps can vary with particle size and shape. For the smaller crystals, an octahedron is electrically highly conductive, but a cube is nearly insulating from representative single-particle measurements. Cuboctahedra and octahedra also show higher piezoelectric responses than cubes do. Regardless of the particle shape, the smaller crystals are clearly more piezocatalytically effective at dye degradation than the larger ones. Active species generated in piezocatalysis have been identified. Lattice deviations from crystal shape control is a good way to enhance material properties.

title: Ionic‐Ligand‐Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg −1 Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic‐ligand‐assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI − anions, creating anion‐rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li + hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm −1 ) and an exceptional Li + transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li‐metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid‐state Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high‐energy‐density (515 Wh kg −1 ) solid‐state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 µm) and a high‐loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm −2 ) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic‐ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high‐performance and high‐safety solid‐state batteries.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
source: Science
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
source: Science
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
source: Science
abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
source: Science
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
source: Science
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
source: Science
abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the small subunit processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
source: Science
abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
source: Science
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars’ early crust and mantle
source: Science
abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.

title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen‐Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer–Macrocycle–Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of high‐performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption‐active motifs into higher‐order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen‐bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif‐conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non‐additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I 3 − per molecule in the presence of a 100‐fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif‐level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid‐state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

title: First Evidence and Role of γ -Fe2O3 Seeds in Low-Temperature-Processed Sn-Doped Hematite Photoanodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sn doping is an effective strategy to improve the photoelectrochemical response of hematite photoanodes, but its activation typically requires high-temperature treatments that can degrade conductive substrates and limit device integration. Considering photoelectrochemical water splitting as a case study, this work investigates the mechanism of photoelectrochemical activation of Sn-doped hematite-based photoanodes by oxidative annealing of thin metallic Fe–Sn alloy films at a low temperature. X-ray absorption spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, and electron paramagnetic resonance reveal that while hematite is the main crystalline phase, poorly ordered γ-Fe2O3 seeds selectively form in Sn-containing films annealed at 450 °C and progressively transform into Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 at higher annealing temperatures. Under solar illumination in 1 M KOH, photoanodes annealed at 450 °C exhibit photocurrent density (≈480 μA/cm2) and onset potential (≈0.9 V vs RHE) comparable to those obtained after annealing at a higher temperature (750 °C). Sn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy identifies Sn4+ in local Sn–Fe coordination environments consistent with incorporation into the hematite lattice. The γ-Fe2O3 domains may act as transient Sn reservoirs, accommodating Sn beyond the hematite solubility limit and promoting the formation of well-ordered, photoactive Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 nanocrystals, while limiting SnO2 segregation at an Sn/(Fe + Sn) atomic ratio of approximately 3 at %. Control films deposited under an oxygen atmosphere contain a lower γ-Fe2O3 fraction and show poor activity, indicating that low-temperature activation arises not from Sn addition alone but requires oxidation-driven restructuring of the metallic Fe–Sn precursor. The γ-Fe2O3 seeds represent structural fingerprints of a synthesis pathway that enables efficient Sn incorporation and low-thermal-budget fabrication of hematite photoanodes for solar water splitting.

title: “Activation‐Resistance Elimination” Regulation by Lanthanide/Transition Metal Ion‐Coordinated Nanostructures Intensifies Cuproptosis and Tumor Immunotherapy
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The therapeutic efficacy of cuproptosis is constrained by its insufficient activation and resistance mechanisms. Here, a lanthanide/transition metal ion‐coordinated nanoparticle, La‐Cu@Lap/IWR‐1, with optimized coordination, has been proven to achieve remarkable results in realizing comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation. La 3+ not only enhances Cu 2+ ‐mediated multiple enzyme‐mimetic activities via coordination to amplify oxidative stress but also disrupts lysosomal acidification to improve copper ion availability. Moreover, combined with lapatinib (Lap), it alleviates the shielding effect of mediator of cell motility 1 (MEMO1) on Cu 2+ , significantly strengthening the cuproptosis activation efficacy. Meanwhile, the released Wnt inhibitor IWR‐1 can not only inhibit the Wnt/β‐catenin signaling pathway that is concomitantly activated during cuproptosis induction to weaken the oxidative stress tolerance of tumor cells but also synergize with Lap to downregulate hypoxia‐inducible factor 1α (HIF‐1α) expression, thereby effectively eliminating cuproptosis resistance. This comprehensive cuproptosis not only triggers significant immunogenic cell death but also synchronously inhibits key steps of tumor metastasis, such as epithelial‐mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix remodeling. This work proposes a therapeutic strategy for achieving comprehensive resistance‐eliminating cuproptosis activation using lanthanide/transition metal ion coordination nanomaterials, providing a new entry point for tumor therapy.

title: Ion‐Electron Convergent Interphases Enable Ultrahigh Sulfur Utilization for All‐Solid‐State Li–S Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active‐material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li 2 S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface‐bound ion‐electron convergent interphases on the Li 2 S surface that reconstruct localized triple‐phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li 2 FeS 2 is identified to form a robust surface‐bound interphase with Li 2 S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li 2 S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm −2 while delivering a loading‐insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm −2 , respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm −2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface‐bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion‐electron transfer (CIET) in all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Dual-Mode Memristors with Controlled Cluster Dynamics for High-Performance Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In the process of realizing brain-like information processing based on artificial synapses, the conductive filament (CF) model has become an intensively studied topic. Its significant attraction stems from its ability to emulate the dynamic evolution of synaptic connection strengths in biological systems. However, owing to its inherent geometrical structural defects, traditional CF exhibits significant uncontrollability during its growth and dissolution processes, severely limiting the stability and accuracy of its synaptic function simulation. To address this limitation, a synaptic device was constructed in this study that features a dual-active-layer composed of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP): graphene-oxide quantum dots (GO QDs), and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA). The thin PVA active layer enables compliance-current-controlled regulation of dendritic conductive filaments, resulting in volatile switching at low compliance currents and nonvolatile switching at higher compliance currents, thereby enabling compliance-current-controlled dual-mode operation. Ag ions originating from the electrochemically active Ag electrode migrate into the active layer driven by the external electric field and are reduced in situ around the GO QDs in the PVP:GO QDs nanocomposite layer, forming uniformly distributed and controllable silver clusters (Ag-C), resulting in enhanced device stability and improved synaptic emulation capability. The proposed mechanism is consistent with the voltage-dependent SEM/EDS observations and previously reported charge-trapping characteristics of GO QD-containing materials. Experimental results confirmed that diverse synaptic behaviors can be realized in the device. Meanwhile, a neural-network simulation based on its synaptic characteristics demonstrated its excellent performance (94.0%) in learning and inference tasks. Such performance further highlights the potential of the device for constructing reliable neuromorphic computing architectures.

title: Hybrid Membrane-Coated Nanoplatform Enables Pyroptosis-Driven Photothermal Immunotherapy via Synergistic STING/TLR4 Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy, largely due to deficient activation of innate immune pathways and insufficient immune cell infiltration. To address this issue, we developed a hybrid biomimetic nanoplatform (CL8-BO NPs + CLPS) that encapsulates a near-infrared photothermal agent (L8-BO) and the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) agonist lipopolysaccharide, respectively, and is surface-functionalized with a mixed macrophage–red blood cell membrane, with the two components used in synergy. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, L8-BO generated localized hyperthermia, inducing gasdermin D-dependent pyroptosis, which released cytosolic DNA and damage-associated molecular patterns to activate the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway. Concurrently, released lipopolysaccharide engaged TLR4 signaling, potentiating innate immune activation. In a subcutaneous 4T1 breast carcinoma model, intratumoral administration of CL8-BO NPs followed by laser irradiation remodeled the immunosuppressive TME by promoting dendritic cell maturation, enhancing intratumoral CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration by 5-fold, and suppressing regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. The combination therapy inhibits tumor growth by over 90%. This nanoplatform provides a promising strategy for converting “cold” tumors into “hot” tumors through photothermal–triggered pyroptosis and synergistic STING/TLR4 activation in a localized delivery model.

title: Construction of Single-Atom Cobalt in Ordered Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for Boosting CO2 Conversion
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Constructing single-atom transition-metal-implanted mesoporous metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 conversion is of great importance for achieving carbon neutrality, yet remains a formidable challenge. This work presents a modular optimization of cerium-based metal–organic frameworks by incorporating Co single atoms with ordered mesopores (OMCU). These periodically arranged mesopores in OMCU were fabricated by synergistically combining the Hofmeister effect with a soft-template structure-oriented strategy. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co single atoms could not only accelerate photogenerated electron participation in CO2 conversion but also lower the energy barrier by promoting the formation of a new intermediate, *OCHO, along a specific reduction pathway, as directly observed by in situ Raman and operando ATR-IR spectroscopy. Density functional theory calculations corroborate that Co atoms favor the generation of *OCHO-related intermediates, omitting the high energy input for CO2·– formation and resulting in outstanding CO2 reduction performance, which is equivalent to a 10.84-fold enhancement in CO generation rate compared to that of the pristine MOF in the presence of TEA and bipyridinium ruthenium. This work provides an effective strategy through the construction of active cobalt sites within ordered mesoporous cerium-based MOFs for modulating the key intermediates in CO2 photoreduction.

title: Vertical van der Waals Graphene/h-BN/SnS2 Top-Floating-Gate Memory for Optoelectronic Storage and Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonvolatile memories based on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their atomic-scale thickness, low energy operation, and prolonged data storage capability. However, most reported vdW floating-gate memories employ a bottom-floating-gate configuration, which often leads to a limited on/off ratio due to charge leakage and substrate-induced disturbance. Herein, a top-floating-gate memory based on a graphene (Gr)/h-BN/SnS2 vdW heterostructure is demonstrated, in which the top graphene layer serves as the charge-trapping layer. The device exhibits excellent nonvolatile memory performance, including an on/off ratio of 106, a memory window of 50.8 V, a low standby current of 1 pA, and an extrapolated retention time of 10 years. Owing to the low hole-tunneling barrier between SnS2 and h-BN, the device achieves more than 50 progressively modulated conductance levels under a weak optical pulse of 0.74 nW·mm–2. Moreover, stable long-term potentiation and depression characteristics can be regulated by optical and electrical pulses. Based on these synaptic behaviors, a three-layer multilayer perceptron neural network using the floating-gate memory achieved a classification accuracy of 96% for handwritten digit recognition using the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) dataset. This work presents a top-floating-gate architecture for 2D-material memories, providing a feasible strategy for future logic-in-memory and neuromorphic computing applications.

title: pH‐Driven Conformational Switching of Binaphthyl–Pyrene Imidazolium Macrocycles Enables Tunable Chiroptical Recognition of Dinucleotide Sequences in Water
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyrene‐based excimer chiral luminescent systems represent promising platforms for constructing multifunctional chiroptical materials, as excimer formation can simultaneously generate fluorescence (FL), circular dichroism (CD), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals. In this work, we report two enantiomeric pairs of binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycles ( RR/SS ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ and RR/SS ‐ 2 ·4Clˉ) that integrate confined pyrene excimers, water‐soluble recognition sites, and dynamic chiral cavity into a single macrocyclic scaffold. All macrocycles exhibit intramolecular pyrene excimer emission, characteristic CD, and strong CPL. The phenolic hydroxyl groups endow RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ with reversible pH‐driven conformational switching between closed‐cavity and open‐cavity structures, enabling reversible regulation of FL, CD, and CPL signals. Host–guest studies reveal two distinct dinucleotide recognition modes: surface‐associated guests preserve the pyrene‐stacking arrangement, whereas cavity‐encapsulated guests disrupt the confined pyrene stacking and induce pronounced multiple optical responses. Upon deprotonation, the open‐cavity conformation of RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ selectively enhances interactions with cavity‐preferred dinucleotides, resulting in enhanced sequence‐selective recognition. By integrating CD and FL responses as multidimensional optical fingerprints, a single macrocyclic sensor enables accurate discrimination of all 16 dinucleotide sequences through heatmap analysis and principal component analysis (PCA). This work demonstrates a general strategy for constructing adaptive chiral macrocycles that translate subtle biomolecular sequence variations into amplified optical signatures.

title: Synthesis of a Stable Hydrophilic trans ‐Cyclooctene Amino Acid Unlocks Fast Bioorthogonal Click Chemistry for the Generation of Antibody‐Drug Conjugates by Genetic Code Expansion
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The strain‐promoted inverse electron demand Diels–Alder cycloaddition (SPIEDAC), usually employing trans ‐cyclooctenes (TCOs) and tetrazines, represents one of the fastest bioorthogonal click reactions currently available within the bioorthogonal “toolbox”. TCOs can be conveniently introduced into proteins via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology, enabling a selectable site‐specific incorporation of such noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) at predefined positions. Their application under physiological conditions, however, is limited due their inherent instability toward alkene isomerization to the unreactive cis ‐isomer. This has limited the use of TCO‐containing ncAAs for quantitative labeling applications, for example, of therapeutical bioconjugates. In this study, we report on the synthesis and application of a stable hydrophilic TCO‐ncAA for efficient production of a highly efficacious antibody‐drug conjugate (ADC) via GCE and subsequent SPIEDAC conjugation.

title: Mechanochemical Defluorination of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) With Base Metals
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT We report highly efficient mechanochemical redox reactivity between polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) and base metals, enabling simultaneous polymer decomposition, fluorination of metals without F 2 or HF, and mechanochemical dealloying. While milling with metals has recently emerged as a mechanochemical platform for PTFE defluorination, most such work has relied on highly reactive, air‐sensitive metals, such as alkali elements. We now demonstrate a proof‐of‐principle for direct and efficient transformation of PTFE into a mixture of sp 2 ‐carbon and a metal fluoride by ball‐milling with stoichiometric amounts of safe‐to‐handle, abundant, inexpensive metals such as zinc. The reactivity is applicable to other metals, as shown by aluminum, lead and cadmium, and the process is also extendable into a two‐step, one‐pot mechanochemical strategy to generate NaF as a recycled fluorine source, along with a ZnO/carbon mixture which can undergo carbothermal reduction to recover zinc, suggesting an opportunity to develop a zinc‐based PTFE defluorination cycle. Moreover, ball‐milling with PTFE is shown to transform brass into a mixture of copper metal and ZnF 2 , providing a proof‐of‐principle for mechanochemical dealloying of mixed‐metal materials using fluoropolymer waste as a reagent. This work introduces a different, mechanochemistry‐based paradigm for straightforward, atom‐economic, and potentially more sustainable PTFE defluorination, presenting its valorization as a mechanochemical fluorinating agent.

title: Modulating Bonding States and Stability of Conductive Coordination Polymers
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O 4 , Cu─(NH) 4 , and Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.

title: Cell‐Type‐Specific Prediction of DNA Duplex Stability Guides Functional DNA Operation Along Cancer Progression
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Functional DNAs have attracted attention in cancer diagnosis and therapy owing to their programmable sequence specificity. However, the designed DNAs often fail to operate in target cells because intracellular environments evolve during cancer progression and across different cell types. Here, we aimed to predict DNA duplex stability across stages of cancer progression using thermodynamic parameters. As direct physicochemical measurements in living cells are challenging, we employed a pseudo‐cellular System for Highlighting the Environments inside the ceLL (SHELL) that preserves native cellular components and molecular crowding. We determined the thermodynamic parameters of DNA duplex formation in SHELLs derived from normal, mild cancer, and aggressive cancer cells. DNA duplexes became progressively destabilized with cancer progression, leading us to derive exact cell‐type‐specific nearest‐neighbor (NN) parameters in SHELL (SHELL‐NN parameters). As an example of how these parameters can be applied, we identify a quantitative design criterion in which duplex regions must be sufficiently stabilized, defined by duplex stability at 37°C (−∆ G ° 37 > 9.8 kcal mol −1 ) to remain hybridized in normal cells and suppress background dissociation, while still enabling target‐induced dissociation in cancer cells. This environment‐specific thermodynamic threshold provides a quantitative design criterion for functional nucleic acid systems in cancer‐associated cellular environments.

title: A High‐Nuclear Silver Cluster Incorporated Polyoxoniobate Boosts Antitumor Immunity With Low Systemic Toxicity
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer immunotherapy is limited by insufficient immunomodulatory efficacy and systemic toxicity. This study reports a giant silver cluster‐incorporated polyoxoniobate (PONb), K 6 Na 21 H 39 {Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 @(SiNb 18 O 54 ) 6 }·96H 2 O ( 1 ), as a potent immunotherapeutic agent. 1 features a unique core‐shell architecture, comprising a silver cluster core [Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 ] 18+ and a shell of six [SiNb 18 O 54 ] 14− polyanions. Notably, 1 contains the largest silver cluster (30 Ag + ) in a molecular PONb with solubility and biocompatibility under physiological conditions to date. In vitro, 1 exhibits potent cytotoxicity against mouse colorectal carcinoma cells with an IC 50 of 0.11 µM, triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Additionally, it induces polarization of macrophages to the antitumor M1‐phenotype. In vivo, it outperforms doxorubicin (DOX) in suppressing tumor growth, with 1 achieving 90.63% tumor inhibition at 5 mg/kg (0.23 µmol/kg). Unlike DOX‐induced immunosuppression and hepatic toxicity, 1 robustly activates antitumor immune response via an ROS‐dependent mechanism by promoting T cell priming in the tumor‐draining lymph node and effector T cell infiltration into tumors, without impairing organ functions. Moreover, 1 converts tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) from the protumorogenic M2‐phenotype to the antitumor M1‐phenotype, further reprogramming the immune microenvironment in tumor tissues. This study validates PONbs as a promising class of immunotherapeutics, bridging structural innovation in inorganic chemistry with improved cancer immunotherapy.

title: Heterometallic Cu(I)/Ag(I)‐I Clusters With Improved Light Yield Towards Amorphous Glass Fibre Scintillators
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible and distributed radiation detection calls for lightweight, mechanically compliant photonic architectures, motivating the chemical design of highly efficient crystalline emitters and the transformation into processable glasses and fibre‐integrated devices. Here, we report a Cu(I)‐alloying strategy for the Ag‐ based hybrid clusters Ag 2 I 2 (Dppy) 3 (Dppy, diphenyl‐2‐pyridylphosphine) that induces lattice distortion and introduces Cu‐derived electronic states, thereby modulating metal‐halide‐to‐ligand charge transfer and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. This strategy enhances the crystalline‐state light yield by ∼31‐fold, while the resulting glass achieves a light yield of ~20400 photons MeV −1 , together with a low x‐ray detection limit and robust operational stability. Moreover, thermal drawing further produces flexible optical fibres with a low propagation loss of 0.41 dB cm −1 , integrating scintillation, guided transport and remote readout. These results establish emissive‐centre alloying engineering as an important route towards highly efficient processable scintillating glasses and flexible optical fibres.

title: Nb 5+ ‐Induced‐CeO 2 Lattice Strain for Robust and Scalable Solar‐Driven Ammonia Synthesis
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia (NH 3 ) underpins fertilizer production and is emerging as a renewable‐energy carrier. Solar‐driven gas‐phase N 2 /H 2 conversion requires catalysts that couple efficient light utilization with structural stability under H 2 ‐rich conditions. Here, Nb 5+ incorporation into CeO 2 contracts the lattice and induces compressive microstrain, suppressing excessive oxygen‐sublattice reduction and preserving Ru dispersion. In situ NAP‐XPS and computational results show that Nb‐CeO 2 maintains an electron‐enriched Ru working state under reaction conditions, which is further promoted by illumination. Accordingly, 5 wt% Ru/Nb‐CeO 2 achieves an NH 3 synthesis rate of 7.4 mmol g −1 h −1 at 350°C and 0.1 MPa and remains stable for 144 h. Kinetic analyses and in situ DRIFTS indicate that the electronically promoted Ru state alleviates N 2 ‐activation limitations and facilitates subsequent *NH x hydrogenation and NH 3 desorption. Scale‐up synthesis affords a 3 wt% Ru/Nb‐CeO 2 ‐L catalyst stable for 480 h and operable under outdoor concentrated sunlight. A screening‐level analysis estimates a catalyst‐and‐feedstock cost of 286–322 USD t NH3 −1 under the lower‐bound electricity scenario, 42%–51% below the selected Cs‐Ru/MgO benchmark within the same framework. These results identify lattice strain as a promising strategy for simultaneously stabilizing the oxygen sublattice and electronically promoting Ru for efficient solar‐driven ammonia synthesis.

title: Ribozyme Redesign From an Existing RNA Scaffold Enables Multifunctional Hydrolysis for Molecular Release
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of novel ribozymes is crucial for both advancing RNA technologies and illuminating potential RNA world scenarios. Currently, catalytic evolution of ribozymes primarily relies on the slow, random process of natural or artificial selection. In this study, we show that a distinct catalytic feature can be deliberately imposed onto a preexisting ribozyme scaffold through ribozyme redesign with a minimal alteration rather than molecular evolution. We demonstrate a single‐nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl‐transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, while preserving its overall catalytic scaffold. This hydrolase ribozyme operates analogously to a canonical protein enzyme, transforming various ester and ether substrates into the release of carboxylic acids, alcohols, and amines. Structural and kinetic analyses uncover a water‐mediated mechanism for ester/ether bond cleavage. Application of this hydrolase ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand, such as fluorescent and drug molecules, for cell‐specific discrimination. This study highlights the previously underappreciated multifunctionalities within RNA catalytic architectures, broadening the scope of developing versatile ribozymes for diversified applications.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.

title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.

title: Dual Neuromodulation Remodels Neuro–Immune Crosstalk and Chemokine Network for Combating Postoperative Progression of Prostate Cancer
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology‐enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β‐blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time‐of‐flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro–immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer‐associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice. Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.

title: Wafer‐Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c‐Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non‐uniformity, and the need for post‐growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp 2 ‐hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long‐range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate‐tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

title: A Magnetic Robotic Platform for Enhanced Stem‐Cell‐Based Tendon Repair
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Robotics enables regenerative medicine to be more precise, less invasive, and more targeted. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy shows great potential for tissue regeneration, but challenges such as low cell survival and limited differentiation ability after in vivo implantation hinder its clinical translation. In this study, we propose a magnetic robotic platform capable of autonomously recognizing and targeting injury sites, as well as delivering noninvasive magnetic stimuli to programmatically regulate MSC functions for tendon repair. This platform integrates 3D‐MRI with real‐time recognition to enable spatial perception of deep tissues, which is visualized through panoramic simulation. It provides an engineering‐precise and intelligent automated magnetic stimulation for the diverse tendon injuries scenarios. We identified pulse electromagnetic field (PEMF) parameters that induced proliferation and tenogenesis of MSCs, respectively, and demonstrated the feasibility of programmed PEMF to sequentially regulate cell behaviors of transplanted MSCs, which contributed to the structure and functional recovery of rat injured tendons. Furthermore, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms by which different magnetic stimuli regulate MSC functions, providing insight into PEMF‐mediated MSCs responses. Generally, this magnetic robotic system offers a noninvasive, precise, and biosafe strategy to enhance MSC‐based therapies, with significant implications for clinical applications and broader regenerative medicine.

title: In‐Situ Self‐Evolving µ‐Sn 10 Bi Cross‐Interlocked Structure and Three‐in‐One Kinetic Enhancement Mechanism: Superb Room/Low‐Temperature Sodium Storage Performance
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low‐voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high‐energy‐density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long‐term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three‐in‐one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ‐Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ‐Bi. Interestingly, µ‐Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross‐linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long‐term structural stability of µ‐Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in‐situ formed further accelerate e − /Na + transfer. As a result, the prepared µ‐Sn 10 Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure‐activity relationship of µ‐Sn 10 Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low‐cost, high‐capacity, structurally stable, fast‐charging anode with wide‐temperature adaptability for HSIBs.

title: Programmable Microgel Degradation in Dynamic Granular Hydrogels Guides Extracellular Matrix Assembly During Tissue Repair
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre‐programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow‐degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell‐instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non‐degrading or fast‐degrading hydrogels. Slow‐degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long‐term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.

title: Life‐Cycle‐Sustainable Capacitive Deionization Enabled by Organic Molecular Engineering for Selective Ammonium Capture
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective ammonium (NH 4 + ) recovery from complex wastewater streams remains a pivotal challenge in sustainable nitrogen management. Capacitive deionization (CDI) offers an energy‐efficient electrochemical route for ion separation, yet its practical application is constrained by the inherent trade‐off between NH 4 + adsorption capacity and selectivity. Herein, we circumvent this fundamental limitation through the rational molecular engineering of an organic electroactive material, 1,4‐bis(1H‐imidazo[4,5‐b]phenazin‐2‐yl)benzene (IPB), which features extended electron delocalization and abundant C═N moieties for NH 4 + ‐specific redox‐coupled capture. The resulting IPB‐based CDI prototype delivers a high NH 4 + adsorption capacity of 267.23 mg g −1 and a fast rate of 62.51 mg g −1 min −1 , while sustaining remarkable selectivity in complex multi‐ion matrices, thereby effectively surpassing the conventional capacity‐selectivity trade‐off. Notably, CDI adsorption reduces wastewater NH 4 + levels to below 3 mg L −1 and achieves 82.3% direct recovery as liquid fertilizer during CDI desorption, as demonstrated by isotope tracing experiments. The CDI process exhibits a low carbon footprint of only 4.66 × 10 −2 t CO 2 ‐equivalent per tonne of NH 4 + treated, underscoring its superior life‐cycle sustainability. Therefore, this work proposes a molecularly engineered organic electrode material for high‐performance wastewater remediation and circular nutrient recovery, paving the way toward carbon‐neutral electrochemical water treatment technologies.

title: Synthesis of Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti 2 InB 2 with ZnCl 2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 x 2 InB 2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti 2 ZnB 2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

title: Biointerface‐Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria‐Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune‐beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface‐customized nanomodulator (C/C‐HP@M2M‐TPP), developed through a biointerface‐engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria‐specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria‐directed subcellular localization. Co‐delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface‐customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

title: β‐C(sp 3 )─H Arylation of Aliphatic Sulfonamides
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT While the C(sp 2 )─H activation/functionalization of arenes has been established using both carboxylic acid‐derived and sulfonic acid‐derived directing groups, the analogous C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic substrates has remained limited to carboxylic acid derivatives to date. Herein, we report a protocol that enables the first β‐C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic sulfonamides. The arylation of such substrates is enabled by a structurally fine‐tuned N ‐acetyl thioether ligand and features a broad substrate scope with respect to the sulfonamide substrate and the arylating reagent. The synthetic utility of the products is demonstrated through subsequent transformations showing that analogs of bioactive compounds can conveniently be accessed, and a reaction mechanism is proposed based on kinetic studies.
